# Preface.

These are the true and genuine Christians in power and in deed, not in mere words and outward appearance, for God's word is power and life to those who believe in it with their hearts. Yes, you might say to this: it is impossible for a person to live like this unless it is given to him by God. Yes, certainly, you speak rightly; it must be given to him by God. But why do the children of men not strive for it and pray to God for it from the bottom of their hearts, that He might bestow such power and virtue upon them? Why do they not research the scripture? Is the Bible, God's word and Holy Scripture, not now so cheap and common that one can buy it for a small amount of money? Many a father of a household has it lying in his parlor, but there is an inch of dust upon it. Why then does one possess it, if one does not wish to read it and use it for the salvation of his soul and the benefit of this temporal life? Why do they not search within it and let the salvation and well-being of their souls be a matter of importance? Does not the Lord Christ, our Lord and Savior, say: Ask, and you shall receive; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you? Why do the children of men have no true faith in God, such that they follow His commandments? Has He not commanded us above all things that we should love one another? By this it would be recognized that we are His disciples and belong to Him. But how well do we...
pages.15:
# Preface.

follow this? Was not Cornelius a heathen? Nevertheless, when he fasted and called upon God, God heard him and helped him onto the right path. How much more we Christians, who are baptized into God's most holy name and can confidently comfort and assure ourselves of our baptismal covenant with God? Why do we not strive for this? Whose fault is it? Is it not our own? Why are we so lazy and negligent regarding the eternal, which lasts into all eternity? Is it not then God, but our own wickedness, that we do not wish to obey His voice? We spend most of our lives with temporal, perishable existence, which in a moment passes away, and we with it—God knows how. Now, even if <term>Weigelius</term> <gloss>Valentin Weigel, a mystic theologian</gloss> and other such authors use exactly such modes of speech in their writings, what can we and another upright Christian do about it? All sects and heresies make use of the Holy Scripture; should we for that reason also despise, reject, disgrace, and slander it? Far be it! They must answer for their own affairs, for what they have written. Everyone must give an account for himself and be certain of his own actions, teaching, and life, as he might stand before God on that day. We have the Holy Scripture, Moses and the prophets, the Holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is prescribed to us as a rule and plumb line for how we should conduct our lives. If we do this, then we act as pious children...

## JACOBI Böhme
# APOLOGIA
->Or<-
# Defense Speech

For the proper justification and rejection of the terrible libel and scolding cards against the little book named *The Way to Christ*, as well as *Of True Repentance and Resignation*. Which libel Mr. Gregor Richter, Senior Pastor at Görlitz, has spread against it.

### Matt. 5, Christ speaks:

> Blessed are you when men shall revile you and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you for my sake: Rejoice and be exceeding glad, for great is your reward in heaven; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

### Matt. 11, Christ speaks:

I praise thee, O Father and Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hidden these things from the wise
pages.20:
# Jacobi Böhme

> and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes. Even so, Father, for so it seemed good in thy sight.

Christ says to Pilate, "My kingdom is not of this world," etc. And to His disciples He said, "I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves," to indicate that where Christ is revealed in a person, that person must be surrounded in this world by nothing but enemies who incessantly wish to root out and kill Christ. This is the way of all true Christians, which they must walk in this world under the devil's thorns, as it also goes for the author of this little book—namely, me—that Satan stirs up his storm winds against the gift of the Holy Spirit and will not tolerate Christ in His members, as can be seen in this libel, how Satan is enraged, how he blasphemes and scolds so horribly, how he sets himself up as a judge over God's word, and wishes to suppress and root it out.

->Follows the title of the libel.<-

# Opinion of Gregorius Richter of Görlitz, Senior Minister of the Local Church, concerning the fanatical books of the shoemaker, whose titles are:

## 1. Aurora, or the Morning Redness in the Rising, etc.
## 2. The Way to Christ, or of True Repentance, etc.
pages.21:
# Closing Speech.

<note>Latin phrase: "ad avertendas sinistras, de Ministerio Gerlicens. suspiciones" <gloss>To avert sinister suspicions concerning the Ministry of Görlitz.</gloss></note>

The libel begins and says:
New ways of speaking generally bring with them new errors.

->Response.<-

The Scripture says, "Prove all things; hold fast that which is good."

->Libel.<-

As many lines as there are, so many blasphemies are to be found in the shoemaker's books, which stink horribly of shoemaker's pitch and blacking. Fie, fie, may such a stench be far from us.

->Response.<-

The little book teaches the *Way to Christ* very earnestly: how a person should depart from the ungodly ways of this world and enter into true, genuine repentance, and put on Christ in faith; be born anew in Christ's Spirit; and how he must be renewed in his mind and disposition and follow Christ.

Secondly, it teaches of true <term>resignation</term> <gloss>the surrender of the self-will to God</gloss>, how the penitent person must surrender himself entirely to God and begin and complete all his works in divine trust. It also indicates how the devil lays traps and snares for the children of Christ at every hour; how a person cannot do otherwise, through such traps...

pages.6: Eternity must remain. **GOD** does not only give us pious preachers, who exhort us to repentance and do their part sufficiently, but also awakens those from among the simple laity who must present the way of repentance to us; and if they were not there, the stones would have to do it at GOD’s command. If we wish to turn to Him with our hearts, GOD has stretched out His hand the whole day to receive us with joy, where there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents. But alas! No one, no one lets our preaching come to their ears; rather, "preach to us very gently, so that it does us good," that is what we like. The heart remains entangled in earthly things and cannot get free, for it is the servant of sin and does not desire to be free. The old habit will not let itself be changed; we would gladly have both heavens, one here and one there again. Whoever teaches us otherwise wants to seduce us. Instead of searching all things according to GOD’s word and testing the spirits to see whether they are from GOD, we fall to slandering and reviling. That is a Schwenkfelder, a Weigelian, a Quaker, a Soriman, and such like heretics; one must not believe them, they do not even know what they write or say. Where should the simple people get such cleverness? They have certainly not studied; that is impossible. GOD’s spirit cannot be with them. Yes, there are a portion who are so godless that they attribute such things to the devil, and thus give to understand what kind of guest they have in their heart, whom they believe more
pages.7: than GOD, just as the Jews also conjectured about the Lord Christ and said: "That must be from the devil; He has not studied the Scripture, so where does He get the knowledge and the great power?" We say exactly the same: At the universities one studies, they know the way of GOD correctly. "That is a saint-eater, he wants to be something special; what the enthusiast says is not to be heeded. If GOD wants me to be pious, He will surely make me pious when the time comes that I must die. I will still convert properly; why should I make my heart heavy for long? I want to be merry as long as I live; I have nothing from it in the end. I know well what I have, but not what I will receive; I will only learn that then. GOD is gracious and merciful, He will surely have mercy on me." But hear! What does GOD’s word say to this, and our Lord Christ in His Holy Gospel: "Whoever wants to follow me, let him take up his cross and follow me." "Repent and believe in the Gospel." "No one can serve two masters." "My kingdom is not of this world." "Here you have fear, but there your sadness shall be turned into joy," and other such heartfelt sayings more. Are all these also Weigelian, Schwenkfeldian, enthusiastic, Socinian, or Quaker-like? For many a pious, honest man has not seen a single letter of the writings of Weigel, Schwenckfeld, and others of that kind in his whole life, much less read them, yet he must let himself be proclaimed by the world
pages.8: as such, for the world remains the world and does not become otherwise, no matter what GOD does; the devil does not rest in his tools. Nevertheless, it must be said to the godless world so that it has no excuse today or tomorrow, and on the Last Day, that it knew nothing of it nor was it presented to it, just as it is commanded to the prophet there: "Call out confidently, do not spare, lift up your voice like a trumpet, and tell my people their transgression, whether they will convert and live; if they do not, you have done your part and saved your soul, but their sin will come upon their own head." Some clergy even agree with the godless crowd themselves, who indeed bear the name of clergy but are in fact spirit-less, and reveal by their fruits what spirit’s children they are, for every tree is known by its fruits. Yet one dares not stir, or one has them at one’s throat: "Do you want to revile the preaching office? You are then a Weigelian; do you despise the clergy? You despise GOD’s servants and revile them?" Just as the Pharisees said to the Lord Christ when He placed the truth before their eyes and uncovered their coarse vices: "Master, with these words you revile us!" So it goes with our present-day Christendom as well. Who then reviles the pious preachers? Live like a Christian, teach simply, draw your listeners toward true Christianity, a godly life, and constant repentance, and lead
pages.9: also yourself an exemplary life; go before your listeners with good examples, so you have a good conscience, and these speeches do not concern you at all. Yes, they say: "Do according to my words and not according to my works." Thereby they indeed give to understand that they are true Pharisees, since they make use of what the Lord Christ said of them, namely: "What they tell you, do; but you should not do according to their works." Such godless clergy will, however, also have to hear again on the Last Day what the Lord Christ says there: "Depart from me, you evildoers!" Even if they say: "Lord, have we not preached in your name, baptized children, administered the Holy Supper, etc.?" For there must be, for both teacher and listener, a fruitful branch on the vine of Christ, and the preachers must also lead a truly Christian life in Christ, so that they do not, as the Holy Apostle Paul says: "preach to others and themselves become reprobate." Otherwise, their teaching and preaching will help them nothing. How can the listeners be taught spiritually if the preachers lead an unspiritual life? Will they not be highly offended by it and say: "Our pastor does that too," even if GOD’s word and the sacraments remain in their power. My dear Christian, tell me, is that <term>Quaker-like</term>, <term>Weigelian</term>, and <term>enthusiastic</term> if I arrange my life according to GOD’s word, live in constant repentance, always have my sinful life before my eyes, always repent of the same, always sigh, and implore GOD hourly, momentarily, in my heart, that He might always govern me with his good Spirit, and therefore wait with longing for a blessed departure, do no human being wrong, rather let wrong be done to me, surrender myself in all things to GOD’s will, even if I must end my life in poverty, hunger, and nakedness, or even on a dunghill, yet in doing so praise GOD and want to thank Him for it, esteem no temporal honor, wealth, or lust, consider myself as nothing, perform my prayer to GOD every morning, noon, and evening on my knees, attend to my professional duties for the remaining time, and live in the comforting hope of the work into which GOD has set and ordained me, that He will surely provide for me, have my best pleasure in this temporal life only in GOD, even if I do my daily work with my hands, yet my mind and spirit [are] always directed toward **GOD**, and thus my body is indeed on the earth, but my conduct [is] in heaven, from whence I wait with joy to be dissolved and to be with Christ, since I then desire to depart from this miserable life with joy, thank **GOD** for all his great benefits, and am glad from the heart that I will be delivered from this miserable life, where my whole life has been to me only a bitter cross, where I have been tempted now by my evil desires, now by the world, now by the devil, and thus have had to endure a thousand kinds of misery, distress, and need, and finally be relieved of it, and know for certain where I
pages.10: go, and also assure myself of it; I have also actually felt it, and my body and soul have rejoiced over it, and still rejoice from the heart, when it will enter into the eternal Sabbath, when there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the righteous judge Christ Jesus will give to me, and not only to me, but also to all who love and long for his appearance. "Yes," you say, "you can chatter finely and bring the thing out quite well; one who did not know better would think you were pure holy angels, for you speak much of humility, gentleness, Christian love, perfection, and the like, and are yet yourselves the most arrogant, puffed-up people in your hearts, in that you despise us others, and think among yourselves that you alone are holy, but we are godless; so you fall into spiritual pride and are greater sinners than we." Yes, indeed, my dear Christian, that is all true. Whoever has this sense, the devil does not rest; he seeks dominion in all men's hearts, now in this manner, now in that. Therefore the Lord Christ admonishes us that we should watch and pray, that we do not fall into temptation, and that the devil sift us, for he goes around like a roaring lion and seeks whom he may devour. It goes indeed many times like this, the devil sows his weeds in all places, GOD builds no church, the devil sets his chapel next to it. Only hear here the difference: the true, real Christians who have come through GOD’s grace to the knowledge of themselves, who have had
pages.11: longing for the truth, and have gladly wanted to convert from their godless ways—for GOD has written it in the heart of man what is right and wrong; therefore the heathens, who knew nothing of GOD, also left behind glorious <term>moralia</term> <gloss>teachings on ethics</gloss>, so that no person would have any excuse that he had not been drawn by GOD—who therefore called upon GOD fervently, and were also heard by GOD upon their fervent prayer and heartfelt longing, and to whom GOD has come to aid in their great distress: they do not do this at all. They know and notice the devil’s deception; they do not despise their neighbor’s person at all, but well his sin and vices; they hold themselves for the greatest, most despised, and most unworthy sinners of all, for GOD’s grace leads them to the knowledge that they see how great and deep the corruption of their heart is. He gives it to them to understand, so that they feel how often and manifold they can fall; therefore they live always in fear, trembling, and yet also in a certain hope and firm trust. They hope, therefore, as the Apostle says, to be saved with fear and trembling, and struggle thereafter, as the Lord Christ commands, that they may enter through the narrow gate. They recognize through GOD’s grace what the Lord Christ says: "The spirit is willing, the flesh is weak." Therefore they fall daily upon their knees and sigh to GOD hourly, that He might preserve them in His grace; therefore is their
pages.12: life a pure cross and tribulation, and thus they live holy, and are joyful when they are dissolved from this temporal, miserable life; so their dying is only a passage from death into life, for they are still united with Christ in their temporal life, and remain thus eternally planted in Him. Of which union no person can speak but he who has felt it, for it is the new name which no one knows but he who receives it. Even if they commit missteps and often stumble—as the devil is a cunning spirit who can insinuate himself into all complexions [temperaments] and thus often puts a leg out for them so that they fall—yet it is GOD’s grace that raises them up again. As soon as the malice has worked, grace steps into their conscience: "What have you done?" There begins again sighing and lamenting, for GOD’s power is mighty in the weak. The tears do not remain absent until they come again to grace; they grow and go thus in cross and tribulation on the narrow way of eternal life, and are fruitful branches on the vine of Jesus Christ, planted in his garden, bear heartfelt fruits in deed and truth, do not know themselves, but think always they are still great sinners, inasmuch as their sin and human infirmities constantly hover before their eyes, as the Holy David laments, yet strive at all times to do good until GOD delivers them from this miserable life, for which they sigh and bear longing hourly and momentarily.

pages.10:

constantly sigh, implore God hourly and in every moment in my heart that He might always govern me with His good Spirit, and therefore wait with longing for a blessed departure, do no human being wrong, rather let wrong be done to me, submit myself in all things to God’s will, even if I must end my life in poverty, hunger, and nakedness, yes, even on a dunghill, yet praise God and want to thank Him for it, esteem no temporal honor, wealth, or lust, hold myself as nothing, perform my prayer to God on my knees every morning, noon, and evening, go about my professional business the rest of the time, and follow my work, into which God has placed and ordained me, live in the comforting hope that He will surely provide for me, have my best joy in this temporal life only in God, even if I do my daily work with my hands, yet my sense and mind are always directed toward **GOD**, and thus my body is indeed upon the earth, but my conduct is in heaven, from where I wait with joy to be dissolved and to be with Christ, where I then desire to depart from this miserable life with joy, thank **GOD** for all His great benefits, and am heartily glad that I am being redeemed from this miserable life, as my whole life has been to me only a bitter cross, where I have been tempted now by my evil desires, now by the world, now by the devil, and thus have had to endure a thousand kinds of misery, trouble, and distress, finally to be delivered from it, and I know for certain where I
pages.11:

am going, am also assured of it, have also actually felt it, and my body and soul have rejoiced over it, and still rejoice from the heart, where it will enter into the eternal Sabbath, where the Crown of Righteousness is laid up for me, which the righteous Judge Christ Jesus will give to me, and not to me alone, but also to all who love and long for His appearing. Yes, you say, you can prattle well and bring the matter forward quite rightly; whoever did not know better would think you were pure holy angels, for you speak much of humility, gentleness, Christian love, perfection, and the like, and yet you yourselves are the most arrogant, puffed-up people in your hearts, in that you despise us others, and think to yourselves that you alone were holy, but we godless. Thus you fall into spiritual pride and are greater sinners than we. Yes, indeed, my dear Christian, that is all true. Whoever has this mindset—the devil does not rest; he seeks dominion in all men's hearts, now in this, now in that manner. Therefore the Lord Christ warns us we should watch and pray, that we do not fall into temptation, and the devil sift us, for he goes about like a roaring lion and seeks whom he may devour. It goes indeed many times so; the devil sows his weeds in all places. GOD builds no church, but the devil sets his chapel beside it. Yet hear here the distinction: the true, real Christians who through GOD’s grace have come to the knowledge of themselves, who have had a longing
pages.12:
<header>Preface.</header>

for the truth and have wanted to gladly convert from their godless ways, for GOD has written in the heart of man what is right and wrong, wherefore also the heathens, who knew nothing of GOD, left behind glorious <term>Moralia</term> <gloss>moral teachings</gloss>, so that no person would have any excuse that he had not been drawn by GOD, who thus fervently called upon GOD and were also heard by GOD upon their fervent prayer and heartfelt longing, and to whom GOD has come to help in their great distress—they do not do this at all. They know and notice the devil’s deception. They do not despise their neighbor’s person at all, but indeed his sin and vices. They hold themselves for the greatest, most despised, and most unworthy sinners of all, for GOD’s grace leads them to the knowledge that they see how great and deep the corruption of their heart is. He gives it to them to understand, so that they perceive how often and manifoldly they can fall; therefore they live always in fear, trembling, and yet also in a certain hope and firm trust, hoping thus, as the apostle says, to be saved with fear and trembling, and strive thereafter, as the Lord Christ commands, that they enter through the narrow gates. They recognize through GOD’s grace what the Lord Christ says: The spirit is willing, the flesh is weak. Therefore they fall daily upon their knees and sigh to GOD hourly that He might preserve them in His grace; therefore is their
pages.13:

life a pure cross and tribulation, and thus they live holy and are joyful. # Preface.
<meta>continues from previous page: ...to carry longing hourly and momentarily.</meta>

These are the true, genuine Christians in power and in deed, not in mere words and outward show, for God’s word is power and life to those who believe in it from the heart. Yes, if you say to this, "A man cannot possibly live this way unless it is given to him by God," then you are certainly saying it rightly; it must be given to him by God. But why do the children of men not strive for it, and pray to God for it from the bottom of their hearts, that He might grant them such power and virtue? Why do they not search the Scriptures? Is the Bible, God’s Word and Holy Scripture, not now so cheap and common that one can buy it for a small amount of money? Many a father of a house has it lying in his parlor, but it is covered with a finger’s thickness of dust. Why, then, do they have it, if they do not wish to read therein and use it for the salvation of their souls and the benefit of this temporal life? Why do they not search within it and let the salvation and well-being of their souls be a matter of concern? Does the Lord Christ, our Lord and Savior, not say: Ask and you shall receive, seek and you shall find, knock and it shall be opened unto you? Why do the children of men have no true faith in God, so that they would follow His commandments? Did He not command us above all things that we should love one another, by which one would recognize that we are His disciples and belong to Him? But how beautifully we follow...
pages.15:
# Preface.

...this. Was not Cornelius a Gentile? Nevertheless, when he fasted and called upon God, God heard him and helped him onto the right path. How much more should we Christians, who are baptized in God’s most holy name and can confidently comfort and assure ourselves of our baptismal covenant with God, why do we not strive for this? Whose fault is it? Is it not our own? Why are we so lazy and negligent regarding the eternal, which lasts for all eternity? Is it therefore not God, but our own wickedness, that we do not want to obey His voice? We spend the greatest part of our lives with temporal, fleeting beings, which vanish in an instant, and we with them, God knows how. Now, even if We <note>referring to Valentin Weigel, a mystic whose writings were often compared to Böhme's</note> and other such authors use similar modes of speech in their writings, what can we or any other upright Christian do about it? All sects and heresies make use of the Holy Scripture; should we for that reason despise, reject, disgrace, and revile it? Far be it! They must answer for their own matters, for what they have written. Each one must give an account for himself and be certain of his own deeds, doctrine, and life, so that he might stand before God on that day. We have the Holy Scripture, Moses and the prophets, the Holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ; this is prescribed to us as a rule and plumb line for how we should conduct our lives. If we do this, then we act as pious children...
pages.16:
# Preface.

...for God has created us. He is our Father and wills that we should fulfill His holy will, as He has revealed it to us in His holy word. Thus, He will provide for us not only here temporally, but also eternally, if we believe this from the bottom of our hearts and act accordingly. Is not the Bible—GOD's word and Holy Scripture—now so cheap and common that one can buy it for a small amount of money? Many a householder has it lying in his parlor, but there is a finger's thickness of dust upon it. Why then do they possess it, if they do not wish to read it and use it for the salvation of their souls and the benefit of this temporal life? and pass through snares, other than by prayer, true repentance, and humility, and how Christ himself leads and sustains him with His power, and how a Christian must be a branch on the vine of Christ, and eat Christ's flesh, and drink His blood, if he wishes to be a Christian at all.

Thirdly, it teaches very earnest prayers of repentance, how the poor soul should, in great earnestness, turn into Christ’s merit, suffering, death, and resurrection, and die daily from the evil earthly will in Christ’s death, and how it must go to the Father through Christ’s wounds and blood-shedding.

Fourthly, it shows in the dialogue between the master and disciple what our eternal Fatherland is, and how the entering into it happens.

This teaching is the true foundation of the New Testament, as Christ and the apostles have taught us.

But because the <term>Pasquill</term> <gloss>libelous pamphlet</gloss> says that there are as many blasphemies as there are lines in this booklet, it is evident that he blasphemes and reviles the Spirit of Christ. For he calls repentance and prayer a blasphemy; for the booklet deals only with repentance and the new rebirth.

Dear haughty judge, where do you want to go, or where do you want to turn, when the supreme Judge, Christ, whom you revile (desecrate) in His members, will appear in His wrath, and will judge the judging judge, and will Himself be the law and the judge.
pages.23:
This Judge will not look upon a <term>Primarium</term> <gloss>high-ranking clergyman/dean</gloss> or his following which he draws to himself, nor any king, prince, or lord of the world, according to their past power, nor their laws, but will judge the life, and test it in His fire. Where will your desecrations and revilements remain then, which you have driven against <term>Christ</term> in His members? It is written: whoever blasphemes the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness eternally. What will you then answer for, that you have knowingly blasphemed His gift, and persecuted the children of <term>Christ</term> so miserably? When <term>Christ</term> will say: what you have done to these my least brothers, you have done to me, what answer will you then give?

You also despise me because I am a layman and have not come from the <term>hohe Schul</term> <gloss>university/higher school</gloss> with my learning, and you spit upon my gift, which I have nonetheless received from **GOD** as a noble gift, which is dearer to me than the whole world, and you also desecrate my craft with your spitting, and call it, together with my gift, a stench.

How might it go with you, when such blasphemies would awaken in you in body and soul, and your "fie," with which you spit upon the gift of the Holy Spirit, would awaken in you and be ignited by **GOD's** wrath, so that the world would become too narrow for you? What would you then wish to give, that you had not done such a thing.
pages.24:
The spirit which now delights you, that you may spend your courage in blaspheming and reviling me, it might yet become the hellish fire for you and step into your conscience; where do you want to remain then?

You drive away my tears and earnest prayers against your blasphemy of God, in that you accuse me entirely with falsehood. Watch out that my tears do not become glowing coals upon your head. I have prayed much to GOD for you, that GOD might enlighten you and let you recognize the truth; but you become ever worse with blaspheming. I will be innocent of you, should God's wrath touch you.

Dear Mr. Primarius, why do you despise me because I am a <term>layman</term> and have divine and natural knowledge? Do you think that the <term>Holy Spirit</term> is bound to your schools? Did not Christ our Beloved say: my Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it. Item: Ask, so you shall receive, knock, so it will be opened to you, etc.

I have received my gift through earnest asking and knocking, and have tasted such a thing that I would not give for all the world's honor and property, and also can never deny. Why do you ascribe the gift of GOD to the devil? Look back into the world, what GOD has often used simple people for His work.

Were Abel, Seth, Enoch, and Noah, who were the patriarchs? Shepherds, who also were no
pages.25:
doctors. Who was Moses? A shepherd! Who was David? A shepherd! Who were the prophets, especially Elisha and Habakkuk? Simple and pious people, who dealt with agriculture. Who was Mary, the mother of Christ? A poor, pious, orphaned maiden! Who was Christ’s foster father in His childhood? A carpenter! Who were Christ’s apostles? All together, poor, simple craftsmen, such as fishermen and the like. Why did Christ not reject them too, because they had not studied? Did He also spit on them because they were craftsmen, as you do?

What has been the beginning of the Christian nobility? Humility and fear of God!

Where now lies your great glory in the Scripture with your art? Show it to me then! D. Paul was a scholar of the Scriptures, but when he was a Christian, he had to become a fool in his art and wisdom, so that Divine Wisdom might find a place in him. Why do you boast then of your art, if you otherwise call yourself a Christian? Do you not know that we are all but one in Christ, that is, Christ in us all? If Christ teaches us and loves us, why do you curse us then, and call Christ in us a stench.

It has not an evil appearance for that, as if the evil spirit were in you, which cannot tolerate Christ, and also does not like to see that which you cannot deny, because you say there is a blasphemy of God in every line, and
pages.26:
forbid people to read it, under threat of eternal punishment.

Dear Mr. Primarius, open your heart! And read the booklet correctly, you will find something else in it; you have never read it! I see that in the title of your <term>Pasquill</term> <gloss>libelous pamphlet</gloss>, for you put the title wrong, and have never yet seen the booklet on true <term>Gelassenheit</term> <gloss>resignation/surrender to God</gloss> and on the following of Christ therein. You put the *Aurora* for the first book, in which you know little and nothing, and the *Way to Christ* for the second booklet. You put the one on repentance for the third, and it is the first in the printed ones, and have never yet seen the last.

23. O Mr. Primarius! Satan has blinded you and led you into wrath, so that you could not read it because of wrath, but he has immediately hurried with you to revilement and blasphemy, for it is a stench before his eyes. Dear Mr. Primarius, drive away the evil apes from you and read it properly, you will find much else in it.

24. Do you also know that GOD has converted some people thereby, that they have entered into true repentance and attained that which Christ promised us, namely the gift of the Holy Spirit? Mr. Primarius, there are powerful examples present.

25. You call this gift of people from the Holy Spirit all a stench; from that one can perceive that this booklet is entirely contrary to the devil, and that no good spirit must live in you
pages.27:
because you blaspheme God's gift, for you say: this stench (namely, doing repentance and praying, which is this booklet's entire content) be far from you. It might well be assumed that God's gift has come far from you.

### Pasquil.

26. You also say that great punishment hangs over those places where such blasphemy of God can be devised, spread, and believed unpunished, where one also may audaciously and unhindered devise, write, and believe whatever one wants.

### Response.

27. Yes, dear Mr. Primarius, I also believe it, that great punishment hangs over those places where one blasphemes GOD’s gift and ascribes it to the devil. Great punishment also truly hangs over the earthly man (where such earnestness of repentance is used), for he must be killed daily and be made a fool to the world when he is to walk the Divine way.

28. You see well how I am punished by you on such ways, and not only by you, but you also incite the whole city against me with revilement, so that they believe you and punish me, but it is Christ’s mark of distinction.

29. But that you prescribe to the people a model of faith, so that not everyone should believe according to his Divine gift, as the Spirit of GOD reveals to them in their souls,
pages.28:
to this belongs another <term>Pasquill</term> <gloss>libelous pamphlet</gloss>; this one does not satisfy them.

30. But that you threaten them with punishment, that I believe of you almost well; if you had the power, they would have to go into the fire, or all out of the land.

31. That you also say that the way to repentance is a devised teaching, the New Testament does not say that; for when Christ began his Gospel with John the Baptist, so He said: Repent! And my booklet says that too!

32. Mr. Primarius, the natural man perceives nothing of this way, you do not need to punish him; he goes without that well in the devil’s ways, until Christ enlightens him in repentance. Only look at yourself and punish yourself, whether you yourself are also on such a way, before you prescribe goal and measure in our gifts of GOD to me and other children of GOD, where your prescribing is yet only a libelous pamphlet defamatory to honor.

->Pasquil.<-

33. Further speaks the <term>Pasquill</term>, GOD will wondrously save His honor, and will not let Himself have His honor taken by such enthusiastic shoemakers, tanners, tailors, women, priests, doctors.

->Response.<-

34. I also hold it for that and believe it firmly, that GOD will not let any devil take His honor, which He has revealed in JESUS Christ with the victories of death and hell in us poor people,
pages.29:

word, and to the Pharisees He said: "Therefore you do not hear, for you are not from GOD." Item: "You are not My sheep."

So when one goes from one crowd to another, people say, "There comes a fool," and many might even say, "It is the devil." But it is not all true; people only give them such titles because they assume such an image; afterward they become like the

Pasquil.

Responsio.

131. Christ was indeed sober, but what Mr. Primarius attributes to the cobbler, that he is himself. # Responsio.

149. Christ's title was the will of the Father; his honor was in God, and he leads the same into our humanity, and raises our humanity to the right hand of the power of God. The same honor he has gifted to his Christians, that they are also in him at the right hand of the power of God, and rule over sin, death, the Devil, and the world. This high title the cobbler also claims and desires the highest royal title, the victory of our Lord Jesus Christ, as a knight of death and hell; he desires such a high title that he might conquer in the struggle against death and hell, and that he intends to overcome the whole world in Christ, and to be a king in Christ, and to rule over all hostile pasquils and slanders of the Primarius. 150. From that time on, I did not cease to inquire solicitously whether this is so, etc. Finally, a few days ago, I came to Eger, and among other things, I saw there at a friend’s house three manuscript books, and quite large ones at that, by this Böhme. What shall I say? As I read, I was astonished. Is it possible that a man from the multitude, not educated in school, would address such profound mysteries and write so politely! Indeed, the method itself and the exposition of the abstruse matters make me doubt the author. Böhme is said to be an idiot <note>in the classical sense of an unlearned layman</note>. I cannot believe it yet, unless I am made more certain that such a person exists in Görlitz and that he has written such things; and this by the testimony of one or another more sincere man, etc. Among the aforementioned friends of J.B. whom I have known, there was one in particular, whose company I often and much enjoyed, who knew how to tell how a medical doctor here, named Tob. Kober—whom I also knew well—put J.B. to the test several times with his language of nature, in that they, as secret friends, would show each other flowers, herbs, and other plants of the earth while walking, and J.B. would immediately indicate the inner power, effect, and properties from their outward <term>signatura</term> <gloss>signature/characteristic form</gloss> and formation, together with the letters, syllables, and words of the name spoken into and attributed to them. However, he wanted to hear the names, above others, in the Hebrew language, as it would be the closest to the language of nature; and when one did not know those same names, he asked after the Greek

### Responsio.

179. The shadow of St. Peter harms the devil greatly; so too, my shadow harms only the devil and the Antichrist. You perhaps think that my shadow might harm you in your earthly life. Because I confess the following of Christ, those people who would accept such teaching would demand of you that you also live as the apostles of Christ and follow their example, and that does not taste good to you. Therefore you say my shadow harms some, as it does those false clergy, terribly much. It cannot be otherwise; it is likely to be so.

180. However, I know a great many spiritual priests whom it will not harm, but rather many pious ones to whom their office is a matter of seriousness. But who can account for the time that brings everything?

181. If the Lord Primarius <note>Gregor Richter, the primary pastor in Görlitz</note> meant his warning so honestly, he would desist from slandering from the pulpit, and call me alone to him, and point out my error, if I should find that he had something true against me, and he would show me a better way. Oh, how gladly would I hold him dear and thank him honestly for it. But he rejoices that he only has something with which he can slander.

182. At the beginning, after his first slander and persecution, I bowed for six years and wrote not a word. Why did he not stop slandering? Who did anything to him? But he
pages.71:
could not. Why? Because GOD had made him into a driving-hammer, so that he had to drive the work forward.

183. His slandering has been my strength and growth; through his persecution my little pearl has grown. He pressed it out, and even published it himself. Therefore I wish him God’s mercy, so that he might also enjoy it, since GOD has used him as my tool.

184. I would act much more humbly toward him, if he were to convert, than he has done toward me. He must not think that I am afraid before his countenance. I have a good conscience, and I wish him one as well.

185. To judge without hearing is valid in no law. I do not submit myself to his judgment in such a way, for my heart is not satisfied with his verdict. I am innocent of all the accusations; everything he has spoken against me from the pulpit is entirely against my meaning, and there is not a single true word in it. He has only twisted all my words with a foreign understanding.

186. Therefore, because I can otherwise have no judge at present who wants to understand my gift, I appeal from him and his <term>judicio</term> <gloss>judgment</gloss> before the court of my Savior JESUS Christ, until I am heard in an orderly fashion; then I will give an account of my case.
pages.72:
### Pasquil.

187. You have acted like Cerinthus <note>A figure in early Christian history often accused of heresy</note> until now, in that you have invented and concocted strange things and shouted out terrible things. When this Cerinthus bathed, he insulted the Lord JESUS Christ and raged violently with his chatter against GOD. But the house collapsed and crushed him, and so the teacher perished along with his students.

### Responsio.

188. Whether Cerinthus was against Christ, I leave in its place. I am with Christ, and I confess JESUS Christ before my Lord and GOD, and I have submitted myself to Him in obedience, to live according to His commandments and will. But that the Lord Primarius says I have acted like Cerinthus, that would likely require proof, or it will not be true.

189. But that he speaks of my strange things, I say with truth that I have written nothing strange. I have only written what nature and man are. But because this seems strange to the Lord Primarius, the fault is solely that he does not understand such things.

190. What can I do about the fact that he is blind in this regard? I did not write to him, but only to those to whom GOD gives the understanding. Let him just remain a high priest and not become a philosopher and naturalist, so we are
pages.73:
decided. He must not force the old sects upon me; I have seen none of their writings; it is only his malice.

### Pasquil.
191. Your filth, O Shoemaker! has greatly soiled our city.

### Responsio.
192. Lord Primarius, you have thus sprayed the red <note>a reference to blood or the color of accusation</note> of slander because of the shoemaker, so that many a person clinks <note>possibly meaning "rings" or "vibrates"</note> with slander. That is the filth that harms them in their souls, because they believe slander and take it into their hearts and blaspheme GOD’s gift.

### Pasquil.
193. Oh, that all those who read your writings must go away with you.

### Responsio.
194. What a Christian wish that is from a high priest. One would hardly or not at all find it in Caiaphas, and it would likely not stand anywhere in the Bible. It will soon come to pass that his good wish will come true, that the sheep will be separated from the goats, so that the evil ones have room in hell, because they can tolerate no one around them on earth.

### Pasquil.
195. Yes, you have also infected Silesia with your teaching, where you then will be received by many, which I know for certain, who, as they are of nobility and much more distinguished than others, thus also go before others with their novelty. But you, his companions, guard and watch, so that these distinguished writings of this distinguished man do not perish. 

<note>A small printer's mark decorates the bottom of the page.</note>
pages.74:
196. Indeed, one now finds many excellent, learned, God-fearing men in Silesia who see further than the Lord Primarius, to whom their Christianity is a matter of true seriousness, who walk in the following of Christ. These read many good little books that carry the right foundation; they did not first learn the following of Christ from me, but had it beforehand, and they rejoice, however, that GOD pours out such high recognition even into simple people, which is indeed a wonder of GOD.

197. But the Lord Primarius attributes such to the devil, just as the high priests did to Christ, whose nobility you also follow. But the high-ranking nobility in Silesia notice the time and see that GOD has something great in store, but you are blind to it and are hardened; therefore the day of your punishment from GOD is coming and is near; know that.

### Pasquil.

198. Well now, go and never come back, so that you perish miserably, and rather take a shoe than a pen in your hand.
pages.75:
199. Christ said: When they curse you, bless them, so you are children of the highest GOD. Because the Lord Primarius wishes me a miserable death, his wish is from the devil, for it runs entirely against GOD’s commandment and will, as well as against all honest reason and integrity. Here one should know the tree by its fruits, and everyone may well think from what spirit and mind he persecutes me, that he does this to please Satan and is no servant of Christ.

# To the Reader.

<note>A decorative initial "L" begins the text.</note>Dear reader, I consider the Pasquil to be worth no response at all, because only vanity, untruth, and slander are found therein. I have, however, wished to make an answer for the sake of those who do not understand it and have not read my little book, nor know my person, who look only at the standing of the Primarius and think he slanders me out of Christian zeal and does so for God’s sake because of his office. Just as the great crowd is thus led astray so that they give him approval, and think he does right, as if everything he screams from the pulpit were true, because he uses GOD’s name therein and wraps it in such a way that one cannot see his grim heart, also appealing to his office, so simplicity believes it, which knows nothing of the matter, how maliciously he persecutes me and acts entirely against his office, and never wanted to hear me therein. And he judges that which he himself does not understand. Thus I have made an answer, in case some might want to become seeing, and depart from slandering against GOD’s gift, and I testify herewith before GOD that I have answered out of no other intention than purely for the sake of the love of my neighbor, and I admonish the Lord Primarius to reflect on something better: for he does not have a lion, but a little lamb of Christ before him, or he will see in whom he has fled, that the sheep in the spirit of Christ may not become a lion to him, and the sheep judge the wolf, and I mean it heartily and honestly.

### Pasquil.

187. You have acted like Cerinthus <note>A figure in early Christian history often accused of heresy</note> until now, in that you have invented and concocted strange things and shouted out terrible things. When this Cerinthus bathed, he insulted the Lord JESUS Christ and raged violently with his chatter against GOD. But the house collapsed and crushed him, and so the teacher perished along with his students.

### Responsio.

188. Whether Cerinthus was against Christ, I leave in its place. I am with Christ, and I confess JESUS Christ before my Lord and GOD, and I have submitted myself to Him in obedience, to live according to His commandments and will. But that the Lord Primarius says I have acted like Cerinthus, that would likely require proof, or it will not be true.

189. But that he speaks of my strange things, I say with truth that I have written nothing strange. I have only written what nature and man are. But because this seems strange to the Lord Primarius, the fault is solely that he does not understand such things.

190. What can I do about the fact that he is blind in this regard? I did not write to him, but only to those to whom GOD gives the understanding. Let him just remain a high priest and not become a philosopher and naturalist, so we are

X.text:
decided. He must not force the old sects upon me; I have seen none of their writings; it is only his malice.

### Pasquil.

### Responsio.
192. Lord Primarius, you have thus sprayed the red <note>a reference to blood or the color of accusation</note> of slander because of the shoemaker, so that many a person clinks <note>possibly meaning "rings" or "vibrates"</note> with slander. ### Pasquil.

### Responsio.

195. Yes, you have also infected Silesia with your teaching, where you then will be received by many, which I know for certain, who, as they are of nobility and much more distinguished than others, thus also go before others with their novelty. ### Responsio.

by name, who, endowed with a singular grace of the Spirit, speaks various languages, and moreover produces books full of much wisdom. Since that time I have not ceased to inquire solicitously whether this is so, etc. Finally, a few days ago, I came to Eger, and among other things, I saw there at a friend’s house three manuscript books of that Böhme, which were quite large. What shall I say? As I read, I was astonished. Is it possible for a man from the masses, not educated in the schools, to approach such deep mysteries and to write so politely! Indeed, the very method and the exposition of hidden matters make me doubt the author. Böhme is said to be an idiot <note>in the classical sense of an unlearned layman</note>. We cannot yet believe it unless I am made more certain that such a man exists in Görlitz, and that he wrote such things: and that by the testimony of one or another more sincere man, etc. Among the aforementioned former friends of J.B. was, in particular, one whose company I often and much enjoyed, who knew how to tell how a medical doctor here, named Tob. Kober, whom I also knew well, had tested J.B. several times with his natural language, in that they, as secret friends, while walking, would show one another flowers, herbs, and other plants of the earth, and J.B., from their external signature and formation, would immediately indicate the internal power, effect, and properties with the letters, syllables, and words of the name spoken and assigned to them. He wanted, however, to hear the names, above others, in the Hebrew language, as that which would be closest to the natural language: and when one did not know those names, he asked after the Greek

Greek. And whenever the physician had diligently provided a wrong name, the other, when he compared the same property against the plant and its signature, such as form, color, etc., soon noticed the deception, and said that it could not be the right name, and could produce sufficient proof of this. And hence it may have come about that it was rumored of him that he could speak foreign languages: which, however, was not the case, nor did he ever boast of it. Indeed, he was able to understand them in others when he heard them, according to the testimony of Mr. David von Schweinitz, the Governor of the Principality of Legnica, which he let be known not long ago, shortly before his death. by means of the natural language, which he knew, etc. Just as many other noble and other prominent people, and indeed often, and in secret, intimate friendship, associated with him: thus, in particular, the noble Lord von Franckenberg knew him well, and in the year 1622 (under the title, *The Way to Christ*) promoted his booklet on Repentance, Resignation, and the Supersensible Life for printing here in Görlitz. Concerning this von Franckenberg, with whom I stayed for a long time in different places, and from whom I did not distance myself—even when absent—in order not to forgo his edifying conversation, I corresponded with him in many letters; I could bring much testimony that it was J.B. himself, and not someone else under his name, in whom the wonders of God became manifest: for he perceived them sufficiently in his (J.B.'s) person. I pass over those who were also not unknown to me, who, through this man's company and piercing spiritual speech, fell into a remarkable and swift change of their minds and a renewal of their life: so that where they had previously been entirely devoted to the vanity of this world and the lusts of the flesh, and showed themselves to their subjects as nothing other than ravenous wolves, they afterwards, to everyone's astonishment, became enemies of all debauchery and associated with them as patient sheep, and wept for their previous scandalous life with constant remorse. I have never heard from any of those who knew him, nor could I learn through others,

pages.14:
Perhaps because of this frequent commerce with the French, or for other reasons unknown to me, Jansenius fell under suspicion as if he were planning innovations and wishing to incite the Flemings to shake off the Spanish yoke. He cleared himself, and to do so more thoroughly, he published a book which he named the *Gallic Mars* <note>original: "Martem Gallicum"</note>, filled with taunts against the French. As a reward for this, he was appointed Bishop of Ypres by Philip IV—to whom he was known through three embassies undertaken on behalf of the University of Louvain—on his own birthday in 1635, and he was consecrated after the space of one year. But he did not hold the see for long. His first care after entering the episcopate was to put the final polish on his *Augustinus* and to visit his diocese. A grave concern gradually gnawed at his mind, having seen the abundant seed of poison already scattered. Fearing for himself, he adopted the plan of dedicating the work to Urban VIII, where at the same time he submitted himself and his sentiments to the Apostolic See as the sole rule of faith, and to its most certain judgment. Shortly after, a pestilential plague invaded Ypres; the Prelate himself was seized by it and was taken away on May 6, 1638, at the age of 53. In the testament that he drew up, he says:

> "I think it is difficult to find anything (in the book) that should be corrected. If, however, the Holy See should wish to make certain changes in it: I am a son of obedience and a son of the Roman Church, in which I have lived until death. This is my last will."

The first epitaph, placed with great praise by the order of Pope Alexander VII and Archduke Leopold, Governor of the Belgians, was removed, and another was substituted for it by Maes, a Canon of Ypres, with these words carved on the marble:

> "Here lies Cornelius Jansenius, the seventh Bishop of Ypres. I have said enough. He lived
pages.15:
52 years. He died on May 6, 1638. Go, Traveler: may he rest in peace. Amen."

Sancyranus lived no more than five years after Jansenius. An arrogant man who raised himself above all theologians, he held the Council of Trent in such contempt that he considered it the work of the scholastics and of a single Pontiff. He revealed what he felt about the doctrine of grace, having been heard at one time to say: "Calvin felt correctly, but spoke badly." Moreover, being as cautious as possible, he demanded Pythagorean silence from those he spoke to (saying, "in secret because of the fear of the Jews"), and he wished for all his letters to be burned. He had once incautiously offered poison <note>a metaphor for his dangerous theological opinions</note> to a certain priest; he immediately regretted it, and while the man was traveling to Poitiers, fearing a denunciation to the local Bishop, he pursued the man in the middle of his journey and asked to be heard for confession. He was then accustomed to laughingly tell how craftily he had imposed silence on a man of doubtful faith. A deed worthy of a stern enforcer of austere penance, whose spirit led the Virgins of Port-Royal to deprive themselves of heavenly bread <note>the Eucharist</note> even at Easter for many months. Clearer specimens of this penance were given by men, some of whom were directors of the Virgins and ascetics, while others, as penitents, had each built their own little hut within the walls of the monastery. Indeed, these men abstained from the Lord's table for seven years and more, and even until the end of their lives, as a punishment for their sins.

His first work was the *Royal Question* <note>original: "Quaestio Regia"</note>; how far is a subject, especially in time of peace, obliged
pages.16:
to preserve the life of the prince at the cost of his own life? In it, he reviews more than 30 cases in which he contends that suicide is lawful.

He wrote another book on the occasion of the controversies that arose in England between the Missionaries from the secular clergy and the regular clergy. Richard Smith, Bishop of Chalcedon, sent by Urban VIII to compose these, seemed to favor the regulars less, and even to disturb their ministries rather than promote them. Hence arose complaints and various pamphlets, two of which were accused of criticizing episcopal authority, or certainly of showing it too little deference. Sancyranus seized this opportunity to declaim against the regulars and issued that famous pamphlet on *Hierarchy* under the false name of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work pleased as long as the author remained hidden, and it was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on April 27, 1641, and committed to the press at their expense. Godeau, Bishop of Grasse, added a eulogy in which the author is proclaimed "the most invincible defender of Bishops, the most keen lover of truth, the most just vindicator of Hierarchy, and a Theologian educated in the bosom of ancient theology." Sancyranus's modesty did not have enough strength for him to prefer to remain hidden for long in such commendation of himself and his work. But when the author was discovered, a blush invaded his face, and all that pomp of words eventually vanished even from the book *Gallia Christiana*.

Indeed, he proved himself a candidate for ancient theology in a book condemned on April 23, 1654: *Familiar Theology, or a brief explanation of the mysteries of the
pages.17:
Faith, in which, to pass over other errors, he says of the Trinity: "God was not alone before the creation of the world: for He lived in a holy Society of three divine persons, the Father, etc." What then? Is God distinct from the Persons? Further, to him, "the Church is a Society of those who serve God in the light and profession of the true faith, in the union of charity." But sinners do not have charity: are they, therefore, not of the Church?

But to pass over other fragments, the Treatise of Augustine on Virginity, which he had edited with notes in the French idiom under the name of P. Seguenot, a Priest of the Oratory, was fatal to him. For on account of this, and also because he could no longer contain himself, he was arrested by order of Cardinal Richelieu, together with Seguenot, in the same year and month in which Jansenius had passed away, May 14, and was consigned to prison. Released from it after the death of the Cardinal, without doing anything further, he was struck by apoplexy shortly after and departed to the majority on October 11, 1643.

### §. 2.
### *The book of Jansenius is published, condemned, and defended.*

When Jansenius died, the presses soon labored, and the work was brought into the light as soon as possible—with the Apostolic Nuncio resisting in vain—by the following French and Batavian types through the work of the Calvinists, and with the letter to Urban suppressed. The expectation of the work, which had been announced with such great ambition such a long time before, held the learned world in suspense for so long; it was received with that much greater applause, or sorrow, by the dissenters. Swift pens and literary skirmishes began. But when the book was brought to Rome, it was immediately branded by Urban VIII through the Bull *In Eminenti* because of the propositions already "reproved and condemned by his predecessors" contained in it. Having heard this thunderbolt of the Vatican, affections were changed, and the type of battle was changed.

The Louvain Doctors were the first to oppose the condemnation, with the Bishops of Mechelen and Ghent favoring them, in a contumacy continued for 8 years and more. The Bull was brought to the Sorbonne, and in 1644 it was decreed that no one should defend the propositions condemned by Urban and his predecessors in public theses. But since it was not obeyed, the matter was handled more seriously, with Habert on one side agitating against the pestilential doctrine of Jansenius, and Antoine Arnauld on the other struggling for his innocence; with this distinction, that the former remained superior in arguments, while the latter, as patrons of a bad cause are wont to be, remained superior in clamors and calumnies. Finally, in the year 1649, the Syndic of the Parisian Theological Faculty proposed six propositions excerpted from the book of Jansenius to be examined by ten very grave Theologians. Nine Doctors in total condemned them all; one opposed them, Saint-Amour, who with a crowd of 60 other Theologians appealed to the supreme Court of the Kingdom. The appeal was rejected, and those nine Doctors brought the propositions to the Assembly of the Clergy gathered in Paris in 1650. By far the greatest part of the Prelates judged five of them worthy of a more severe censure and to be sent to Rome.
pages.19:
Habert wrote the letter by which the propositions to be condemned are exhibited for Apostolic judgment, to which eighty-five Bishops subscribed, with only eleven others dissenting, led by Gondrin, the Archbishop of Sens.

Soon everything was in an uproar: nothing was left untried to undermine this decision. But when the King himself desired a swift and full decision of the whole controversy, it was at his special wish that the letter was sent to Rome, and Innocent X, the successor of Urban, moved as much by the exhortation of the King as by the gravity of the matter itself, without delay submitted the brought-forth propositions to an extremely rigid examination by chosen and most learned Theologian Consultants and Cardinals.

Then indeed the supporters of Jansenius, now fearing more for themselves, when they saw that they had increased in number and were even supported by the favor of certain Bishops and had already coalesced into a faction, they too sent some of their own to Rome to seek out patronage and to prepare a defense of the cause, which they did abundantly. Twenty-two sessions or congregations were held, besides ten others before the Pontiff himself; prayers were commanded, the opposing party was given space to speak, and its defenses were heard often. They could not be exhausted by the urgency and multiplication of these [defenses], so that twelve days before the final decree was rendered, to apply the final stroke, they offered the Pontiff the *Writing of the Three Columns* <note>original: "Scriptum trium columnarum"</note>, by which they still hoped that their Jansenius could be placed in safety.
pages.20:
The title of this Writing was:
> "Very brief distinctions of the five propositions into various senses, and open statements of the Calvinists and Lutherans, as well as the Pelagians and Molinists, as well as St. Augustine and his disciples, concerning them." * Five delegates were read to have subscribed to this:

*Natalis de la Lane*, Doctor of the Parisian Faculty, Abbot of St. Mary of Valle Crescente; *Tussanus de Mares*, Priest of the Oratory of JESUS; *Ludovicus de Saint-Amour*, Doctor of the Faculty and Fellow of the Sorbonne; *Nicolaus Maneffier*, Doctor of the Faculty and Fellow of the Sorbonne; *Ludovicus Angram*, Licentiate of the Sacred Faculty and distinguished Canon of the Church of Troyes. But this empty evasion having been rejected, those five propositions were finally declared and condemned as heretical by the Bull *Cum occasione* given on May 31, 1655.

---

\* Behold the name of the faction! *Disciples of St. Augustine.*

The Bull brought into France was accepted as soon as possible by thirty Bishops gathered in the Mazarin Palace and was recorded in the registers of the Sorbonne. The King himself gave letters, which were the first of this kind, in which he commanded the Bull to be accepted; yet they were not sent to the Parliament. Nevertheless, the Archbishop of Sens and the Bishop of Comminges scattered the not very honorable mandates of the Bull, and even abstained from injury, throughout their dioceses. The other followers of Jansenius, indeed, at first as if stunned and uncertain what to do, finally congratulating themselves with a marvelous impudence, asserted that "the propositions were indeed rightly condemned by judgment" and that they were to be held as heretical. Yet they affirmed that Jansenius was not at all touched by this thunderbolt; for they claimed that "none of them exist in his book."
pages.21:
Indeed, if the acute men look at the very peaks and the order of the individual words, let us grant that they see no proposition from those in the book. But let them consider the syntax, and let them gouge out their own eyes if they do not see an egg similar to an egg. Come, let us compare them.

*Proposition I in the Bull.* "Some commandments of God are impossible to just men who are willing and endeavoring according to the present powers they have: there is also lacking to them the grace by which they might become possible."

<margin>13.</margin>
Jansenius, Vol. 3, Book 3, of the *Grace of Christ*, ch. 13, says: "From this indubitable doctrine, certain things of no small moment relating to this matter are inferred and made clear. First, indeed, that there are certain commandments impossible to man according to the state and powers in which he is established. Second, that grace is not always present by which we can, that is, by which we have sufficient strength to fulfill the same. Third, that this impotence is found not only in the blinded, the hardened, and the infidels—but also in the faithful and the just. Fourth, that this impossibility happens to the faithful not only when they are unwilling to keep the commandments, but even when they are willing." If you still doubt, he adds in the same chapter, 4: "These—demonstrate that there is nothing more certain and more well-founded in the doctrine of St. Augustine than that there are certain commandments which are impossible to men not only [who are] infidels, blinded, [and] hardened, but also [to those who are] faithful and just, willing and endeavoring according to the present powers they have: and that grace is lacking by which they might become possible."

### §. 2.
### *The book of Jansenius is published, condemned, and defended.*

When Jansenius died, the presses soon labored, and the work was brought into the light as soon as possible—with the Apostolic Nuncio resisting in vain—by the following French and Batavian types through the work of the Calvinists, and with the letter to Urban suppressed. The expectation of the work, which had been announced with such great ambition such a long time before, held the learned world in suspense for so long; it was received with that much greater applause, or sorrow, by the dissenters. Swift pens and literary skirmishes began. The Louvain Doctors were the first to oppose the condemnation, with the Bishops of Mechelen and Ghent favoring them, in a contumacy continued for 8 years and more. The Bull was brought to the Sorbonne, and in 1644 it was decreed that no one should defend the propositions condemned by Urban and his predecessors in public theses. The appeal was rejected, and those nine Doctors brought the propositions to the Assembly of the Clergy gathered in Paris in 1650. Indeed, if those sharp men look at the very points and the order of the individual words, let us grant that they see none of the propositions in the book. *Proposition I. in the Bull.* „ Some precepts of God are impossible to just men, willing and trying according to the present powers they have: there is also lacking to them the grace by which they might become possible. „

Jansenius, Vol. 3, Book 3, on the Grace of Christ, ch. 13, says: „ From this undoubted doctrine, certain things of no small moment relating to this matter are inferred and made clear. He wrote another book on the occasion of the controversies which arose in England between Missionaries from the secular Clergy and the regular Clergy. In order to settle these, Richard Smith, Bishop of Chalcedon, sent by Urban VIII, seemed to favor the Regulars less, and even to disturb their ministries rather than promote them. Hence arose complaints and various libels, two of which were accused of attacking episcopal authority, or certainly of paying it too little deference. Sancyranus seized this opportunity to declaim against the Regulars and issued that famous libel concerning the *Hierarchy* under the false name of *Petrus Aurelius*. The work pleased as long as the Author remained hidden, and it was approved by the Synod of the Gallican Clergy on the 27th of April, 1641, and committed to the press at their expense. Godeau, Bishop of Grasse, added a eulogy in which the author is proclaimed "the most invincible defender of Bishops, a most keen lover of truth, a most just vindicator of the Hierarchy, a Theologian educated in the bosom of ancestral Theology." The modesty of Sancyranus did not have enough strength to prefer to remain hidden for longer amidst such praise of himself and his work. But once the Author was discovered, a blush invaded his face, and all that pomp of words eventually vanished even from the book: *Gallia Christiana*.

He truly proved himself a Candidate of ancestral Theology in a book condemned on April 23, 1654: *Theologia Familiaris, seu brevis explicatio mysteriorum Fidei* <gloss>Familiar Theology, or a brief explanation of the mysteries of the Faith</gloss>

After the death of the Cardinal, he was dismissed from prison, but without initiating anything further, he was struck shortly after by an apoplexy and went to the majority on October 11, 1643.

### §. 2.
### *The book of Jansenius is published, condemned, defended.*

Upon the death of Jansenius, the presses soon labored, and the work was brought to light as soon as possible, with the Apostolic Nuncio struggling in vain against it, by the efforts of the Calvinists, through French and Batavian types, and the letter to Urban was suppressed. The expectation of the work, announced with such ambition so long before

Thus Pascal, I say, wrote no less eruditely and theologically, if you please, unless you would rather say ironically, by which he might mock his own fellow partisans, who did not cease to declaim and write against the Bulls of Innocent and Alexander, and other decrees concerning various nullities. For this writer seemed too fickle to the Jansenists themselves, and indeed sometimes even of doubtful faith, never fearing to contradict himself if it pleased him; of which he also gave a specimen in the <term>Provincial Letters</term>, where he later commends as his own the doctrine of the Thomistic school, which he initially ridicules.

But neither could the command of the King do anything at that time against these men, although he ordered the mandate of accepting the Bull, and the subscription of the same, to be recorded in the registers of the Parliament. This was an entirely new act, and the first of all, by which a declaration of the King of such a kind was sent to the Parliament, by which the Pontifical Bull was commanded to be received as dogmatic by royal power. The King, therefore, in order to cut off all excuses by which they might exempt themselves from the formula of subscription, requested that a formula be prescribed by the Pope himself, which the Clergy also demanded at the same time with the highest prayers.

It was done as was requested, and Alexander sent the Bull <term>Regiminis Apostolici</term> <gloss>Of Apostolic Governance</gloss> in the year 1664, in which he proposed the following formula to be subscribed to by all ecclesiastical men of both Clergy, Bishops, and Archbishops. "I, N. N., submit myself to the Apostolic Constitution of Innocent X, given on May 31, 1653, and to the Constitution of Alexander VII, given on October 16, 1656, of the Supreme Pontiffs, and I reject and condemn with a sincere heart the five
pages.32:
propositions excerpted from the book of Corn. Jansenius, which has the name *Augustinus*, and in the sense intended by the same author, just as the Apostolic See condemned them through the said Constitutions, and I swear it: So help me God, and these holy Gospels of God."

This formula was again soon sent by the King to the Parliament to be entered into the archives; it was commanded that all the Prelates of the Kingdom and Ecclesiastics subscribe to it, and the penalty of loss or confiscation of goods, loss of benefices, or even deportation, etc., was dictated. The far greater part of the Bishops obeyed, and added the threats of canonical penalties. Harduin de Péréfixe, elevated to the Archbishopric of Paris in the same year, was among the first to publish the mandate of subscription throughout his diocese, and in the following year, 1665, he inspected <term>Port-Royal</term> <gloss>a convent central to the Jansenist movement</gloss>, both in Paris and in the fields, and ejected the Virgins who were resisting more fiercely, together with Agnes of Saint Paul, the sister of Arnauld and Abbess of the convent, and confined them to various monasteries, and interdicted the others from the Sacraments.

It is easy to divine with what sense of pain the faction saw its nest disturbed so suddenly. First, there was huge trepidation, then cries: on one side, torments and mournful laments of those deploring the persecution of truth and innocence; on the other, curses upon whatever sacred and profane dignity there was. Finally, there was tumult among the very parts of the faction, and it was contended for many years of the present century. For since everywhere, by the vigilance of the Bishops,
pages.33: and the strict command of the King, they were urged toward subscription, the rigid Morality of many suffered no small stain. They subscribed, without putting aside the error in their minds; they perjured themselves, so that they might be allowed to retain their own for themselves, or to aspire to new things. Those who were of a more tender conscience, or wished to appear so, looked around for subterfuges and means by which they might mitigate the horror of perjury, and took refuge in equivocations and mental restrictions, which even the most lax Morality would shudder at. Thus they condemned the first proposition, and said that grace is given to all the just, by which the commandments of God become possible for them, if they ask for it from God as they ought: but they held in their minds that the grace of asking as one ought is not given to all the just. They condemned the second because the small grace of Jansenius, which excites in us only a weak desire for good, is at the same time inferior to earthly delight, (understand) to the overcoming of which it is not sufficient, it can certainly be resisted: because, they add among themselves, it is always resisted. In the third, they condemned and rejected from their heart the necessity (suppose) natural, or physical, which makes one act not through election, but through impulse. Regarding the fourth and fifth, they argued according to the writing of the three columns, and said that without doubt any prevenient grace can be resisted if the human will should wish it, and grace itself (this in silence) would not make it so that it wishes. Thus, likewise, they conceded that certain graces come to the reprobate from the merits of the death of Christ, but not those without which they could not be saved. Behold the vanity of men!
