<margin>3</margin> Lady, why are they multiplied who trouble me: in your tempest you shall pursue and dissipate them. Dissolve the bonds of our impiety: take away the bundles of our sins. Have mercy on me, Lady, and heal my infirmity: take away the pain and anguish of my heart. Do not deliver me into the hands of my enemies: and in the day of my death, strengthen my soul. Lead me to the harbor of salvation: and render my spirit to my maker and creator. Glory.
<margin>4</margin> When I called, you heard me, Lady: and from your sublime throne, you deigned to remember me. From the roaring <note>beasts</note> prepared for food: and from the hands of those seeking me, your grace shall deliver me. For your mercy and piety are kind: toward all who invoke your holy name. May you be blessed, Lady, forever: and your majesty for ages. Glorify her, you nations, in your strength: and all you peoples of the earth, extol her magnificence. Glory.

Give ear to my words, Lady: and do not turn away the beauty of your face from me. Turn our mourning into joy, and our tribulation into jubilation. May our enemies fall before our feet: may their heads be crushed by your virtue. May every tongue bless you: and may all flesh confess your holy name. For your spirit is sweeter than honey, and your inheritance is sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. **Glory.**

How long, Lady, will you forget me: and not deliver me in the day of tribulation? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me: by the power of your virtue, crush the impious. Open the eyes of your mercy: lest our enemy prevail against us. We magnify you, the finder of grace: through whom the ages are repaired. Exalted above the choirs of angels: pray for us before the throne of God. Glory.

<margin>11</margin>
The unwise adversary said in his heart: I will pursue and seize and my hand shall kill him. Arise, Lady, and anticipate him and supplant him, destroy all his efforts. The sun and moon marvel at your beauty: angelic powers serve and wait upon you. By whose most light touch the infirm are healed: by your rosy scent the dead revive. Virgin mother of God: he whom the whole world cannot contain shut himself within your womb, having become man. Glory to the Father and to the Son.

<margin>12</margin>
Lady, who dwells in the tabernacle of God: or who shall rest with the elders of the people? The poor in spirit and the clean of heart: the meek, the peaceful, and the mourning.
pages.11:
Remember, Lady, that you speak good things for us: and turn the indignation of your Son away from us. Let sinners embrace the footprints of Mary: and let us be cast down at her blessed feet. Let us hold her strongly, nor let us depart until we have deserved to be blessed by her. **Glory.**
Preserve me, Lady, for I have hoped in you: and share with me your trickles of grace. Your virginal womb and your bowels brought forth the Son of the most high God. Blessed be your breasts: from which you nourished the savior with deific milk. Confess the praises of the glorious Virgin: whoever of you have found grace and mercy with her. Give magnificence to her name and praise her forever, for her precept and birth.
Hear, Lady, my justice and my love: remove my tribulation from me. I will confess to you in the voice of exultation: when you shall magnify your mercy over me. Imitate her, you holy virgins of God: as Agnes, Barbara, Dorothea, and Katherine have imitated her. Honor her with the voice of your lips for the sake of her grace.

Glorify her, you just, before the throne of God: for you have worked justice by the fruit of her womb.

My Lady, I have called to you by day and night: and you have made your mercy with your servant. Because I have hoped in your mercy: you have taken eternal reproach away from me. My enemies have derided me on every side: but you have bestowed upon me a good refreshment under the shadow of your hand. Let the families of the nations adore you: and let all the orders of the angels glorify you.

The Lord guides me, O Virgin Mother of God: for you have turned your lovable face toward me. Blessed be your most splendid eyes: which you deign to turn mercifully upon us sinners. Blessed be the light and splendor of your face: blessed be the grace of your countenance. Blessed be the mercy of your hands: blessed be the emanation of your virginal milk. May your apostles and the prophets of God bless you: may the martyrs, confessors, and virgins sing psalms to you.

The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof: but you, most holy Mother, reign with Him forever. You are clothed with glory and beauty: every precious stone is your garment and your covering. The splendor of the sun
pages.15:
upon your head: the beauty of the moon under your feet. The twinkling stars adorn your garments: the constellations glorify you eternally in the morning. Remember us, O Lady, in your good pleasure: and make us worthy of glorifying your name. Glory.

**T**o you, O Lady, I have lifted up my soul: in the judgment of God, may I not blush because of your prayers. Neither let my adversaries mock me: for those who trust in you shall be strengthened. May the snares of death not prevail against me, and let not the camps of the wicked hinder my steps. Crush their onslaught by your virtue: and come to meet my soul with gentleness. Be my guide to the homeland: and deign to gather me to the assembly of the angels. Glory.

**J**udge me, O Lady, for I have wandered from my innocence: but because I have hoped in you, I shall not be weakened. Burn my heart with the fire of your love: and restrain my loins with the girdle of chastity <note>referencing a common ascetic metaphor for purity</note>. For your mercy and your clemency are before my eyes: and I have delighted in the voice of your praise. O Lady, I have loved the beauty of your face: and I have venerated your holy majesty.
pages.16:

### ¶ Monday
### ¶ Nocturn

**M**ay your face, O Lady, be my illumination: and may the serenity of your grace shine upon my mind. Exalt my head over my enemies and I shall sing: I will chant a psalm to your name. Do not turn your face from me: for I have longed for your hope and your beauty from my youth. I have loved you and sought your mercy, O Queen of Heaven: and do not withdraw your grace from your servant. I will confess you among the nations: and I will honor the throne of your glory. Glory.

**I** will cry out to you, O Lady, and you will hear me: you will make me joyful in the voice of your praise. Have mercy on me in the day of my anguish: and deliver me in the light of your truth. Blessed be you, O Lady: in all the ends of the orb of the earth. The sanctuary which your hands have strengthened: is the holy temple of your body. Your conscience is clean and immaculate, the place
pages.17:
of propitiation and the holy dwelling-place of God. Offer to our Lady, O sons of God: offer to our Lady praise and reverence. Grant virtue to your servants, O holy Mother: and blessing to those who praise and glorify you. Hear the groaning of those sighing to you: and do not despise the vows of those invoking your name. May your hand be prepared to succor me: and may your ear be attentive to my supplication. May heaven and earth bless you: the sea and all the orbs of the earth.

I will exalt you, O Lady, for you have taken me up: you will deliver me from the iniquitous adversary. Turn to me and vivify me: lead me back from the gates of death: and from the waves of tribulations that have surrounded me. Because of your own self and the magnificence of your right hand: crush and dissipate all my adversaries. And I will offer to you a sacrifice of praise: and I will more devoutly exalt your glory. Exult, O heavens, and rejoice, O earth: for the Virgin consoles her own: and she will have mercy on her poor.

In you, O Lady, have I hoped, let me not be confounded forever: in your grace, take me up.
pages.18:
You are my strength and my refuge: my consolation and my protection. To you, O Lady, I have called while my heart was troubled: and you have heard me from the summit of the eternal hills. Lead me out of the snare which they have hidden for me: for you are my helper. Into your hands, O Lady, I commend my spirit: my whole life: and my final day.

Blessed are those whose hearts love you, O Virgin Mary: their sins shall be mercifully washed away by you. Holy, chaste, and flowering are your breasts: which have burst forth with the flower of perpetual greenness. The beauty of your pulchritude shall not see corruption: and the grace of your face shall never wither in eternity. Blessed are you, O lofty Virgin of Jesse: who have dilated yourself even unto Him who sits on the throne. O royal Virgin, you yourself are the way: through whom the Savior from the highest seats has visited us.

Exult, O righteous, in the Virgin Mary: and in the rectitude of the heart, praise her together. Approach her with reverence and devotion: and may your heart be delighted in her salutation.
pages.19:
Offer to her the sacrifice of praise: and be mindful of the breasts of her sweetness. For she flows for you with the rays of her piety: and she will clarify you with the flashes of her mind. Most sweet is her fruit in the mouth: and in the heart of the wise it grows sweet. Glory.

I will bless our Lady at all times: and her praise shall not fail in my mouth. Magnify her with me: all you who are nourished with the honey and milk of her recreation. In perils and in doubtful matters, invoke her: and in necessities, you shall find aid and sweet refreshment. Take an example of her conduct: and emulate the studies of her charity and humility. Because, therefore, O Lady, you were most humble: you compelled the uncreated Word to take flesh from you.

Judge, O Lady, those who injure me and rise against them: and vindicate my cause. My soul shall rejoice in you: and I will exult, devoted to your benefits. The heavens and the earth are full of your grace and sweetness: for wherever we go: the diffusion of your virginal womb meets us. Behold
pages.20:
and everywhere you have extended the snares of your kindness. Let us run, therefore, most beloved: and let us salute such a noble and sweet-flowing Virgin: so that we may rest in the bosom of her sweetness. **Glory**.

The unjust man plots to sin in secret: let the Mother of God turn him away from his evil purpose. Incline the face of God upon us: compel Him to have mercy on sinners. O Lady, your mercy is in heaven: and your grace is diffused over the earth. Power and virtue are in your arm: strength and fortitude in your right hand. Blessed be your empire over the heavens: blessed be your magnificence over the earth. **Glory**.

Do not emulate the malignant, O Lady: sweeten their fury through your grace. Hope in her, O religious and cloistered: trust in her, O clerics and students. Delight in her praises and she will hear the petitions of your heart. Better is a little with her grace: than the treasures of silver and precious stones. **Glory forever**.
pages.21:
be to you, O Queen of Heaven: and at no time do not forget us. Glory.

O Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury: offer us, O best one, pardon for our sins. In your sight may our every desire be: our hope and our confidence. My heart is troubled within me: the light has departed from my bowels. Illuminate my blindness with your splendor: sweeten my contrition with your sweetness. Do not abandon us, O Lady, Mother of God: let your grace and virtue be at my right hand. ¶ Hail Mary.

I said I will guard my ways, O Lady: since through you the grace of Christ was given to me. My heart is liquefied by your sweetness: my bowels are inflamed by your love. Hear my prayer, O Lady, and my supplication: and may my adversaries be consumed. Have mercy on me from the heavens and from the altitude of your throne: and do not permit me to be troubled in the valley of misery. Guard my foot so that it may not be injured: and at my end, may your grace be present. Expecting, I have expected your grace: and you have done unto me according to the multitude of your mercy.

N.text:
Confess to His name, for it is holy: they shall recount His wonders forever. Glory to the Father.

### ¶ Monday
### ¶ Nocturn

**M**ay your face, O Lady, be my illumination: and may the serenity of your grace shine upon my mind. Exalt my head over my enemies and I shall sing: I will chant a psalm to your name. Do not turn your face from me: for I have longed for your hope and your beauty from my youth. I have loved you and sought your mercy, O Queen of Heaven: and do not withdraw your grace from your servant. I will confess you among the nations: and I will honor the throne of your glory. Glory.

**I** will cry out to you, O Lady, and you will hear me: you will make me joyful in the voice of your praise. Have mercy on me in the day of my anguish: and deliver me in the light of your truth. Blessed be you, O Lady: in all the ends of the orb of the earth. The sanctuary which your hands have strengthened: is the holy temple of your body. Your conscience is clean and immaculate, the place

X.text:
of propitiation and the holy dwelling-place of God. Offer to our Lady, O sons of God: offer to our Lady praise and reverence. Grant virtue to your servants, O holy Mother: and blessing to those who praise and glorify you. Hear the groaning of those sighing to you: and do not despise the vows of those invoking your name. May your hand be prepared to succor me: and may your ear be attentive to my supplication. May heaven and earth bless you: the sea and all the orbs of the earth.

I will exalt you, O Lady, for you have taken me up: you will deliver me from the iniquitous adversary. Turn to me and vivify me: lead me back from the gates of death: and from the waves of tribulations that have surrounded me. Because of your own self and the magnificence of your right hand: crush and dissipate all my adversaries. And I will offer to you a sacrifice of praise: and I will more devoutly exalt your glory. Exult, O heavens, and rejoice, O earth: for the Virgin consoles her own: and she will have mercy on her poor.

In you, O Lady, have I hoped, let me not be confounded forever: in your grace, take me up.

pages.6:
Bless the Lord with all your heart: for the earth is full of his mercy. Glory be as it was. 
<margin>3</margin> O Lady, why have they who trouble me multiplied? In your tempest you shall pursue and dissipate them. Dissolve the bonds of our impiety: take away the bundles of our sins. Have mercy on me, Lady, and heal my infirmity: take away the pain and anguish of my heart. Do not deliver me into the hands of my enemies: and on the day of my death, comfort my soul. Lead me to the port of salvation: and render my spirit to my maker and creator. Glory. 
<margin>4</margin> When I called, you heard me, Lady: and from your sublime throne: you deigned to remember me. From the roaring ones prepared for food: and from the hands of those seeking me, your grace shall deliver me. For your mercy and piety are kind: to all who call upon your holy name. Blessed may you be, Lady, forever: and your majesty for all time. Glorify her, O nations, with your strength: and all peoples of the earth, extol her magnificence. Glory.
pages.7:
<page-num>4</page-num>
<margin>5</margin>
Receive my words with your ears, O Lady: and do not turn the beauty of your face away from me. Convert our mourning into joy and our tribulation into jubilation. May our enemies fall before our feet: by your virtue may their heads be crushed. May every tongue bless you: and may all flesh confess your holy name. For your spirit is sweeter than honey, and your inheritance is sweeter than honey and the honeycomb. **Glory.**

<margin>6</margin>
Lady, do not allow me to be chastised in the fury of God: nor to be judged in his wrath. Because of the honor of your name, O Lady: may the fruit of your glorious womb be propitious to us. From the gate of hell and from the belly of the abyss: by your holy prayers, deliver us. May the eternal gates be opened for us: so that we may tell of your wonders forever. For neither the dead, nor those who are in hell shall praise you, O Lady: but those who, through your grace, will obtain eternal life. **Glory.**

<margin>7</margin>
In you, my Lady, I have hoped; deliver me from my enemies, O Lady. Close the mouth of the lion and its teeth
pages.8:
and bind the lips of those who pursue me. Do not delay, for your name's sake: to do your mercy to us. May the splendor of your face shine upon us: so that our conscience may be preserved before the Most High. If the enemy pursues my soul, O Lady, may your aid comfort me: so that he may not brandish his sword against me. Glory.

<margin>8</margin>
O Lady, our Lord has been made our brother and our savior. Like fire in the bush and dew in the fleece: the eternal Word of God descended into you. With the Holy Spirit rendering you fruitful: the power of the Most High overshadowed you. Blessed be your most pure conception: blessed be your virginal birth. Blessed be the purity of your flesh: blessed be the sweetness of the mercy of your heart. Glory.

<margin>9</margin>
I will confess to you, O Lady, with my whole heart: and I will narrate your praise and glory among the peoples. For to you are owed glory, thanksgiving, and the voice of praise. Sinners will find grace before God through you, the inventress <note>meaning the one who brings or provides</note> of grace and salvation.
pages.9:
<page-num>5</page-num>
May humble penitents breathe toward indulgence: heal the contritions of their hearts. In the beauty of peace and in plenteous rest: you shall feed us after the labor of our pilgrimage. Glory.

<margin>8</margin> I trust in the Lady because of the sweetness of her name. Her eyes look upon the poor: and her hands are extended to the pupil and the widow. Seek her out from your youth: and she shall glorify you before the face of the peoples. May her mercy take away the multitude of our sins: and may she confer upon us the fruitfulness of merits. Extend your arm toward us, O glorious Virgin: and do not turn your glorious face away from us. Glory.

<margin>9</margin> Make me safe, O Mother of beautiful love: fountain of clemency, and sweetness of piety. You alone go around the circle of the earth: so that you may bring help to those who call upon you. Your ways are beautiful: and your paths are peaceful. In you shines the hope of chastity, the light of justice, and the splendor of truth. Clothed in solar light as if with a garment: shining with a crown of twelve stars.
pages.10:
<margin>10</margin>
How long, O Lady, will you forget me: and not deliver me in the day of tribulation? How long shall my enemy be exalted over me: by the power of your virtue, crush the impious. Open the eyes of your mercy: so that our enemy may not prevail against us. We magnify you as the inventress of grace: through whom the ages are repaired. Exalted above the choirs of angels: pray for us before the throne of God. Glory.

<margin>11</margin>
Our adversary said in his heart: I will pursue and catch and my hand will kill him. Rise, O Lady, and forestall him and supplant him, destroy all his efforts. The sun and moon marvel at your beauty: angelic powers serve and wait upon you. By whose most light touch the infirm are healed: by your rosy scent the dead revive. Virgin Mother of God: He whom the whole world cannot contain, enclosed himself within your womb, having become man. Glory to the Father and to the Son.

<margin>12</margin>
Lady, who shall dwell in the tabernacle of God: or who shall rest with the senators of the people? The poor in spirit and the clean of heart: the meek, the peaceful, and those who mourn.
pages.11:
<page-num>6</page-num>
Remember, O Lady, to speak good things for us and turn the indignation of your Son away from us. Let us sinners embrace the footsteps of Mary and let us be cast down at her blessed feet. Let us hold her strongly, nor let her go until we have merited to be blessed by her. **Glory.**
Preserve me, O Lady, for I have hoped in you: and impart your drops of grace to me. Your virginal womb and your bowels brought forth the Son of the most high God. Blessed be your breasts: from which you nourished the Savior with deific milk. Confess the praises of the glorious Virgin: all you who have found grace and mercy with her. Give magnificence to her name and praise together for all time her conception and birth.
Hear, O Lady, my justice and love: remove my tribulation from me. I will confess to you with the voice of exultation: when you will have magnified your mercy over me. Imitate her, O holy virgins of God: as Agnes, Barbara, Dorothea, and Katherine have imitated her. Honor her with the voice of your lips for the sake of her grace.
pages.12:
Agatha, Lucia, Margaretha, and Cecilia have received. He will give to you the Son of the Father as a Spouse: and a crown from the lilies of paradise, shining incomparably.
The heavens and the earth praise you, O Lady: and I will glorify your name among the nations. Confess to her with a troubled heart: and she will strengthen you against your enemies. Drop down to us, O Lady, the grace of your riches: from the flowing milk of your sweetness, refresh the bowels of your children. All you religious, honor her, for she is your helper and special advocate. Be our refreshment, O glorious Mother of Christ, because you are the wonderful support of all religion. The heavens declare your glory and the fragrance of your ointments is dispersed among the nations. Breathe toward her, O lost sinners: and she will lead you to the port of indulgence. In hymns and psalms and canticles, strike her heart: and she will drop down to you the grace of her sweetness. Glorify her, O you just, before the throne of God, because by the fruit of her womb you have worked justice.
pages.13:
<page-num>7</page-num>
Praise her, O heavens of heavens: and let all the earth glorify her name. Glory.
May you hear us, O Lady, in the day of tribulation: and turn your clement face to our prayers. Do not cast us off in the time of our death: but succor [the soul] when the body has deserted it. Send an angel to meet it: by whom it may be defended from enemies. Show it the most serene judge of the ages: whom she may grant it to see because of your grace. May it feel your refreshment in its punishments: and grant it a place among the elect of God. Glory.
For in your virtue our heart shall rejoice: and in the sweetness of your name our soul shall be consoled. From your seats, send us wisdom: by which we may be sweetly illuminated in all truth. Grant us the grace of abstaining from carnal desires: so that the light of grace may rise in our hearts. How sweet are your words, O Lady, to those who love you: how sweet are the drops of your graces. I shall sing glory and honor to you: and in your name I shall boast forever.
May the eye of my God look upon me: through your merits, O Virgin Mary, always.

pages.14:
My Lady, I have called out to you day and night, and you have performed your mercy with your servant. Because I have hoped in your mercy, you have taken eternal reproach away from me. My enemies have mocked me on all sides, but you, under the shadow of your hand, have brought me sweet refreshment. May the families of the nations adore you, and may all the ranks of the angels glorify you.

The Lord rules me, O Virgin Mother of God, for you have turned the lovable countenance of his face toward me. Blessed be your most splendid eyes, which you deign to turn mercifully upon us sinners. Blessed be the light and splendor of your face; blessed be the grace of your countenance. Blessed be the mercy of your hands; blessed be the emanation of your virginal milk. May your apostles and prophets of God bless you; may martyrs, confessors, and virgins sing psalms to you.

The earth is the Lord's and its fullness, but you, most holy Mother, reign with him forever. You have clothed yourself in glory and beauty; every precious stone is your garment and your covering. The splendor of the sun
pages.15:
upon your head, the lunar beauty beneath your feet. The glittering stars adorn your path, the heavenly bodies glorify you in the morning. Remember us, Lady, in your good pleasure, and make us worthy to glorify your name. Glory.

To you, Lady, I have lifted up my soul; in the judgment of God, may I not be put to shame through your prayers. Nor may my adversaries mock me, and those who trust in you will be strengthened. Let not the snares of death prevail against me, and let not the camps of the wicked impede my steps. Crush their impetus with your virtue, and come to meet my soul with gentleness. Be my guide to the homeland, and deign to gather me into the assembly of the angels. Glory.

Judge me, Lady, for I have departed from my innocence, but because I have hoped in you, I shall not be weakened. Burn my heart with the fire of your love, and gird my loins with the belt of chastity. For your mercy and your clemency are before my eyes, and I have delighted in the voice of your praise. Lady, I have loved the beauty of your face, and I have venerated your holy majesty.

Confess to his name, for it is holy; they declare his wonders throughout the age. Glory to the Father.

pages.18:
You are my strength and my refuge, my consolation and my protection. To you, Lady, I called out while my heart was troubled, and you heard me from the top of the eternal hills. Lead me out of the snare that they have hidden for me, for you are my helper. Into your hands, Lady, I commend my spirit, my whole life, and my last day.

Blessed are they whose hearts love you, Virgin Mary; their sins will be mercifully washed away by you. Holy, chaste, and flower-bearing are your breasts, which erupted with the flower of perpetual greenery. The beauty of your splendor will not see corruption, and the grace of your countenance will not wither forever. Blessed are you, O lofty scion of Jesse, who have extended yourself even to the one sitting on the throne. O royal Virgin, you are the path through which the Savior visited us from the highest seats.

Exult, O righteous, in the Virgin Mary, and praise her in the uprightness of your heart. Approach her with reverence and devotion, and let your heart delight in her greeting.
pages.19:
Offer her the sacrifice of praise, and be mindful of the breasts of her sweetness. For she pours out to you the rays of her piety, and she will clarify you with the flashes of her mercy. Most sweet is her fruit in the mouth, and in the heart of the wise it becomes sweet. Glory.

I will bless our Lady at all times, and her praise will not fail in my mouth. Magnify her with me, all you who are refreshed by the honey and milk of her recreation. In perils, in doubtful matters, invoke her, and in necessities, may you find aid and sweet refreshment. Take an example of her conduct, and emulate the studies of her charity and humility. Because, therefore, Lady, you were most humble, you compelled the uncreated Word to take flesh from you.

Judge me, Lady, those who harm me, and rise up against them, and vindicate my cause. My soul will rejoice in you, and I will exult, devoted to your benefits. The heavens and the earth are full of your grace and sweetness, for wherever we go, the diffusion of your virginal womb meets us. Behold
pages.20:
and everywhere you have extended the snares of your kindness. Let us run, therefore, most beloved, and greet so noble and sweet-flowing a Virgin, so that we may rest in the bosom of her sweetness. **Glory.**

The unjust man plots so that he may sin in secret; let the Mother of God turn him away from his evil purpose. Incline the face of God upon us; compel him to have mercy on sinners. Lady, your mercy is in heaven, and your grace is diffused over the earth. Power and virtue are in your arm; strength and fortitude are in your right hand. Blessed be your empire over the heavens; blessed be your magnificence over the earth. **Glory.**

Do not emulate the wicked, Lady; sweeten their fury through your grace. Hope in her, you religious and monastics; trust in her, you clerics and scholars. Delight in her praises, and she will hear the petitions of your heart. Better is a little with her grace than silver treasures and precious stones. **Glory forever.**
pages.21:
may it be unto you, O Queen of Heaven, and at no time do not forget us. Glory.

Lord, may the Lord not argue with me in his fury; grant us, best Lady, pardon for our sins. In your sight may all our desire be; our hope and our confidence. My heart is troubled within me; the light has receded from my innards. Illuminate my blindness with your splendor; sweeten my contrition with your sweetness. Do not abandon us, Lady Mother of God; may your grace and virtue be at my right hand. Hail Mary.

I said I will guard my ways, O Lady, since through you the grace of Christ was given to me. My heart has been liquefied by your sweetness; my innards have been inflamed by your love. Hear my prayer, Lady, and my supplication, and may my adversaries melt away. Have mercy on me from the heavens and from the altitude of your throne, and do not permit me to be troubled in the valley of misery. Guard my foot so that it may not be injured, and at my end may your grace be there.

Waiting, I have waited for your grace, and you have done unto me according to the multitude of your mercy.

pages.22:
you have heard my prayers and brought me out of the lake of misery and from the pit of the enemy. Many and marvelous are your gifts, O Lady: incomparable are the rewards of your grace. Let all who love you exult and rejoice in you: those who hate your name will fall into hell. Blessed may you be forever, O Lady: for ever and ever. **Glory**.

Blessed Mary has understanding for the needy and the poor: in her praises she remains. O Lady of the angels, Queen of the world: cleanse my heart with the fire of your love and charity. You are the light of my heart: you are the nurse who refreshes my mind. My mouth desires to praise you: my mind yearns to venerate you most affectionately. My soul desires to pray to you: because all my substance corrects itself through your protection. **Glory**.

As the deer desires the fountains of water: so my soul pants for your love. Because you are the mother of my life: and the nourisher of the repairer of my flesh. Because you are the one who suckled the savior of my soul
pages.23:
the beginning and the end of all my salvation. Hear me, O Lady, let my filth be cleansed: illuminate me, O Lady, so that my darkness may be enlightened. Let me be kindled by your love, restore me: let your grace expel my sloth. Glory.
Judge me, O Lady, and discern my cause: from a perverse nation, from the malignant serpent, and from the pestiferous dragon deliver me. Let your holy fecundity destroy him: may your blessed virginity crush his head. May your holy prayers strengthen us against him: may your holy merits empty out his power. Cast the persecutor of my soul into the abyss: may the infernal pit swallow him while alive. But I and my soul in the land of my captivity: will bless your name: and I will glorify you for ever and ever.
O Lady, we have heard with our ears: and our fathers have told us. Because your merits are ineffable: and your wonders are truly stupendous. O Lady, your virtues are innumerable: and your mercies are inestimable. Exult, my soul, and rejoice in her: because
pages.24:
many good things are prepared for those who praise you. Blessed are you, Queen of the angels: and let those who praise your magnificence be blessed by God. Glory to the Father.
My heart has uttered a good word, O Lady: with honeyed dew it has been sweetened. Through your holiness may my sins be purged: through your integrity may incorruptibility be granted to me. Through your virginity my soul is loved by Christ: and is joined to him by the bond of death. Through your fecundity I, a captive, have been redeemed: through your virginal birth I have been snatched from eternal death. Through your most worthy plenitude I, who was lost, have been restored: and from the exile of misery I have been brought back to the primal beatitude.
O Lady, you are our refuge in all our necessity: and a more powerful strength crushing the enemy. The world is full of your benefits: they surpass the heavens and penetrate the depths. By the plenitude of your grace, those who were in hell rejoice that they are freed. By the entitlement of your virginal fecundity: those who are above
pages.25:
the world rejoice that they are restored. Through the glorious birth of your most holy virginity, men become companions and fellow citizens of the angels. Glory.

All nations, clap your hands: sing in jubilation to the glorious Virgin. For she is the gate of life, the door of salvation, and the way of our reconciliation. The hope of the penitent, the solace of the mourning: the blessed peace and health of hearts. Have mercy on me, O Lady, have mercy on me: for you are the light and the hope of all who trust in you. Through your saving fecundity, may it please you that the forgiveness of sins be granted to me. Glory.

Great are you, O Lady, and greatly to be praised: in the city of the God of heaven: in the entire church of his elect. You have shown yourself to the alternating angelic choirs: surrounded by roses and crowned with lilies. Run to her, powers and principalities: meet her, virtues and dominations. Cherubim, thrones, and seraphim: exalt her: and place her at the right hand of the bridegroom, your most beloved son. O with what joyful spirit
pages.26:
the world rejoice that they are restored. Through the glorious birth of your most holy virginity, men become companions and fellow citizens of the angels. Glory.

pages.27:
and serene aspect you have received her, O God of angels and men: and you have given her dominion over every place of your sovereignty.
Hear, O nations of men: perceive with your ears, you who desire to enter the kingdom of God. Honor the Virgin Mary: and you will find life and eternal salvation. Guide your poor servants, O Lady, with happy confederation and <unclear>peace</unclear>. Feed and sustain the hungering of your followers with the fruit of your womb. You remained incorrupt after birth and inviolate after having a son. Glory to the Father and

The God of gods has spoken of Mary: saying through Gabriel his messenger, Hail full of grace, the Lord is with you: through you the salvation of the world is repaired. Your son desires your beauty and your grace. Adorn your bridal chamber and prepare for the coming of your God. Through the Holy Spirit you will conceive: which will make your birth virginal and pleasant.
Have mercy on me, O Lady: you who are called the Mother of mercy. And according to the bowels of your mercies: cleanse me
pages.28:
from all my iniquities. Pour out your grace upon me: and do not withdraw your accustomed clemency from me. For I will confess my sins to you and before you I accuse myself of my wicked deeds. Reconcile me with the fruit of your womb: and make peace between me and Him who created me.
Why do you glory in malice, O malignant serpent and infernal dragon? Bow your head to the woman: by whom you are cast down with strength into the deep. Crush him, O Lady, with the foot of your virtue: let him rise and dissipate his malice. Extinguish his power and reduce his strength to ash. So that we who live may exult in your name: and with joyful spirit say praise to you. <insert>Wednesday</insert>
The foolish enemy has said in his heart: let him cast out men from the tabernacle of the sons of God. I will go forth and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of the serpent: and through the woman I will cast out her husband. As the heavens are exalted from the earth: so the thoughts of God are exalted from your thoughts. Do not be puffed up by the fall of the woman: because the woman will crush your head. You prepared a pit for her
pages.29:
and you will be caught in her net. Glory to the Father.
O Lady, in your name save me: and deliver me from my enemies. So that the craftiness of the enemy may not harm me: protect me under the shadow of your wings. O my Lady, help me: bestow your grace upon my soul. Voluntarily I will offer you a sacrifice of praise: and I will confess to your name for it is good. From all tribulation you will deliver me: and my eye will despise my enemies.
Hear, O Lady, my prayer: and do not despise my supplication. I am saddened in my thought: because the terrors of God have terrified me. The darkness of death has come over me: and the fear of hell has invaded me. But I, in my solitude, await your consolation: and in my bed I attend to your mercy. Glorify the right hand of your arm: so that our enemies may be laid low before us. Glory.

pages.14:
My Lady, I have cried to you by day and night: and you have made your mercy with your servant. Because I have hoped in your mercy: you have taken away eternal reproach from me. My enemies have derided me on all sides: but you, under the shadow of your hand, have brought me good refreshment. Let the families of the nations adore you: and let all the orders of the angels glorify you.

The Lord rules me, O Virgin Mother of God: for you have turned his lovable face toward me. Blessed be your most splendid eyes: which you deign to turn mercifully upon us sinners. Blessed be the light and splendor of your face: blessed be the grace of your countenance. Blessed be the mercy of your hands: blessed be the emanation of your virginal milk. May your apostles and the prophets of God bless you: let the martyrs, confessors, and virgins sing psalms to you.

The earth is the Lord's and its fullness: but you, most holy mother, reign with him forever. You have clothed yourself with glory and beauty: every precious stone is your garment and covering. The splendor of the sun
pages.15:
upon your head: the lunar beauty beneath your feet. The glittering stars adorn your bed: the stars glorify you perpetually in the morning. Remember us, O Lady, in your good pleasure: and make us worthy to glorify your name. Glory.

To you, O Lady, I have lifted up my soul: in the judgment of God, may I not blush because of your prayers. Neither let my adversaries mock me: and those who presume in you shall be strengthened. May the snares of death not prevail against me, and let not the camps of those who do evil impede my steps. Strike down their impetus with your power: and come to my soul with gentleness. Be my guide to the fatherland: and deign to gather me to the company of the angels. Glory.

Judge me, O Lady, because I have strayed from my innocence: but because I have hoped in you, I shall not be weakened. Burn my heart with the fire of your love: and restrict my loins with the girdle of chastity. Because your mercy and your clemency are before my eyes: and I have delighted in the voice of your praise. O Lady, I have loved the beauty of your face: and I have venerated your holy majesty.
pages.16:
Confess to his name because it is holy: they tell of his wonders in the age. Glory to the Father.

### ¶ Monday
### ¶ Nocturn

**O** Lady, let the splendor of your face be my illumination: and may the serenity of your grace shine upon my mind. Exalt my head over my enemies and I shall sing: I will chant a psalm to your name. Do not turn your face away from me: because I have desired your hope and beauty from my youth. I have loved you, O Queen of Heaven, and I have sought your mercy: and do not withdraw your grace from your servant. I will confess you among the nations: and I will honor the throne of your glory. Glory.

**I** will cry to you, O Lady, and you will hear me: you will gladden me in the voice of your praise. Have mercy on me in the day of my distress: and in the light of your truth deliver me. Blessed be you, O Lady: in all the ends of the globe of the earth. The sanctuary which your hands have strengthened: is the holy temple of your body. Your pure and immaculate conscience is the place
pages.17:
of propitiation and the holy dwelling place of God. Offer to our Lady, O children of God: offer praise and reverence to our Lady. Give strength to your servants, O holy Mother: and blessing to those praising and glorifying you. Hear the groanings of those sighing to you: and do not spurn the vows of those invoking your name. May your hand be prepared to succor me: and your ear attentive to my supplication. May the heavens and the earth, the sea and the circuit of the lands bless you.

I will exalt you, O Lady, because you have taken me up: you will deliver me from the unjust adversary. Turn to me and bring me to life: lead me back from the gates of death: and from the waves of tribulations that have surrounded me. For your own sake and the magnificence of your right hand, crush and dissipate all my adversaries. And I shall offer you a sacrifice of praise: and I will more devotedly exalt your glory. Exult, O heavens, and rejoice, O earth: because Mary consoles her own through her brothers: and will have mercy on her poor.

In you, O Lady, I have hoped, I shall not be confounded forever: in your grace, take me up.
pages.18:
You are my strength and my refuge: my consolation and my protection. To you, O Lady, I have cried while my heart was troubled: and you have heard me from the top of the eternal hills. Lead me out of the snare which they have hidden for me: for you are my helper. Into your hands, O Lady, I commend my spirit: my whole life: and my final day.

Blessed are they whose hearts love you, O Virgin Mary: their sins shall be mercifully washed away by you. Holy, chaste, and flowering are your breasts: which erupted with the flower of perpetual greenery. The decor of your beauty shall not see corruption: and the grace of your face shall not wither forever. Blessed are you, O lofty Virgin of Jesse: who expanded yourself even to him who sits on the throne. O royal Virgin, you yourself are the way: through whom the Savior visited us from the highest seats.

Exult, O righteous, in the Virgin Mary: and praise her in the uprightness of your heart. Approach her with reverence and devotion: and let your heart delight in her salutation.
pages.19:
Impend to her a sacrifice of praise: and be mindful of the breasts of her sweetness. For she pours out to you the rays of her piety: and she will brighten you with the flashes of her mercy. Her fruit is most sweet in the mouth: and it sweetens in the heart of the wise. Glory.

I will bless our Lady at every time: and her praise shall not fail in my mouth. Magnify her with me: all you who have been nourished by the honey and milk of her recreation. In perils and in doubtful matters, invoke her: and in necessities you may find aid and sweet refreshment. Take the example of her conversation: and emulate the studies of her charity and humility. Because, therefore, O Lady, you were most humble: you compelled the uncreated Word to take flesh from you.

Judge, O Lady, those who injure me and rise up against them: and vindicate my cause. My soul shall rejoice in you: and I will exult, devoted to your benefits. The heavens and the earth are full of your grace and sweetness: for wherever we go: the diffusion of your virginal womb meets us. Behold
pages.20:
and everywhere you have extended the snares of your kindness. Let us run, therefore, most beloved: and let us salute such a noble and sweet-flowing Virgin: so that we may rest in the bosom of her sweetness. **Glory**

The unjust man seeks to sin in secret: let him depart from his evil intent, O Mother of God. Incline the face of God upon us, compel him to have mercy on sinners. O Lady, your mercy is in heaven: and your grace is diffused over the earth. Power and virtue are in your arm: strength and fortitude in your right hand. Blessed be your empire over the heavens: blessed be your magnificence over the earth. **Glory**

Do not emulate those who act with malice, O Lady: sweeten their fury through your grace. Hope in her, O religious and cloistered: trust in her, O clerics and students. Delight in her praises and she will hear the petitions of your heart. Better is a little with her grace: than the treasures of silver and precious stones. **Glory forever**
pages.21:
be to you, O Queen of Heaven: and in no time do not forget us. Glory.

O Lord, do not argue with me in your fury: O Mother, obtain for us pardon for our sins. In your sight may our every desire be: our hope and our confidence. My heart is troubled within me: the light has departed from my bowels. Illuminate my blindness with your splendor: sweeten my contrition with your sweetness. Do not abandon us, O Lady, Mother of God: let your grace and virtue be at my right hand. ¶ Hail Mary

I have said I will guard my ways, O Lady, when grace of Christ was given to me through you. My heart has been liquefied by your sweetness: my bowels are inflamed by your love. Hear my prayer, O Lady, and my supplication: and let my adversaries pine away. Have mercy on me from the heavens and from the altitude of your throne: and do not permit me to be troubled in this valley of misery. Guard my foot that it may not be injured: and at my end let your grace be.

Waiting, I have waited for your grace: and you have done to me according to the multitude of your mercy.

<note>Red decorative initial O</note>Why do you glory in malice, O malignant serpent and infernal dragon? Submit your head to the woman, by whose fortitude you are submerged into the deep. Crush him, Lady, with the foot of your virtue; may he arise and dissipate his malice. Extinguish his power, and reduce his strength to ash. That we who live may exult in your name, and with a joyful spirit may say praise to you. <insert>Wednesday</insert>
<note>Red decorative initial O</note>The foolish enemy said in his heart: I will banish men from the tabernacle of the sons of God. I will go forth and be a lying spirit in the mouth of the serpent, and through the woman I will banish her man. Just as the stars of heaven are exalted from the earth, so are the thoughts of God exalted from your thoughts. Do not be puffed up by the fall of the woman, because the woman will crush your head. You prepared a pit for her
pages.29:
and in her snare you shall be caught. Glory to the Father.
<note>Red decorative initial D</note>Lady, save me in your name, and free me from my enemies. That the craftiness of the enemy may not harm me, protect me under the shadow of your wings. My Lady, help me; bestow your grace upon my soul. Voluntarily I will offer you a sacrifice of praise, and I will confess to your name, for it is good. You will free me from all tribulation, and my eye shall look down upon my enemies.
<note>Red decorative initial O</note>Hear, Lady, my prayer, and do not despise my supplication. I am saddened in my thought, because the judgments of God have terrified me. The darkness of death has come upon me, and the dread of hell has invaded me. But I, in my solitude, await your consolation, and in my bed I attend to your mercy. Glorify your right hand, your arm, so that our enemies may be cast down by us. Glory.
<note>Red decorative initial M</note>Have mercy on me, Lady, for my enemies have trampled upon me; daily all their thoughts are against me for evil.

N.text:
many good things are prepared for those who praise you. Blessed are you, Queen of angels; and may those who praise your magnificence be blessed by God. Glory to the Father.
My heart has uttered a good word, Lady, with mellifluous dew it was sweetened. By your holiness may my sins be purged; by your integrity may incorruptibility be granted to me. By your virginity my soul is loved by Christ, and is joined to him by the bond of death. By your fecundity I, a captive, have been redeemed; by your virginal birth I have been snatched from eternal death. By your most worthy fullness I have been restored, and from the exile of misery I have been led back to the first beatitude.
Lady, you are our refuge in all our necessity, and a more powerful virtue crushing the enemy. The world is full of your benefits; they surpass the heavens, they penetrate even the depths. By the fullness of your grace, those who were in the depths rejoice that they are freed. By the entitlement of your virginal fecundity, those who are above

the world rejoice that they are restored. By the glorious birth of your most holy virginity, men become companions and fellow citizens of the angels. Glory.

All nations, clap your hands; sing in jubilee to the glorious Virgin. For she is the gate of life, the doorway of salvation, and the way of our reconciliation. The hope of the penitent, the solace of those who mourn; blessed peace to hearts, and salvation. Have mercy on me, Lady, have mercy on me, because you are the light and hope of all who trust in you. By your salutary fecundity, may it please you that the pardon of sins be granted to me. Glory.

Great are you, Lady, and very praiseworthy in the city of the God of heaven, in the entire church of his elect. You have stood before the alternating angelic choirs, surrounded by roses and crowned with lilies. Run to her, powers and principalities; meet her, virtues and dominations. Cherubim, thrones, and seraphim, exalt her, and place her at the right hand of the spouse, her most beloved son. O with what joyful spirit

of mercy. I am overwhelmed by your ornaments:

and chrysolite on your left. Hyacinth
and agate on your breast: carbuncles
sparkling in your necklaces. Myrrh,

phire and emerald on your fingers.

<note>A red decorative initial O begins the text.</note>You have turned us away because of our sins,

are the sadness turned to exultation: and
rewarded with joy and sweetness. Gladden us
with the sweet-flowing sound of your mouth: and
pour into our hearts your rose-colored liquor. Give

<header>Wednesday</header>

<note>A red decorative initial 'N'.</note>Unless you, Lady, build the house of our heart, its building will not remain. Build us up by your grace and power so that we may remain firm forever. Blessed be your eloquence and blessed be all the words of your mouth. May those who bless you be blessed by God and may they be counted in the number of the just. Bless, Lady, those who bless you and never turn your glorious face away from them. Glory.

<note>A red decorative initial 'B'.</note>Blessed are all who fear our Lady: and blessed are all who know how to do your good pleasure. Blessed are the father and mother who bore you, whose memory remains forever. Blessed is the womb that carried you: and blessed are the breasts that suckled you. Turn your mercy upon us and be favorable toward your own. Look upon and regard our reproach: take away from us all our iniquities.

<note>A red decorative initial 'S'.</note>Often have they fought against me from my youth, my enemies: free me, Lady, and vindicate me from them. Do not give the power of my soul to them, guard
pages.67:
all my interior and exterior parts. Obtain for us the forgiveness of sins: through you may the grace of the Holy Spirit be given to us. Make us worthy to repent praiseworthily: so that we may come to God by a blessed end. Then, show us the placated and most serene glorious fruit of your womb.

<note>A red decorative initial O.</note>Out of the depths I have cried to you, Lady: Lady, hear my voice. May your ears be intent on the voice of my praise and glorification. Free me from the hand of my adversaries: confound their snares and their efforts against me. Rescue me in the day of evil: and in the day of death do not forget my soul. Lead me to the harbor of salvation: may my name be written among the just. Glory.

<note>A red decorative initial D.</note>Lady, my heart is not exalted: nor are my eyes lifted up. The Lord has blessed you in his power, who through you reduced our enemies to nothing. pages.68:
us, Lady, and comfort us in your grace: so that we may stand present before the face of the Lord. 

<note>A red decorative initial M.</note>Remember, Lady, David: and all those who call upon your name. Give us confidence in your name: and may our adversaries be confounded. Console us in the land of our pilgrimage: and relieve our poverty. Give us, O holy Virgin, the bread of tears: and the sorrow for sins in the land of our sojourning. Give back to us the propitious, blessed fruit of your womb: so that we may be filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit. Glory to the Father and to the Son.

<note>A red decorative initial E.</note>Behold, how good and how pleasant it is to love the name of Mary, your name. Your name is as oil poured out and spices to those who love it. Glory to the Father and to the Son.

<note>A red decorative initial E.</note>Behold now, bless the Lady, all you who hope in her holy name. Rejoice with great joy, you who exalt and glorify her: because you shall be satisfied from the breasts of her consolation. Behold, now, she will pour out abundance upon you to console and make your hearts joyful. Bless her, all you her servants: and may her memorial be in the desire of your soul. Bless her, all you angels and saints of God: praise her wonderful works forever.

<note>A red decorative initial L.</note>Praise the name of the Lord, bless the name of Mary, his mother. Frequent the prayers of Mary: and she will stir up in you eternal delights. With a contrite soul I will come to her and the desire of sin will not stimulate us. He who thinks of her in the tranquility of the mind finds sweetness and the rest of peace. Let us breathe toward her in our end: and she will unlock for us the halls of the triumphant. Glory to the Father and to the Son.

<note>A red decorative initial C.</note>Confess to the Lord, for he is good: for through his most beloved mother, the Virgin Mary, he gives mercy to us. Obtain for us
pages.70:
Lady, the friendship of Jesus Christ and guard our innocence. Compel our enemy by your command: lest he strike against us by the power of charity. Keep the good nature in us: and may good grace be multiplied through you. Illumine our ways and paths so that we may know what things are well-pleasing to God.

<note>A red decorative initial S.</note>By the rivers of Babylon the Hebrews wept: but we, let us lament over our iniquities. Let us cry out humbly to the Virgin who brought forth a child: let us offer her our mourning and our sighs. No propitiation is found without her: nor salvation without the fruit of her. Through her, sins are purged: and through the fruit of her, souls are made white. Through her, satisfaction is made for sins: through the fruit of her, the health of the soul is granted. Glory.

<note>A red decorative initial C.</note>I will confess to you, Lady, with my whole heart: because through you I have experienced the clemency of Jesus Christ. Hear, Lady, my words and my prayers, and in the sight of the angels I will sing praises to you.
pages.71:

<note>A red decorative initial D.</note>Lady, you have tested me and known me: my ruin and my transgression. Abundant has your mercy become upon me: and your clemency has been extended over me. May the light of your mercy make our hearts serene: and may the sweetness of your peace recreate us. Glory.

all my interior and exterior parts. Obtain for us the forgiveness of sins: through you may the grace of the Holy Spirit be given to us. Make us worthy to repent praiseworthily: so that we may come to God with a blessed end. Then show us the appeased and most serene, glorious fruit of your womb.

¶ Monday
I will confess to you, Lady, for through you the Lord is appeased toward me, and you have consoled me. Behold, Lady, my savior, I will act with confidence in you and will not fear. For you are my strength and my praise in the Lord, and you have become my salvation. I will draw waters in joy from the stream, and I will always invoke your name. Make known among the peoples the virtues of our Lady, for her name is exceedingly high. Exult and praise, O whole human race, because the Lord your God has given you such a mediatrix.
<note>A red decorative initial 'E'.</note>
¶ Tuesday
I said in the midst of my days: I go to Mary that she may reconcile me to Christ. I sought the remainder of my years in the bitterness of my soul. My generation has been taken away, for father and mother and all have abandoned me, but Mary has taken me up. I hoped in her morning, evening, and at noon; like a lion, she has crushed all the bones of my sins. And you, Lady, have saved my soul that it should not perish, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Lady, make me safe, and I will sing your praise in all
pages.78:
the days of my life, O pious mother of my Lord.
<margin>Wednesday</margin>
<note>A red decorative initial 'E'.</note> My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my heart has been exalted in my Lady. For he who is powerful has done great things for me through Mary, his mother. Now she is made as our Lady who alone has surpassed all. Let the old things depart from our mouth, and let us speak with new tongues. Exult and praise Mary, O Sion and Jerusalem, for Mary is among the ladies of Israel. She makes the poor, and she enriches; she humbles and she exalts. Higher than heaven, wider than the earth is this our Lady. Glory.
<margin>Thursday</margin>
<note>A red decorative initial 'O'.</note> Let us sing to the glorious Lady, the Virgin Mary; in hymns and confessions let us bless her. Our Lady, almighty through God, cast the chariot of Pharaoh and his army into the sea. Your right hand, Lady, has been magnified in strength, for in the multitude of your mercy you have laid out my adversaries. From the mouth of the lion you have freed me, Lady, and like an infant you have taken up my moan. Dearest Lady, cover me like a hen with your wonderful protection. I am wholly yours, and all my things are yours, O Virgin above all.

Because you are my strength and my praise in the Lord, and you have become my salvation. I will draw waters in joy from the rivulet, and I will always invoke your name. Make known among the peoples the virtues of our Lady, for her name is highly exalted. Exult and praise, O whole human race, because the Lord your God has given you such a mediatrix. ¶ Tuesday

I said in the midst of my days, I go to Mary that she may reconcile me to Christ. I sought the rest of my years in the bitterness of my soul. My generation was taken away, for father and mother and all have forsaken me, but Mary has taken me up. I hoped in her morning, evening, and at noon; like a lion, she thus crushed all the bones of my sins. And you, Lady, watched over my soul that it might not perish, and my only one from the hand of the dog. Lady, make me safe, and I will sing your praise in all
pages.78:
39

the days of my life, O pious mother of my Lord. <margin>Wednesday</margin>
<note>A red decorative initial 'E'.</note> My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my heart is exalted in my Lady. Because he has done great things for me, for he is powerful through Mary, his mother. Now she is made as she is our Lady, who alone has surpassed all. Let what is old depart from our mouth, and let us speak with new tongues. Exult and praise Mary, O Sion and Jerusalem, for Mary is among the ladies of Israel. She makes poor and enriches; she humbles and exalts. Higher than heaven, wider than the earth is this our Lady. Glory. <margin>Thursday</margin>
<note>A red decorative initial 'O'.</note> Let us sing to the glorious Lady, the Virgin Mary; in hymns and confessions let us bless her. Our Lady, the omnipotent through God, threw the name of her chariot and his army into the sea. Your right hand, Lady, is magnified in strength, for in the multitude of your mercy you have leveled my adversaries. From the mouth of the lion you have delivered me, Lady, and like a child you have taken up my lamentation. Dearest Lady, cover me like a hen with your wonderful protection. I am all yours, and all my things are yours, O Virgin, above all
pages.79:
<margin>Friday</margin>
blessed. Place me like a seal upon my heart, for love is strong as death. I have heard your report and I have been struck with awe; I considered your works and I trembled. Lady, you have brought to life your work in the midst of the years. I will confess to you, Lady, for you have hidden these things from the wise and have revealed them to the little ones. Your glory covered the heavens, and your mercy is full of the earth. You have gone forth, O Virgin, for the salvation of your people, for salvation with your Christ. O blessed one, our salvation is deposited in your hands; remember, O pious one, our poverty. Whoever will see her will be saved, and from whom you turn your face, he goes into destruction.

<margin>Saturday</margin>
Hear, O heavens, what I shall speak of Mary; let the earth hear the words of my mouth. Magnify her always with me, and let us exalt her name for ever and ever. You wicked and perverse generation, acknowledge our Lady, your savior. Is she not your mother who fed you and in faith generated you? If you dismiss her, you are not a friend of the supreme Caesar, because he himself will not save you without her.
pages.80:
40

If only you knew and understood, and provided for the last things. Just as an infant cannot live without a nurse, so you cannot have salvation without our Lady. Therefore, let your soul thirst for her; hold her and do not let her go until she has blessed you. Let your mouth be filled with her praise; sing her magnificence all day long. Glory to the Father.

<note>A red decorative initial 'B'.</note> Bless all the works of the glorious Lady; praise and exalt her forever. Bless, O angels, our Lady; bless, O heavens, our Lady. Let every creature bless our Lady, whom the King here wished to be blessed. Blessed are you, O daughter of the High King, who by your scent restore all lilies. Blessed are you, crown of all ladies; blessed are you, glory of Jerusalem. Your scent is like a field full of flowers which the Lord has blessed. For those who bless you abound, irrigating all their innermost parts. Whoever will bless you, O blessed Virgin, may he be blessed forever. Whoever will curse you, O most white rose, may he be cursed. May there not depart from the house of your servants, of wine and

N.text:
with the ointment of piety. <note>A red decorative paragraph mark.</note> Great is her virtue, and her clemency shall have no end. <note>A red decorative paragraph mark.</note> Sing to her in jubilation, and in confession sing a psalm to her. It is well-pleasing to her to be above those who fear God and in those who hope in her mercy. <note>A red decorative paragraph mark.</note> Glory.

<note>A large red decorative initial 'L'.</note> Praise the Lady, Jerusalem; glorify her, O Sion. For she builds up your walls and blesses your sons; she fattens your land and gives peace to your borders. The Most High sends forth his word, and her virtue has overshadowed it. Let us lift our hearts with our hands to her, that we may feel her influence.

<note>A large red decorative initial 'L'.</note> Praise our Lady from the heavens; glorify her in the highest. Praise her, all men and beasts, birds of the sky and fish of the sea. Praise her, O alone moon, stars, and circles of the planets. Praise her, Cherubim and Seraphim, Thrones, Dominions, and Powers. Praise her, all legions of angels; praise her, all orders of heavenly spirits.

X.text:
38

<note>A red decorative initial 'C'.</note> Sing to our Lady a new song; her praise is in the congregation of the just. Let the heavens rejoice in her glory, the islands of the sea, and the whole world. Let water and fire praise her, cold and heat, splendor and light. Let her exultations be in the throat of the just, and her praises in the gathering of the triumphant. City of God, rejoice in her, and for your inhabitants, frequent the song to her. Glory to the Father.

<note>A red decorative initial 'L'.</note> Praise the Lady in her saints; praise her in her virtues and miracles. Praise her, O assembly of the apostles; praise her, choirs of the patriarchs and prophets. Praise her, army of the martyrs; praise her, troops of doctors and confessors. Praise her in the college of virgins and those who are continent; praise her, orders of anchorites and monks. Praise her, gathering of all the religious; praise her, all souls of the heavenly citizens; every spirit praises our Lady. Glory.
Canticles.

<note>A large red decorative initial 'Q'.</note>Whoever wishes to be saved, before all things it is necessary that he hold to a firm faith in Mary. Unless each person keeps this whole and inviolate, without doubt, he will perish for eternity. For she alone remains a Virgin forever: she alone has destroyed all heresies. Let the Hebrew be confounded and blush who says that Christ was born from the seed of Joseph. Let the Manichaean be confounded: who says that Christ had a feigned body. Let everyone turn pale who says that this same person is from elsewhere and not from Mary.
pages.86: and not from her alone. For the Son, who is the only-begotten in the divinity of the Father, is also the true only-begotten Son of the Virgin Mary; in heaven without a mother, on earth without a father. Just as a rational soul and flesh are truly born as a human being through union, so God and man, Christ, are truly generated from Mary. He put on flesh from the flesh of the Virgin, which was fitting to redeem the human race. Who, according to his divinity, is equal to the Father; but according to his humanity, is lesser than the Father. Conceived in the womb of the Virgin Mary, the angel announcing it, by the Holy Spirit, but the Holy Spirit is not his father. He came into the world without the pain of the flesh of the Virgin Mother, whom he conceived without the pleasure of the flesh. Whom the Mother suckled from her breast, while the full heaven surrounded him, with the angels acting as midwives and announcing great joy to the shepherds. He, adored by the Magi with gifts; chased into Egypt by Herod; baptized by John in the Jordan; handed over, captured, scourged, crucified, died, and buried. He rose again with glory: he ascended into the heavens. He sent the Holy Spirit upon the disciples and the Mother.

of God, because you knew that he looked upon the humility of his handmaid. Through whom he gave the knowledge of salvation to his people, in the remission of their sins. Through the heart of the multitude of your mercy, visit us, O morning star rising from on high. Illuminate the darkness of those sitting in the shadow of death, and deign to illuminate them with the light of your most beloved Son. Have mercy, Mother of mercy, on us miserable sinners, who neglect to repent for past sins, and commit many things daily that require repentance. Glory be to the Father and to the Son.

<note>A red decorative initial 'E' beginning the paragraph "E matre dei...".</note> We praise you from the Mother of God: we acknowledge you, Mary the Virgin. To you all powers and all virtues of the heaven of heavens, and all dominions obey. To you all choirs, to you cherubim and seraphim exultantly assist. To you all angelic creation with ceaseless voice proclaims: Holy, Holy, Holy Mary, Mother of God
pages.83: and Virgin. Heaven and earth are full of the majesty of the glory of the fruit of your womb. The glorious choir of the apostles praises you as the mother of their Creator. The lovable dance of holy virgins proclaims you the example of virginity and humility. The whole celestial court honors you as Queen. pages.85:
of the inheritance of your Son. And rule over us and guard us eternally. Day by day, O pious one, we greet you. And we desire to praise you forever in mind and voice. Deign, sweet Mary, to keep us safe from sin now and always. Have mercy, pious one, have mercy on us. Let your great mercy be with us, because we, Virgin Mary, trust in you. In you, sweet Mary, we hope; may you defend us eternally. To you praise is fitting, to you rule is fitting; to you belongs virtue and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

<note>A large red decorative initial 'Q'.</note> Whoever wishes to be saved, before all things it is necessary that he hold firm faith regarding Mary. Which faith, unless each person preserves it whole and inviolate, without doubt he shall perish eternally. For she alone remains a virgin forever; she alone has destroyed all heresies. Let the Hebrew be confounded and blush, who says that Christ was born from the seed of Joseph. Let the Manichaean be confounded, who says that Christ had a feigned body. Let everyone turn pale who says this same thing of another, not of Mary
pages.86: as being born. For the Son, who in the divine is the only-begotten of the Father, is also truly the only-begotten Son of the Virgin Mary, in heaven without a mother, on earth without a father. Just as the rational soul and flesh are truly born as a man through union, so God and man, Christ, was truly generated from Mary. Putting on flesh from the flesh of the Virgin, just as it was fitting that the human race be redeemed. Who according to his divinity is equal to the Father: but according to his humanity is less than the Father. Conceived in the womb of the Virgin Mary while the angel announced it, by the Holy Spirit, not that the Holy Spirit is his father. Born in the manner of the flesh of the Virgin Mother, which he was conceived without the delectation of the flesh. Whom the Mother nursed with a breast full from heaven, whom the angels surrounded in the place of midwives, announcing to the shepherds great joy. He was adored by the Magi with gifts, driven into Egypt by Herod, baptized by John in the Jordan, betrayed, captured, scourged, crucified, died, and was buried. He rose again with glory: he ascended into heaven; he sent the Holy Spirit upon the disciples and the Mother.
pages.87:

pages.19: my members dedicated to generation or also touched the impudently of women and young girls: and I stained them with <term>fornicationibus</term> <gloss>fornications</gloss>. Item, I stained my belly with luxury and drunkenness. Item, I desired the heat of lust in my loins. Item, in my heart I held various thoughts and temptations which I would have brought to fulfillment had the fear of the world and the shame of men not restrained me. Item, I did not bend my knees to my God and the saints and superiors as I should have. Item, with my feet I ran to indulge in luxury, to steal, and to shed blood. However I have offended God with any member of my body, I state my guilt and confess it to God and to you. Sixth, I sinned in the last way of sinning, namely by omission. For when the poor person in need was established in necessity, I did not exercise the seven corporal works of mercy. For when I could, I did not give bread to the hungry, nor did I provide drink to the thirsty; the guest, the pilgrim, and the wanderer I did not lead to my own inn or to the right path; the sick I did not visit with necessities. The naked I did not cover with clothing; the justly imprisoned I did not redeem; the dead person abandoned I did not bury, nor did I cause to be buried. Item, I did not fulfill the spiritual works of mercy to which I was bound. For I did not teach those ignorant of the things that are the salvation of the soul. I did not give counsel to the one destitute of human help and the sinner. I did not chastise nor correct the wandering and the sinner. I did not comfort the sad and the desolate, nor did I spare those who were angry and doing evil.
pages.20:
I did not patiently endure injuries and insults brought upon me. Item, I did not pray to God for the salvation of the souls of friends and enemies, and I did not provide the reward of labor to those working for me. However I have not completed the works of mercy, I state my guilt and render myself culpable to God and to you.

### Concerning the twelve articles of faith

Seventh, I sinned because I did not firmly believe the twelve articles of faith, nor did I confess them with heart and mouth for justice; rather, I sometimes doubted concerning them and the sacraments of the altar. And I did not have living and just faith with good works as a good Christian, nor did I defend and preach my faith at all against Jews, infidels, and heretics. Rather, I willingly listened to those wandering and arguing against the faith.

### Concerning the seven sacraments of the church

Eighth, I sinned because I bypassed and neglected the seven sacraments of the church as a good Christian. First, because although I am baptized, I did not renounce the devil and his pomps as I promised in baptism. And although I am confirmed, I nonetheless blushed and neglected to speak and preach the faith of Christ and the truth because of the fear of the world. And I did not honor or keep the order of matrimony. Ecclesiastical orders
pages.21:
I received unworthily, and I exercised them unworthily in sin, and I did not honor those persons placed in holy orders for the sake of God. I did not perform the penance, fasts, prayers, or alms enjoined upon me for my sins. I neglected to make the profession of mouth and to receive the communion of the body of Christ. However I have sinned in the seven sacraments, I state my guilt and render myself culpable to God and to you.

### Concerning the seven theological and cardinal virtues

Ninth, I sinned by omission, because I neglected to keep the three theological virtues and the four cardinal virtues. In me there is not true faith in Christ with good works. In me there is not certain hope for future heavenly goods. In me there is not charity, which loves God above all things, and I have not loved my neighbor as myself. In me there is not prudence, because I did not do my actions as I ought to have done them when and how, and I acted in my deeds inconsiderately according to the desires of pleasure. In me there is not fortitude, because I did not manfully subjugate internal and external passions for Christ; I did not fear to do shameful and embarrassing things. In me there is not temperance, because I did not want to endure labors, fasts, and tribulations. In me there is not justice, because I did not decline from evil, but I neglected to do the good that I was bound to do. I did not justly give to each one what was his.
pages.22:
And because of my own utilities, I neglected the common good and the salvation of many. Whatever I have sinned against the seven virtues, I state my guilt and render myself culpable.

### Concerning the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit

Tenth, I sinned because I did not care for the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. In me there is not wisdom to contemplate divine things; in me there is not intellect to consider the final things of my death, the punishments of hell, and the day of judgment; in me there is not counsel to choose the good and reject the evil; in me there is not knowledge to recognize myself and my deeds; in me there is not fortitude to resist temptations, tribulations, and evil thoughts; in me there is not piety to sympathize with the poor and afflicted in heart and deed; in me there is not the fear of God to flee evil and seek salvation. However I have sinned in these, I state my guilt.

### Concerning the twelve fruits of the Holy Spirit

Eleventh, I sinned because I knowingly neglected the twelve fruits of the Holy Spirit. In me there is not charity, nor joy in the service of God, nor peace with my neighbor, nor patience in adversity, nor long-suffering in the face of foolishness, nor goodness in my life, nor kindness toward my neighbor, nor modesty
pages.23:
in my demeanor and attire and works, nor mildness in disturbances, nor humility in deeds, nor truth in words and speech, nor self-control and chastity in my affections. But I have sinned grievously against the aforementioned, like a horse and a mule in which there is no understanding. Concerning all and each of these, I state my guilt.

### Concerning the eight beatitudes

Twelfth, I sinned because I failed to live as a servant of Christ according to the eight evangelical beatitudes. First, I did not have voluntary poverty with spiritual intention. Second, I did not remain meek and mild in persecutions and injuries brought against me. Third, I did not lament my sins, nor did I approach this confession with the contrition I should have had. Fourth, I did not study to live justly, but I was accustomed to sins; I neglected to do good, to help, and to pray. Fifth, I was not merciful to myself and others, and I did not distribute the ecclesiastical goods entrusted to me to the poor. Sixth, I did not live with a pure heart toward God and my neighbor through good examples, but I remained a hypocrite in deeds and words with a double mind. Seventh, I was not a peacemaker, but because of the ambition for benefices and goods, I sowed discord and made schisms. Eighth, because not for the sake of Christ
pages.24:
did I endure the persecutions and curses of men, but when I could, I avenged myself. Twelfth, I have sinned because I failed to live according to the eight evangelical beatitudes as a servant of Christ. ¶ First, I did not have voluntary poverty with a spiritual intention. ¶ Second, I was not meek and mild in persecutions and in injuries brought upon me. ¶ Third, I did not weep for my sins, nor did I approach this confession with the contrition that I should have. ¶ Fourth, I did not strive to live justly, but I was accustomed to sins; I neglected to aid and pray for those doing good. ¶ Fifth, I was not merciful to myself and to others, and I did not distribute the ecclesiastical goods committed to me to the poor. ¶ Sixth, I did not live with a pure heart toward God and my neighbor through good examples, but I was a hypocrite in deeds and words with a double mind. ¶ Seventh, I was not a peacemaker, but because of ambition for benefices and goods, I sowed discord and created schisms. ¶ Eighth, because not for the sake of Christ
pages.24:
did I endure the persecutions and curses of men, but when I could, I avenged myself. Whenever and however I, an unhappy sinner, have sinned against the eight beatitudes and against all the aforementioned and each of them and their circumstances, knowingly or unknowingly, sleeping or waking, I render myself culpable to God and state my guilt. I seek indulgence from my God and absolution and a salutary penance from you, Father. I seek to be absolved from all sentences of excommunication, if I have perhaps incurred any by participating with those excommunicated or otherwise, and from all my sins for the sake of God.

Therefore, I beseech the most blessed Virgin **Mary**, the holy apostles of God **Peter** and **Paul**, and all the holy men and women of God, and you, Father, to pray for me to the Lord **Jesus Christ** that he may spare me all my mortal, criminal, and venial sins, those forgotten and neglected, those confessed by me, and those I would willingly confess if I had memory of them. And those which, from the time I began to sin until this present day, I have thought, said, and done, and the works I ought to have done but omitted. May he confer upon me grace so that hereafter I may not commit similar sins, and may he grant me a good end to my life and perseverance in good works, and may he lead this soul of mine to heavenly glory. And I ask you, Father, on behalf
pages.25: of God Almighty, and of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and of the holy Roman Church, and by the authority of the keys, that you absolve me from all my sins and offenses, those confessed, neglected, and forgotten, and from my mortal sins committed and omitted, and venial ones, and from whatever other offenses and sins, and from the other punishments of hell and purgatory which I have deserved for these sins.
