### On the Seven Theological and Cardinal Virtues

Ninth, I have sinned by omission, because I neglected to keep the three theological virtues and the four cardinal virtues. In me, there is no true faith in Christ with good works. In me, there is no certain hope for future heavenly goods. ¶ In me, there is no charity, which loves God above all things, nor have I loved my neighbor as myself. In me, there is no prudence, because I did not consider what, when, and how I ought to have performed my actions, and I carried out my actions incautiously according to the desires of pleasure. In me, there is no fortitude, because I did not manfully subjugate internal and external passions for Christ. I did not fear to do foul and shameful things. ¶ In me, there is no temperance, because I refused to sustain labors, fasts, and tribulations. ¶ In me, there is no justice, because I did not turn away from evil, but I neglected to do the good that I was bound to do. I did not justly give to each one what was his.

X.text:
And for the sake of my own utilities, I neglected the common good and the salvation of many. ¶ Whatever I have sinned against the seven virtues, I state my guilt and render myself culpable.

### ¶ The Seven Gifts of the Holy Spirit

Tenth, I have sinned because I did not care for the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. In me, there is no wisdom to contemplate divine things. In me, there is no intellect to consider the last things of my death, the pains of hell, and the day of judgment. In me, there is no counsel to choose the good and reject the evil. In me, there is no knowledge to recognize myself and my deeds. In me, there is no fortitude to resist temptations, tribulations, and evil thoughts. In me, there is no piety to sympathize with the poor and the afflicted in heart and deed. In me, there is no fear of God to flee from evil and seek salvation. ¶ However I have sinned in these, I state my guilt.

### ¶ The Twelve Fruits of the Holy Spirit

Eleventh, I have sinned because I knowingly neglected the twelve fruits of the Holy Spirit. In me, there is no charity, nor joy in the service of God, nor peace with my neighbor, nor patience in adversity, nor long-suffering in the face of the foolishness of others, nor goodness of my life, nor kindness toward my neighbor, nor modesty

Nor in my justifications do I cast my prayers before your face, but in your many and immense mercies, through our Lord Jesus Christ and the merits and intercessions of the glorious Virgin Mary and the blessed angel my guardian, John the Baptist, the blessed patriarchs, prophets, apostles, evangelists, martyrs, confessors, virgins, ascetics, and all your elect who have been pleasing to you from the beginning of the world, whose imitator I desire to be, a true and legitimate co-heir, a faithful servant, and a prudent and devoted son of yours. Finally, most sweet Father, I principally beseech you for the Christians in whom you do not dwell on account of their sins, that you may recall the haughty and disobedient to humility, the angry and the hateful and the slanderous and the murmurers to gentleness, the pusillanimous, the negligent, and the fearful to perseverance, the avaricious, the usurers, and the ambitious to the love of spiritual riches, the thieves, the robbers, and the obstinate to satisfaction, the liars, the impure, and the wicked judges to the acknowledgement
pages.37:
of you and the love of you, that you may restrain the gluttonous, the drunkards, and the spendthrifts to moderation, that you may lead back the immodest, the impudent, and the vain-speakers to the norm of honesty, that you may teach the luxurious, the impure, and the shameful to be chaste and real, and teach the wordy to be silent. And for all those living in the body or outside the body who are joined to us by blood, familiarity, or otherwise, and who have commended themselves to us by praying or asking, as well as those whose benefits or alms we have received, and to whomsoever we are bound, living or dead, that you may deign to mercifully grant them the desired indulgence of all their offenses and lead them kindly to eternal rest, through our savior your Son in the Holy Spirit. my coldness with the fire of your love; illuminate my blindness with the brightness of your presence. Turn for me all earthly things into bitterness, all heavy and contrary things into patience. May you alone become sweet to me from this time forth unto eternity, for you alone are my food and drink, my love and my joy, my sweetness. Would that you would totally ignite and burn me by your presence and transform me into yourself, so that I may be made one spirit with you through the grace of internal union and the liquefaction of burning love. Do not suffer me to depart from you fasting and arid, but mercifully work in me as you have often worked wonders with your saints. What wonder if I should be totally ignited from you and fail within myself, since you are the fire that always burns and never fails, love that purifies hearts and illuminates the intellect. Amen.

Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, have mercy on me, a miserable sinner, and on all your servants who today offer to you the most sacred and precious sacrament of our salvation, namely the sacrament of your precious body and blood. And give to us grace, virtue, and fortitude for immolating, offering, and consuming your most holy body and blood in right faith, firm hope,
pages.41: and perfect charity, with an increase of humility, patience, obedience, chastity, and all holiness. In the honor and praise of the most holy and undivided Trinity and the most blessed Virgin Mary. To the joy of the holy archangels and angels, patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins, and all your saints and elect who are already rejoicing in the eternal fatherland. And I pray that, just as you already make them rejoice in the full and serene splendor of your countenance without defect, so you may refresh us living in this misery with your grace, and deliver those who are in the pains of purgatory and are burning in the heat of your mercy. And just as you are joy to them, so may the reception of this vital sacrament be for us a support, and for those who are in pain, a refreshment. Have mercy therefore, most clement Lord Jesus Christ, through the virtue of this life-giving sacrament, upon your holy and universal church, and root out from it all evils, namely heresies, discords, and dissensions. Correct those who wander in it. Bring the incredulous to the faith. Cause the schismatics to return to the unity of the holy church and show them the light of your truth. Grant true penance to sinners. Make the just persevere in their good purpose. Have mercy on the Christian people. Defend the clergy. Deign to preserve the religious in your holy service. Fortify the laboring, the sad, and the lonely
pages.42: . Restore health of body and soul to the infirm. Bestow all things necessary for body and soul upon the poor and the needy. Cause pilgrims and exiles to return to their own with safety. Cause those placed in the perils of the waters to reach the port of their desire. Mercifully grant to those who are pregnant the joy of childbirth. Absolve those detained in bonds and prisons. Merciful Father, pardon all those with whom we have sinned or whom we have led to sin, and pardon us. Gracious Creator, pay on behalf of all those whom we have disturbed, injured, scandalized, or defrauded. Bestow all goods upon all our parents, friends, and enemies, our confreres and kinsmen, our familiars and benefactors, and those whose alms we use or have used, and all those who pray to God for us or commend themselves to our prayers, and defend them from all evil. Cause them to persevere in your service until the end. And after the course of this misery, grant them to arrive at you, who are the true fatherland, the eternal reward, and the glory. In tribulations, persecutions, and temptations, help those who cry out to you. Succor those placed in the agony of departing from this world and snatch their souls from the jaws of the roaring enemy. Grant true charity to our enemies and to us, and by the power of this sacrament, grant to all your faithful
pages.43:
the provision of help and consolation. Grant your grace to those still present in the flesh, and assist those who are to come with your mercy. To all those who have passed away, grant eternal rest. O God, who are triune and one, blessed for all ages of ages. Amen.

I aspire with intention. I embrace You with all my heart, and desire to receive Your body and blood, that You may remain in me always, and that I may not be separated from You, O most sweet Father. Amen. ¶ Another prayer before Mass.
<note>A red decorative initial 'O'</note>O most holy flesh, or holy communion of Christ, and blood. Hail, highest sweetness, who know no decay, who take away disgust, who kill death, who grant eternal life. Hail, blessed refreshment, who lead Your elect from the exile of this world to the homeland. Hail, happy host, who on the altar of the cross were offered to God the Father for the weight of our sins. Hail, manna whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, more precious than all gold. Take away, I beseech You, good Shepherd, my iniquities, that with purified body and spirit I may deserve to taste the Holy of Holies. And may this venerable sacrament be for me an impregnable defense against hostile snares, that, refreshed by this salutary food for the journey, I may be able to pass through the slippery paths of this life on an immaculate road, and arrive at You, the living and true bread, the Lord of the angels, without the impediment of diabolical fraud. Hear me, be placated, O Lord, attend, and see that I do not perish, for no one can be worthy of such a mystery unless You, through Your own work, make them worthy. Amen.
<note>A red decorative initial 'I'</note>Another prayer before Mass or holy communion.
O table of Your most sweet purity, pious Lord Je
pages.45: sus Christ, I, a sinner, presuming nothing of my own merit, but approaching in faith to Your mercy and goodness, fear and tremble. For I have a heart and body stained with many crimes. My mind and tongue have not been carefully guarded. Therefore, O pious Deity, O tremendous Majesty, I, a wretch, caught amidst distress, return to You, the fountain of mercy. I hasten to You to be healed; I flee under Your protection, and I, who cannot endure You as Judge, sigh to have You as Savior. To You, O Lord, I show my wounds; to You I uncover my shame. I know my sins are many and great, for which I am afraid. I hope in Your mercies, of which there is no number. Look therefore upon me with the eyes of Your mercy, pious Lord Jesus Christ, King eternal, God-man crucified for man. Hear me, who hope in You, and have mercy on me, full of miseries and sins, You who never cease to flow from the fountain of compassion. Hail, salutary victim, offered for me and all the human race on the gibbet of the cross. Hail, noble and most precious blood, flowing from the wounds of my crucified Lord Jesus Christ, and washing away the sins of the whole world. Remember, O Lord, Your creature, whom You have redeemed with Your sacred blood. It repents me that I have sinned; I desire to amend what I have done. Take away, therefore, from me, most merciful Father, all iniquities and sins, that with purified mind and body, I may worthily
pages.46:
deserve to taste. And grant that the holy libation of Your body and blood, which I, unworthy, intend to take, may be the remission of my sins. Let it be the perfect purging of my faults, the putting to flight of base thoughts, the ruling of good feelings, the healthy efficacy of works pleasing to You, and a most firm protection against the snares of my enemies. Amen.

<note>A red decorative initial 'O'</note>O Lord Jesus Christ, most pious and most merciful, I ask with all my heart that You forgive all my sins in this present life, that You do not afflict me with punishment for them, nor reserve any penalty for purgatory. O God of immense piety, whose strength is infinite, because without You I cannot resist sins, strengthen me in such a way that I may not now commit mortal sin, and that I may hereafter overcome every temptation of the devil. May I direct my whole life, thoughts, words, and works entirely to You, and may You guard me at the end of my life, lest the devil cast me into the pit of hell and thus lead me into desperation. O fountain emanating charity, make my mind free from every creature that could attract it to itself and hinder Your love, so that I may be perfected in Your love. Now and at the end of my life, may I worthily take You, and thus may You lead my soul, stripped of the sack of the body, to the pious eternal palace, to see clearly the mirror of the Holy Trinity. Amen. <note>Actions of thanksgiving to be said after Mass at one's pleasure follow here.</note>
pages.47:
<note>A red decorative initial 'S' at the beginning of the text.</note>Most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which I, most unworthy, have taken, and for the salvation of my soul and body were sacrificed on the cross, I beseech You, through the mystery of Your admirable sacrament, that You may save and protect my soul and body from all fraud and illusion of demons. And through this offering, which I have offered to You for the praise and glory of Your name, may You erase all my sins and not permit me to be deceived or punished by the devil or any creature on account of my sins. But You, most pious God, rebuke and correct me in Your mercy, and grant me, Lord, faith, hope, charity, humility, patience, obedience, and chastity of mind and body, and the love of You and my neighbor. I also humbly ask You, through Your most holy body which I, unworthy, have taken, and the chalice which I have drunk, and that peace which You made between God and man, who offered Yourself as a living and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father, that You may strengthen peace and concord among us Christians, through that terror which, hanging on the cross, You made formidable to the serpent devil, acceptable to friends, and appeasing to enemies. And make me, so that I may rejoice in Your peace and that of the whole Church in the present and future prosperity.

¶ Also, I ask You through the communion of Your most holy body and blood and through the drops of bloody sweat
pages.48:
for me, through the anguish of Your most holy death, and through the merits of the most holy Virgin, the exalted Mother, our Lady, Saint Mary, and of all the saints and elect, that You deign to deliver the souls of our parents and benefactors and all the faithful from the lake of hell and from the anguishes of the abyss, and to place them in the kingdom of eternal clarity. O good Jesus, through Your most holy blood and body, deliver me from all sins and dangers, from sudden death, and proceed with perfect contrition for all sins, a full confession, with the invocation of Your holy name, and transfer me into the region of eternal peace. Who with the Father
<note>A red decorative initial 'G'</note>Another prayer after communion.
I give thanks to You, O God. I give thanks to You, true life of the living, eternal hope of believers, Jesus Christ, fostering Redeemer, who alone are to be adored, loved, and praised, who alone doest wondrous things, who, because You have left us, Your poor ones to be consoled, as pilgrims and orphans in this misery, through the mystery of the priests, through words from the mouth and in Your name, open the heavens and descend and fill all the earth with blessing. Who do not disdain to be handled, blessed, and consecrated by the hands of man for our salvation. Who, through His mystery, exhibits outwardly the signs of the sacrament. But You, O invisible God, re
pages.49: maining the one who acts. To You, therefore, Lord our God, great and immense, eternal and exalted, to You be praise, to You be glory, to You be thanksgiving now and forever, because You delivered this same incomprehensible mystery, as the article of Your salutary Passion drew near, to Your disciples with such gratuitous piety. Moved by mercy and paternal affection, You spoke to them, saying: "I have desired with desire to eat this passover with you before I suffer," as if You were saying: "I have desired with desire to deliver Myself to you." Then, bearing Yourself marvelously in Your own hands, You testified, saying: "This is my body." "Take this for your salvation, as often as you take it in my commemoration and in memory of the love with which I have loved you, when I left Myself as a pledge of salvation." O inestimable love of Your charity, Lord Jesus Christ, kind One, that You may reconcile us, unworthy, to Your Father, You exhibit Yourself as a salutary victim. Therefore, I humbly implore the immense clemency of Your mercy, that this sacrament of Your highest charity and union may be for me and all Your faithful the most efficacious medicine against the wounds of all our sins, and the complement of all virtue and grace. May it be the most powerful protection against all evils and the most solid support of eternal beatitude. Amen.
pages.50:

I give thanks to You and refer praises to You, Lord my God, who have deigned to create me from nothing to Your image and likeness, to redeem me with Your precious blood, to aggregate me among the adopted sons through the ablution of holy baptism, and to refresh me with the mysteries of the price of Your body and blood. Therefore, I give praises and thanks to You, who from the time of my raw infancy until this hour, through many flowing vices, have awaited me for amendment with the patience of Your immense piety. I praise You, I glorify You, who have most often delivered me from many tribulations and anguishes, calamities and miseries. Who have hitherto mercifully exempted me from eternal punishments and from the torments of body and soul. I praise You, I glorify You, who have mercifully bestowed upon me the soundness of limbs, the tranquility of times, and the effect of good things, along with many other virtues. I ask, Lord God, in Your ineffable sweetness, that You may perfect in me the begun benefits and gifts. And whatever displeases You in me, repel it; and deliver me from all the tribulations and iniquities and diverse evils that still remain and in which I am entangled. Dispose my thoughts, words, and acts alike according to Your will. Amidst adversity and
pages.51:
prosperity, guard me always and everywhere, and finally lead me happily to the desired joys of Your vision. ¶ After Mass.
<note>A red decorative initial 'L'</note>These are the first things that please You, which You left for us orphans in memory of Your love. O Wisdom of the Father, born of a Virgin, who did not disdain to have Your venerable body touched and taken by me, an unworthy sinner. What shall I worthily return to You for all that You have repaid? For if the merits of the whole world were gathered into one, they would not be able to be compared in any way to Your dignity. Therefore, I give thanks to You, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, King of kings and Lord of lords. I refer actions of thanksgiving for the power of my frailty to Your tremendous majesty and immense piety, most pious Jesus, because You have sweetly refreshed my soul, which was too arid, with Your sacred body and blood. I ask You that whatever is found in me as vicious and contrary to Your will, You may root out utterly through the contrition of this sacred rite, and prepare my heart as a worthy dwelling place for the Holy Spirit. And most sweet Jesus, may this sacrament of Your body and blood be the sweetness and delight of my soul, salvation and holiness in every temptation, peace and joy in every tribulation, light and solace in every virtue and work, and a final protection in death. Amen. ¶ Prayer after Mass.

Hail, supreme sweetness, that knows no decay, removes loathing, kills death, and bestows eternal life. Hail, blessed refreshment, that leads your chosen ones from the exile of this world to the fatherland. Hail, happy host, which was offered on the altar of the cross to God the Father for the weight of our sins. Hail, manna whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, more precious than all gold. Take away, I beseech you, good Shepherd, my iniquities, that, with purified body and spirit, I may deserve to taste the Holy of Holies. And may this venerable sacrament be for me an impregnable protection against hostile ambushes, so that, refreshed by this salutary provision, I may be able to pass through the slippery paths of this life on an immaculate way and reach you, the living and true bread, the Lord of angels, without the hindrance of diabolical fraud. Hear me, be appeased, O Lord; attend and ensure that I do not perish, for by yourself, no one can be worthy of so great a mystery unless you, the one who receives, make them worthy. Amen.
<note>A red decorative initial 'I'</note>Also another prayer before Mass or holy communion.
O table of your sweetest purity, pious Lord Je
pages.45: sus Christ. I, a sinner, presuming nothing from my own merits, but approaching with faith in your mercy and goodness, fear and tremble. For I have a heart and body stained with many crimes. My mind and tongue have not been kept carefully. Therefore, O pious Deity, O tremendous Majesty, I, a wretch, caught in distress, return to you, the fountain of mercy. I hasten to you to be healed; I flee under your protection. And I sigh to have you as my Savior, whom I cannot endure as a judge. Lord, I show you my wounds; I uncover my shame to you. I know my sins are many and great, for which I fear. I hope in your mercies, of which there is no number. Look therefore upon me with the eyes of your mercy, pious Lord Jesus Christ, King, eternal God, human crucified for the sake of man. Hear me, hoping in you, and have mercy on me, full of miseries and sins, you who will never cease to flow in the fountain of mercy. Hail, salutary victim offered for me and for all the human race on the gibbet of the cross. Hail, noble and most precious blood flowing from the wounds of my crucified Lord Jesus Christ, and washing away the sins of the whole world. Remember, Lord, your creature, whom you have redeemed with your sacred blood. It repents me that I have sinned; I desire to amend what I have done. Take away, therefore, from me, most clement Father, all iniquities and sins, that with a purified mind and body, I may worthily
pages.46:
deserve to taste. And grant that this holy libation of your body and blood, which I, unworthy, intend to take, may be the remission of my sins. Let it be the perfect purging of my offenses. Let it be the driving away of foul thoughts, the reigning of good senses, and the wholesome efficacy of works pleasing to you. Let it be the strongest protection against the ambushes of my enemies. Amen.

<note>A red decorative initial 'O'</note>O Lord Jesus Christ, most pious and most merciful. I ask with my whole heart that you forgive all my sins in this present life, that you do not afflict me with punishment for them, nor reserve any penalty for purgatory. O God of immense piety, whose strength is infinite, since without you I cannot resist sins, strengthen me in such a way that I do not now commit mortal sin. And may I henceforth overcome every temptation of the devil, and direct my life, thoughts, words, and works entirely to you. And at the end of my life, guard me, lest the devil cast me into the pit and so lead me into desperation. O fountain emanating charity, make my mind free from every creature that could attract it to itself and hinder it from your love, so that I may be perfected in your love. Now and at the end of my life, may I worthily take you and thus lead my soul, stripped from the satchel of the body, to your eternal palace, to see clearly the mirror of the Holy Trinity. Amen. <note>Followed by acts of thanksgiving to be said after Mass at one's pleasure.</note>
pages.47:
<note>A red decorative initial 'S' at the beginning of the text.</note>Most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which I, most unworthy, have received and which was sacrificed on the cross for the salvation of my soul and body, I beseech you, through the mystery of your admirable sacrament, to save my soul and body and protect me from every fraud and illusion of demons. Through this oblation, which I have offered to you in praise and glory of your name, may you delete all my sins and not permit me to be deceived or punished by the devil or any creature on account of my sins. But do you, most pious God, rebuke and correct me in your mercy, and give me, Lord, faith, hope, charity, humility, patience, obedience, and chastity of mind and body, and the love of you and of my neighbor. I also humbly ask you, through your most sacred body which I, unworthy, have received, and the chalice which I have drunk, and that peace which you made between God and man, who offered yourself as a living and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father, that you may strengthen peace and concord among us Christians, through that terror which, hanging on the cross, you made formidable to the serpent devil, acceptable to friends, and appeasing to enemies. Make me also to rejoice in your peace and the prosperity of the whole Church, present and future.

¶ Also, I ask you through the communion of your most holy body and blood and through the drops of your bloody sweat
pages.48:
through the distress of your most holy death, and through the merits of the most holy Virgin, the exalted mother of our Lord, Saint Mary, and of all the saints and elect, that you may deign to deliver the souls of our parents and benefactors and of all the faithful from the lake of hell and from the distresses of the underworld, and place them in the kingdom of eternal clarity. O good Jesus, through your most holy blood and body, deliver me from all sins and dangers, from sudden death, and proceed with perfect contrition for all sins, a full confession with the invocation of your holy name, and transfer me into the region of eternal peace. Who with the Father
<note>A red decorative initial 'G'</note>Another prayer after communion.
I give thanks to you, God. I give thanks, O true life of the living, eternal hope of believers, Jesus Christ, gracious redeemer, who alone are to be adored, loved, and praised. Who alone do wonders, who for the sake of us your poor, needing consolation, whom you have left in this misery as if we were pilgrims and orphans, through the mystery of the priests, through the words from your mouth and in your name, you open the heavens and descend and fill the whole earth with a blessing. Who do not disdain to be handled by the hands of man, to be blessed and consecrated for our salvation. Who through your mystery exhibit to the outside the signs of a sacrament. But you, O invisible God, re
pages.49:
maining the one who does these things.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>To you, therefore, our Lord God, great and immense, eternal and exalted, to you be praise, to you be glory, to you be thanksgiving now and forever, who, at the impending moment of your saving passion, with such gratuitous piety, handed down this very incomprehensible mystery to your disciples. Moved by mercy and paternal affection, you addressed them saying: I have desired with desire to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. As if you were saying: I have desired with desire to hand myself over to you.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Then, bearing yourself wonderfully in your own hands, you protested, saying: This is my body.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Take this for your salvation, as often as you take it, in my commemoration and in memory of the love with which I loved you, when I left myself as a pledge of salvation.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>O inestimable love of your charity, Lord Jesus Christ, kind that you are, so that you may reconcile us unworthy ones to your Father, you exhibit yourself as a salutary victim.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Therefore, I humbly pray for the immense clemency of your mercy, insofar as this sacrament of your supreme charity and union may be for me and for all your faithful the most effective medicine against the wounds of all our sins and the complement of all virtue and grace; may it be the strongest protection against all evils and the most solid support of eternal beatitude. Amen.
pages.50:
<note>Decorative red initial 'G' at the beginning of the prayer.</note>Item, another prayer after Mass.

I give thanks to you and render praises to you, Lord my God, who deigned to create me from nothing to your image and likeness, to redeem me with your precious blood, and through the ablution of holy baptism to aggregate me among the adopted sons, and to refresh me with the price of the mysteries of your body and blood. Therefore, I offer praises and thanks to you, who, from the time of my raw infancy until this hour, through many flowing vices, have awaited me with the patience of your immense piety for amendment. I praise you, I glorify you, who very often delivered me from many tribulations, distresses, calamities, and miseries. Who until now have mercifully exempted me from eternal punishments and from the torments of body and soul. I praise you, I glorify you, who in the health of my limbs, in the tranquility of times, and even in the effect of good things, along with many other virtues, have mercifully endowed me. I ask, Lord God, that you would make your begun benefits and gifts effective in me through your ineffable sweetness. And whatever displeases you in me, repel it, and deliver me from all the remaining tribulations and iniquities and diverse evils in which I am entangled. Order my thoughts, words, and acts equally in your will. Between adversity and
pages.51:
prosperity, always and everywhere, guard me, and finally lead me happily to the desired joys of your vision. 
<note>Red paragraph mark</note>Go, after Mass.
<note>Red decorative initial 'L'</note>These are the first things which are pleasing to you, which you left to us orphans in memory of your love. O source of wisdom, born of the Virgin, who did not disdain for your venerable body to be touched and taken by me, an unworthy sinner. What shall I worthily render to you for all the things you have repaid? For if the merits of the whole world were gathered into one, it would not suffice to be compared in any way to your dignity. I give thanks, therefore, to you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, King of kings and Lord of lords. I offer actions of thanks to your tremendous majesty and immense piety for the power of my fragility, most pious Jesus, that you have sweetly refreshed my soul, which was too arid, with your sacred body and blood. I ask you that whatever you find in me that is vicious and contrary to your will, may be thoroughly eradicated by the power of this sacred rite, and may you prepare my heart to be a worthy dwelling place for the Holy Spirit. And, sweetest Jesus, may this sacrament of your body and blood be the sweetness and delight of my soul, my health and holiness in every temptation, my peace and joy in every tribulation, my light in every virtue, and my consolation in every work, my final protection in death. Amen.

X.text:
<note>A red decorative initial 'S' at the beginning of the text.</note>Most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which I, most unworthy, have received and which was sacrificed on the cross for the salvation of my soul and body, I beseech you, through the mystery of your admirable sacrament, to save my soul and body and protect me from every fraud and illusion of demons. Through this oblation, which I have offered to you in praise and glory of your name, may you delete all my sins and not permit me to be deceived or punished by the devil or any creature on account of my sins. But do you, most pious God, rebuke and correct me in your mercy, and give me, Lord, faith, hope, charity, humility, patience, obedience, and chastity of mind and body, and the love of you and of my neighbor. I also humbly ask you, through your most sacred body which I, unworthy, have received, and the chalice which I have drunk, and that peace which you made between God and man, who offered yourself as a living and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father, that you may strengthen peace and concord among us Christians, through that terror which, hanging on the cross, you made formidable to the serpent devil, acceptable to friends, and appeasing to enemies. Make me also to rejoice in your peace and the prosperity of the whole Church, present and future.

¶ Also, I ask you through the communion of your most holy body and blood and through the drops of your bloody sweat

pages.52: <note>A red decorative drop cap 'S'</note>Blood of the most sacred body of our Lord Jesus Christ, which was offered on the cross for the salvation of the human race. I, a most miserable sinner entangled in many sins, humbly implore You: through Your wondrous mystery, save my soul and body, and protect me from every deception and fraud of the devil and all my enemies. And through this most holy oblation, which I also have offered today for the praise and glory of Your name, and for the memory of Your passion, and for the honor of the most holy Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, and of all the saints, deign to erase all my sins. Do not permit me, most clement Lord, to be punished or captured by the devil or any other creature on account of my sins. But You, most pious Lord, who show mercy to all, deign to have mercy on me and correct me in Your infinite mercy, and not in anger. Grant me, most pious Lord, a right faith, a firm hope, and a perfect charity, an unfaked patience, and such penance as may please You, my God, so that Your holy angels may rejoice in my conversion. I pray to You, my God, through that peace which You made between God and man when You offered Yourself as a pure and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father on the cross, that You may make and confirm peace and harmony between me and all faithful Christians. And by that terror which, hanging on the cross, You struck into the serpent
pages.53: formidable to the devil and acceptable to friends, make me reconciled, so that I may rejoice in Your peace and that of the whole Church, and in present and future prosperity. Savior of the world, save us, who have redeemed us through Your blood and cross; assist us, we pray You, our God. I pray to You, Lord Jesus Christ, by the drops of Your bloody sweat, by the agonies of Your most precious death, by the merits and intercession of Your most blessed Mother, the perpetual Virgin Mary, by the prayers of blessed John the Baptist, and of all the saints pleasing to God, that You may free me, Your servant, [and] also Your servants, and all my parents, benefactors, and those entrusted to me, from every danger of body and soul, and grant us a perpetual dwelling in the heavenly fatherland after this life. And free also, Lord, the souls of Your servants and handmaids, and of my parents and benefactors, and those entrusted to me, from the lake of hell and from the mire of filth, and place them in the kingdom of peace and eternal brightness. I ask You, most pious Lord, through the most holy presence and libation of Your body and blood, that You may free me from all my sins, past, present, and future, from necessities and agonies, and from the snares of all enemies, visible and invisible. And I ask You, most pious Lord Jesus Christ, that in
pages.54:
the trembling hour of my death, You may not deny me the full and perfect communion of Your most holy body and blood, with the happy promise of the present life. Amen.

<note>A red decorative initial 'A'</note>Other useful and devout acts of thanksgiving to be said after communion.

<note>A red decorative initial 'G'</note>I give thanks to Your immense majesty and everlasting piety, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who, not because any merits of mine demanded it, but through Your many and great mercies, have deigned to satisfy me, Your unworthy servant and miserable sinner, with the body and blood of Your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. And I pray that this communion may not be for me a matter of punishment, but a salutary intercession for pardon. Let it be for me the armor of faith and the shield of good will. Let it be the evacuation of my vices, the extermination of concupiscence and lust, the augmentation of humility, charity, patience, chastity, obedience, and all virtues, and of all holiness and salvation. Let it be a firm defense against the snares of all my enemies, visible and invisible, the perfect quieting of my motions, both carnal and spiritual, a firm adhesion to You, the living and true God, and the happy consummation of my end.
pages.55:
<note>A red paragraph mark</note>May it be, I beseech You, holy Father, that this most holy sacrament of the body and blood of Your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, be the sweetness and pleasantness of my soul, its salvation and sanctity in every temptation, peace and joy in every tribulation, light and virtue in every word and deed, solace and final protection in death. And I pray You that through this I may deserve to be filled with Your Holy Spirit, and directed along the way of Your commandments, and that I may be refreshed by this same viaticum at the last moment of my life, and having been refreshed now, be preserved without intermission until then, and be led by Your holy angels to that place where You Yourself are to Your saints the true light, full satisfaction, consummate joy, perfect happiness, and everlasting joy. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen. 

<note>A red paragraph mark</note>We give You thanks for all the blessed, asking to be helped by their intervention. 

<note>A red paragraph mark</note>But for those who are in the places of purgatory, the Son offers Himself to You, Father, in supplication, so that through this most holy host their pain may be lighter and shorter. 

<note>A red paragraph mark</note>But for us, whom sins of flesh and blood still weigh down, the Son offers Himself to You, Father, in supplication, so that the blood of Your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may wash away the sins we have contracted from flesh and blood, and His flesh may cleanse us. Amen.

<note>A large red decorative initial 'A'</note>Hail, most holy flesh, the highest sweetness of life.
pages.56: which is, before all things, a sweet heavenly drink to me. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Most kind and most pious lover and reconciler of the human race, Jesus Christ, the eternal salvation of all who love You, who, on account of Your patience, have permitted me, an unworthy sinner, with polluted heart and mouth, to receive Your holy body and blood, which everyone who receives unworthily receives not as a remedy but as judgment. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>I beseech You, be merciful to me, a most unworthy sinner. And You who are the true and eternal life, deign through these holy things which I have taken to remit all the iniquity and impiety of my former life, and to transform the action of my subsequent life into the praise and glory of Your most holy name, so that when I am presented to You for judgment after this life, do not, I beseech You, most clement God, condemn me on account of my innumerable sins. But through this reception of our redemption, avert from us Your anger, which I admit with much grief I have very often provoked by my many negligences and the perpetration of sins. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O most serene and illustrious Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, perpetual Virgin, who were worthy to carry in Your most sacred womb the same Creator of all creatures, whose true body and blood I, a miserable and unworthy sinner, have taken and received, I humbly beseech Your mercy that You may deign to intercede for me with Him,
pages.57: so that whatever I have committed in His ineffable sacrament, whether ignorantly or negligently, He may deign to forgive me through Your most holy prayers, by His ineffable piety and inenarrable mercy. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O you all, angelic choirs, angels, archangels, virtues, powers, dominations, principalities, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim, who, having been inebriated from the abundance of the fountain of the deific Trinity, have received eternal splendor from the light of the eternal divinity itself, in whom you, being happy, truly blessed, rejoice assiduously in gladness, loving without satiety, seeing without a medium, you eat with full mouth that same honeyed bread of eternal life, which today has deigned to gladden me, a poor man, with its goodness. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>You, the blessed and elect, I, an exile and an orphan, humbly implore that, standing today in the sight of His throne, you may sing with a unanimous voice a hymn and praise to His glory, praising together the condescension of the life-giving divinity, which has deigned to look upon me, unworthy as I am, in the perception of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Dismissal. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O you, number of the elect and all citizens of heaven, chorus of patriarchs, John the Baptist, precursor of Christ, John the Evangelist, the chaste guardian of Christ, the laudable number of apostles, the roseate army of martyrs, the glorious chorus of priests and confessors
pages.58: and the chaste virgin and widowed army of the brides of Christ. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>I summon you all, the beloved and elect of God, and I ask you with a suppliant vow to praise and glorify for me our Lord <note>A red letter 'I'</note>Jesus Christ, the bestower of all good things, who, though I am unworthy, has fed me with His holy body and has given me His own blood to drink, He who came from heaven and wished to be incarnate by <note>A red letter 'M'</note>the glorious Virgin Mary, and here gives life to the world. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Ask also, pious fathers, that, helped by your merits, the sweetness of His most sacred body may reach me and remain in me, and that I may feel no other sweetness of flavor than that. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Implore also for me, before the glorious Virgin <note>A red letter 'M'</note>Mary, Mother of God, that she may obtain for me from her Son, Jesus Christ, purity of life, contrition for sins, true confession, and worthy satisfaction, and after this misery of life, may associate me with His promises and joys, He Himself granting it, who lives and reigns as God for ever and ever. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O blessed and sanctified and glorious Trinity, Creator and Governess of all, holy and undivided Unity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, of whose exuberant and magnificent glory heaven and earth are full. Through the fruit of the ever-Virgin <note>A red letter 'M'</note>Mary, consecrated by You, Holy Trinity, born of the everlasting Begetter, and co-eternal and glorious to the same Begetter, who was crucified for us, deign to consecrate me today with the Holy Spirit, most pure in heart and chaste in body, to receive Him, so that through this sweet nourishment of the most holy body and the chalice of His precious blood, all the increments of vices may perish in me, and I may deserve to be united to the very fountain of all good things, in whom, having been absolved and sanctified, I may have the strength to see and praise happily, enjoying Him together with the angels forever, my Lord and the spouse of my soul, the Trinity and one God, for ever and ever. Amen.
pages.59: <note>A red pilcrow symbol</note>Adorable Trinity and to-be-admired Unity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, true light and blessed light, incomprehensible to human senses. Come to me, heart born of the Parent, food filling the Virgin, holy light shining upon the blind. May it be permitted to me to taste and relish the worthy host, the blessed body of Jesus Christ, our Savior, with the palate of my heart, and to kiss and embrace my sweetest lover by the arms of faith and love. Finally, however, when this corruptibility is removed, may I freely grasp my most noble Co-heir, together with the angels and the choirs of holy virgins, through whom I may know from then on the Trinity and the true Unity, perfectly praising Him for ever and ever. Amen. <note>A red pilcrow symbol</note>Here follows the jubilus of Saint Bernard.

pages.52: <note>Decorative red drop cap "S"</note>Most sacred body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which was shed on the cross for the salvation of the human race. I, a most miserable sinner, bound by many sins, humbly implore You that through Your wonderful mystery You may save and protect my soul and body from all deception and fraud of the devil and all my enemies. And through the most holy offering, I too have offered today for the praise and glory of Your name and for the memory of Your passion, and for the honor of the most holy Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, and of all the saints; may You deign to erase all my sins, and, most merciful Lord, do not permit me to be given over to the devil or to any creature for punishment or destruction on account of my sins. But You, most pious Lord, who show mercy to all, deign to have mercy on me, and correct me in Your infinite mercy and not in Your anger. Give me, most pious Lord, a right faith, a firm hope, and perfect charity, a patience that is not feigned, and such penance as may please You, my God, so that Your holy angels may rejoice in my conversion. <note>Red decorative initial 'G'</note>I give thanks to Your immense majesty and everlasting piety, Lord holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who, with no merits of mine requiring it, but through Your many and great mercies, have deigned to satisfy me, Your unworthy servant and miserable sinner, with the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. And I pray that this communion may not be for me guilt unto punishment, but a salutary intercession unto pardon. May it be for me armor of faith and a shield of good will. May it be the evacuation of my vices, the extermination of concupiscence and lust, and the augmentation of humility, charity, patience, chastity, obedience, and all virtues, as well as of all holiness and salvation. May it be a firm defense against the snares of all my enemies, visible and invisible; a perfect quieting of my motions, both carnal and spiritual; a firm adhesion to You, the living and true God; and the happy consummation of my end.

<note>A red paragraph mark</note>May it be, I beseech You, holy Father, that this most sacred sacrament of the body and blood of Your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, be the sweetness and pleasantness of my soul, its salvation and sanctity in every temptation, peace and joy in every tribulation, light and virtue in every word and deed, and my final solace and protection in death. And I pray to You that through this I may deserve to be filled with Your Holy Spirit, and directed along the path of Your commandments; that I may be refreshed by this same viaticum <note>a traveler's provision, here referring to the Eucharist for the dying</note> at the final article of my life; that I may be preserved without intermission until then, having been refreshed now; and that I may be led to that place by Your holy angels where You Yourself are for Your saints the true light, the full satisfaction, the consummate joy, perfect happiness, and everlasting gladness. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>We give You thanks for all the beatified, asking to be helped by their intercession. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>But for those who are in the places of purgatory, the Son offers Himself to You, Father, in supplication, that through this most holy host their pain may be lighter and shorter. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>But for us who are still burdened by the sins of the flesh and blood, the Son offers Himself to You in supplication, that the blood of Your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may wash away the sins which we have contracted from flesh and blood, and that His flesh may cleanse us. Amen.
<note>Large decorative initial A</note>Hail, most holy flesh, supreme sweetness of life,
pages.56: which is heavenly drink, sweet to me above all things. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Most kind and most pious lover and reconciler of the human race, Jesus Christ, eternal salvation of all who love You, who, on account of Your patience, have permitted me, an unworthy sinner, to receive Your holy body and blood with a polluted heart and mouth, which also everyone who receives unworthily, receives not for a remedy but for judgment. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>I beseech You, be propitious to me, a most unworthy sinner. And You who are the true and eternal life, deign through these sacred things which I have consumed to remit all the iniquity and impiety of my former life and to transform the action of my subsequent life into the praise and glory of Your most holy name. So that when I am presented to You for judgment after this life, do not, I beseech You, most merciful God, condemn me on account of my innumerable sins, but through this reception of our redemption, avert Your anger from us, which, alas, I confess to have stirred up most frequently by my many negligences and the perpetration of sins. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O most serene and renowned Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, perpetual Virgin, who were worthy to carry the same Creator of all creatures in Your most sacred womb, whose same most true body and blood I, a miserable and unworthy sinner, have taken to handle and consume, I humbly pray for Your mercy that You may deign to intercede for me to Him,
pages.57:
so that whatever I have committed in His ineffable sacrament through ignorance or negligence, He may deign to forgive me through Your most holy prayers by His ineffable piety and inenarrable mercy. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O you all, angelic assemblies, angels, archangels, virtues, powers, dominations, principalities, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim, who, inebriated by the abundance of the fountain of the deific Trinity, have received eternal splendor from the light of the eternal divinity itself, in which you who are happy truly rejoice as blessed, constantly in gladness, loving without weariness, seeing without intermediary, eating with a full mouth that very honey-sweet bread of eternal life which has deigned to gladden me, a poor man, by its goodness today. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>You, the blessed and chosen, I, an exile and an orphan, humbly implore that, standing today in the sight of His throne, you may chant with unanimous voice a hymn and praise to His glory, praising the condescension of the life-giving divinity which has deigned to look upon me, unworthy, in the reception of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Dismissal.
<note>A red paragraph mark</note>O you, number of the elect and all citizens of heaven, chorus of the patriarchs, John the Baptist, precursor of Christ, John the Evangelist, the virgin guardian of Christ, the praiseworthy number of the apostles, the rose-colored army of martyrs, the glorious chorus of priests and confessors
pages.58: and the virgin army of the brides of Christ, and the chastity of widows. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>All you, the beloved and chosen of God, I call upon, and with a suppliant vow I ask of you that you may praise and glorify for me the giver of all good things, our Lord <note>Red letter I</note>Jesus Christ, who, although I am unworthy, fed me with His holy body and gave me His own blood to drink, He who came from heaven and deigned to be incarnate of <note>Red letter M</note>Mary, the glorious Virgin, and here gives life to the world. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Ask also, pious fathers, that, helped by your merits, the sweetness of His most sacred body may come to me and remain in me, and that I may feel no other sweetness of flavor besides that. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>Implore also for me before the glorious Virgin <note>Red letter M</note>Mary, Mother of God, that she may obtain for me in her Son Jesus Christ purity of life, contrition for sins, true confession, and worthy satisfaction, and that after this misery she may associate me with the blessed, He Himself granting it. Who lives and reigns God in the ages of ages. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note>O blessed and benignant and glorious Trinity, Creator and Governess of all, holy and undivided Unity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, of whose exuberant and magnificent glory heaven and earth are full. By the fruit of the Everlasting Begetter, born of the blessed always-Virgin <note>Red letter M</note>Mary, which was consecrated by You, holy Trinity, and by the
pages.59: co-eternal, glorious, and everlasting Begetter Himself, who was crucified for us, deign today to consecrate me, with a pure heart and chaste body, to receive <note>it</note> so that through this sweet nourishment of the most holy body and the drink of His precious blood, all increments of vices may perish in me, and I may deserve to be united to the very fountain of all good things, in which, being absolved and sanctified, I may be able to see and praise happily, forever enjoying Him with the angels, the Lord and Spouse of my soul, the Trinity and one God, for ages of ages. Amen. <note>¶</note> Venerable Trinity and to be admired Unity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, true light and blessed light, incomprehensible to human senses. May You proceed to me, heart born of the Begetter, the nourisher who fills the womb of the Virgin, the holy light shining upon the blind. May it be permitted for me to taste the worthy host, the blessed body of Jesus Christ our Savior, with the palate of the heart and mouth, and to kiss and embrace my most sweet lover out of divine grace with the arms of faith and love. Finally, however, this corruptibility being removed, may I freely embrace my most noble co-heir together with the angels and the choirs of holy virgins, through whom I may know from then on the Trinity and the true Unity, praising perfectly for ages of ages. Amen. <note>¶</note> Follows the jubilus of Saint Bernard.

I aspire with intention, whom I embrace with all my heart, whose body and blood I desire to receive, so that you may always remain in me and not depart from me, O sweetest Father. Amen. ¶ Another prayer before Mass.
<note>A red decorative initial 'O'</note>O most holy flesh or holy communion, Christ's body and blood. Hail, supreme sweetness, which knows no decay, removes disgust, kills death, and provides eternal life. Hail, blessed refreshment, which leads your elect from the exile of this world to the fatherland. Hail, happy host, which was offered on the altar of the cross to God the Father for the weight of our sins. Hail, manna, whiter than snow, sweeter than honey, more precious than any gold. Take away, I beseech you, good Shepherd, the iniquities from me, that having purified body and soul I may deserve to taste the Holy of Holies. And may this venerable sacrament be to me an impregnable protection against hostile snares, so that, refreshed by this salutary food for the journey, I may be able to traverse the slippery paths of this life on an immaculate track and arrive without the impediment of diabolical fraud to you, the living and true bread, the Lord of the angels. Hear me, placate me, Lord, attend, and ensure that I do not die, for by yourself, O Lord, no one will be able to be worthy of such a mystery unless you, the receiver, make them worthy. Amen.
<note>A red decorative initial 'I'</note>Here is another prayer before Mass or holy communion.
O table of your sweetest purity, pious Lord Je
pages.45: su Christ, I, a sinner, presuming nothing from my own merit, but approaching from your great mercy and goodness, fear and tremble. For I have a heart and body stained with many crimes, my mind and tongue not carefully guarded. Therefore, O pious Deity, O tremendous Majesty, I, a miserable one, caught among anxieties, run back to you, the fountain of mercy. I hasten to you to be healed; I flee under your protection, and whom I cannot sustain as Judge, I yearn to have as Savior. To you, Lord, I show my wounds; to you I uncover my shame. I know my sins are many and great, for which I fear. I hope in your mercies, of which there is no number. Look, therefore, upon me with the eyes of your mercy, pious Lord Jesus Christ, King eternal, God-man crucified for humanity. Hear me, hoping in you, and have mercy on me, full of miseries and sins, you who will never cease to flow in the fountain of compassion. Hail, salutary victim, offered for me and for all the human race on the gibbet of the cross. Hail, noble and most precious blood, flowing from the wounds of my crucified Lord Jesus Christ and washing away the sins of the whole world. Remember, Lord, your creature whom you redeemed with your sacred blood. It repents me to have sinned; I desire to amend what I have done. Take away, therefore, from me, most clement Father, all iniquities and sins, so that, purified in mind and body, I may deserve to worthily
pages.46:
partake of the holy things. And grant that this holy libation of your body and blood, which I, unworthy, intend to receive, may be the remission of my sins. May it be the perfect purging of offenses, the driving away of foul thoughts, the reigning of good senses, the salutary efficacy of works pleasing to you, and the strongest protection against the snares of my enemies for my soul and body. Amen.
<note>A red decorative initial 'O'</note>O Lord Jesus Christ, most pious and <note>Another prayer.</note> most merciful. I ask with all my heart that you forgive all my sins in this present life, that you do not afflict me with punishment for them, and that you do not reserve any punishment for purgatory. O God of immense piety, whose strength is infinite, since without you I am unable to resist sins, strengthen me so that I may not commit mortal sin now. And may I overcome every temptation of the devil from now on; may I direct my life, thoughts, words, and works entirely to you; and may you guard me at the end of my life, lest the devil carry me into the throat of hell and thus lead me into despair. O fountain emanating charity, make my mind free from every creature that could attract it to itself and hinder your love, so that I may progress in your love. Now and at the end of my life, may I worthily receive you and thus lead my soul, stripped of the garment of the body, through your mercies to the eternal palace to see clearly the mirror of the Holy Trinity. Amen. <note>Followed by acts of thanksgiving to be said after Mass at one's pleasure.</note>
pages.47:
<note>A red decorative initial 'S' at the beginning of the text.</note>Most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which I, most unworthy, have received, and for the salvation of my soul and body were sacrificed on the cross, I beseech you through the mystery of your admirable sacrament that you save and protect my soul and body from all fraud and illusion of demons. And through this offering which I have offered to you for the praise and glory of your name, may you delete all my sins and not permit me to be deceived or punished by the devil or any creature on account of my sins. But you, most pious God, rebuke and correct me in your mercy, and give me, Lord, faith, hope, charity, humility, patience, obedience, and chastity of mind and body, and the love of you and my neighbor. I also supplicantly ask you through your most holy body which I, unworthy, have received, and the chalice which I have drunk, and that peace which you made between God and man, who offered yourself as a living and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father, that you may strengthen peace and concord among us Christians through that terror which, hanging on the cross, you made formidable to the serpent, the devil, acceptable to friends, and appeased to enemies. And make me enjoy your peace and the peace of the whole Church, both present and future. 

¶ Likewise, I ask you through the communion of your most holy body and blood and through the drops of bloody sweat
pages.48:
for your anguish, your most holy death, and for the merits of the most holy virgin, the exalted mother of our Lord, Saint Mary, and of all the saints and elect, that you deign to deliver the souls of our parents and benefactors and of all the faithful from the lake of hell and from the anguishes of Tartarus, and to place them in the kingdom of eternal clarity. O good Jesus, through your most holy blood and body, free me from all sins and dangers, from sudden death, and proceed with a perfect contrition for all sins, a full confession with the invocation of your holy name, and transfer me into the region of eternal peace. Who with the Father
<note>A red decorative initial 'G'</note>Another prayer after communion.
I give thanks to you, O God. I give thanks, true life of the living, eternal hope of believers, Jesus Christ, kindly redeemer, who alone are to be adored, loved, and praised, who alone perform miracles, who for our sake, to console your poor, whom you have left in this misery like pilgrims and orphans, through the mystery of the priests, through words from your mouth and in your name, you open the heavens and descend and fill the whole earth with a blessing. You who do not disdain to be handled by the hands of man, to be blessed and consecrated for our salvation. You who, by your mystery, show forth the signs of the sacrament on the outside. But you, invisible God, remaining
pages.49:
the same, you are the performer.
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Therefore, to you, our Lord God, great and immense, eternal and exalted, to you be praise, to you be glory, to you be thanksgiving now and forever, because you handed down this very incomprehensible mystery to your disciples with such gratuitous piety at the impending article of your salutary passion. Moved by mercy and paternal affection, you addressed them, saying: I have desired with desire to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. As if you were saying: I have desired with desire to hand myself over to you. 
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Then, bearing yourself wonderfully in your hands, you protested, saying: This is my body. 
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Receive this for your salvation, as often as you receive it in my commemoration and in memory of the love with which I loved you, when I left myself as a pledge of salvation. 
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>O inestimable love of your charity, Lord Jesus Christ, kind One, so that you might reconcile us unworthy ones to your Father, you exhibit yourself as a salutary victim. 
<note>Decorative red paragraph mark</note>Therefore, I supplicantly implore the immense clemency of your mercy that this sacrament of your supreme charity and union may be to me and to all your faithful the most efficacious medicine against the wounds of all our sins and the complement of all virtue and grace; may it be the most valid protection against all evils and the most solid support of eternal beatitude.

I give thanks to you and render praises to you, Lord my God, who deigned to create me from nothing to your image and likeness, and to redeem me with your precious blood, and through the ablution of holy baptism to aggregate me among your adopted children, and to refresh me with the mysteries of the price of your body and blood. Therefore, I render praises and thanks to you, who, from the time of my raw infancy until this hour, through many flowing vices, waited with the patience of your immense piety for my amendment. I praise you, I glorify you, who very often freed me from many tribulations, anxieties, calamities, and miseries. Who hitherto mercifully exempted me from eternal punishments and from the torments of body and soul. I praise you, I glorify you, who mercifully granted me [life] in the health of limbs, the tranquility of times, and the effect of good things, along with many other virtues. I beseech you, Lord God, in your ineffable sweetness, that you may effect in me the benefits and gifts you have begun. And whatever displeases you in me, repel it, and deliver me also from all the tribulations and iniquities and diverse evils with which I am entangled. Order my thoughts, speeches, and acts alike according to your will. Between adversities and
pages.51:
prosperities, guard me always and everywhere, and finally lead me happily to the desired joys of your vision. <note>Red paragraph mark</note> After Mass.
<note>Red decorative initial 'L'</note>These are the first things which are pleasing to you, which you left to us orphans in memory of your love. O Source of Wisdom, born of a Virgin, who did not disdain to have your venerable body touched and received by me, an unworthy sinner. What shall I worthily render to you for all that you have returned? For if the merits of the whole world were gathered into one, they would not be worthy to be compared to your dignity in any way. Therefore, I give thanks to you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, King of kings and Lord of lords. I render thanks to your tremendous majesty and immense piety, O most pious Jesus, to the best of my fragile ability, because you have sweetly refreshed my soul, which was too dry, with your sacred body and blood. I ask you that whatever you find in me that is vicious and contrary to your will, you may root out through the reception of this sacrament and prepare my heart to be a worthy dwelling place for the Holy Spirit. And, sweetest Jesus, may this sacrament of your body and blood be the sweetness and delight of my soul, my health and holiness in every temptation, peace and joy in every tribulation, the light of virtue in every work, and a final protection in death. Amen. <note>Red paragraph mark</note> Prayer after Mass.

pages.52: <note>A decorative red drop cap "S"</note>Most sacred Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, which was sacrificed on the Cross for the salvation of the human race. I, a miserable sinner, wrapped in many sins, humbly implore You that through Your wonderful mystery You may save my soul and body, and protect me from all deception and fraud of the devil and all my enemies. And by the most holy offering that I also have offered today to the praise and glory of Your name, and to the memory of Your divine Passion, and in honor of the most holy Mother of God, the Virgin Mary, and of all the saints, deign to erase all my sins. Do not permit me, most clement Lord, to be punished or captured by the devil or any creature on account of my sins. But You, most pious Lord, who have mercy on all, deign to have mercy on me, and correct me in Your infinite mercy, and not in Your wrath. Grant me, most pious Lord, true faith, firm hope, perfect charity, unfailing patience, and such penance as may please You, my God, so that Your holy angels may rejoice at my conversion. I beseech You, my God, by that peace which You made between God and man, when You offered Yourself as a pure and immaculate host to reconcile the human race to God the Father on the cross, that You may make and confirm peace and concord between me and all faithful Christians. And by that terror which You caused the serpent while hanging on the cross
pages.53: formidable to the devil and acceptable to friends, make me reconciled so that I may enjoy Your peace and that of the whole Church, as well as present and future prosperity. Savior of the world, save us, You who have redeemed us by Your blood and cross. We pray You, help us, our God. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, by the drops of Your bloody sweat, by the anguish of Your most precious death, by the merits and intercession of Your most blessed Mother, the perpetual Virgin Mary, and by the prayers of blessed John the Baptist and all the saints who are pleasing to God, that You may deliver me, Your servant, and also Your servants, and all my parents, benefactors, and those entrusted to me, from all danger of body and soul. And after this life, grant us a perpetual dwelling in the heavenly fatherland. And deliver also, Lord, the souls of Your servants and handmaids, and of my parents and benefactors, and of those entrusted to me, from the lake of hell and from the mire of filth, and place them in the kingdom of peace and eternal clarity. I ask You, most pious Lord, by the most holy presence and libation of Your Body and Blood, that You may deliver me from all my sins, past, present, and future, from necessities and anguishes, and from the snares of all my enemies, visible and invisible. And I ask You, most pious Lord Jesus Christ, that in
pages.54:
the trembling hour of my death, You do not deny me the reception of Your most holy Body and Blood, complete and perfect satisfaction, with the happy assurance of the present life. Amen.

pages.56: which is the heavenly drink, sweet to me above all things. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> Most fine and pious lover and reconciler of the human race, Jesus Christ, the eternal salvation of all who love You, who on account of Your patience permitted me, an unworthy sinner, to receive Your holy Body and Blood with a polluted heart and mouth, which anyone who receives unworthily, receives not as a remedy but unto judgment. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> I beseech You, be merciful to me, a most unworthy sinner. And You who are the true and eternal life, deign through these holy things which I have taken to remit all the iniquity and impiety of my previous life, and to transform the action of my subsequent life into the praise and glory of Your most holy name, so that when I am presented before You to be judged after this life, do not, most clement God, I beseech You, condemn me on account of my innumerable sins, but through this reception of our redemption, avert Your wrath from us, which I confess with grief I have very often provoked by my many negligences and the perpetration of sins. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> O most serene and renowned Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, perpetual Virgin, who were worthy to carry in your most sacred womb the same Creator of all creatures, whose most true Body and Blood I, a miserable and unworthy sinner, have taken, handled, and consumed, I humbly pray for your mercy that you may deign to intercede for me with Him, so that whatever I have committed in His ineffable sacrament through ignorance or negligence, He may deign to forgive me through your most holy prayers, by His ineffable piety and inenarrable mercy. Amen.
pages.57:
<note>A red paragraph mark</note> O all you angelic choirs, angels, archangels, virtues, powers, dominations, principalities, thrones, cherubim, and seraphim, who, inebriated from the abundance of the fountain of the divine Trinity, have received eternal splendor from the light of the eternal Divinity itself, in which you, truly blessed and happy, rejoice assiduously in gladness, loving without satiety, seeing without intermediary, and eating with full mouth that honey-sweet bread of eternal life, which deigned to gladden me, a poor man, today out of His goodness. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> You blessed and elect, I, an exile and an orphan, humbly implore that, standing today in the sight of His throne, you may sing with unanimous voice a hymn and praise to His glory, praising the condescension of the life-giving Divinity which deigned to regard me, an unworthy one, in the reception of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> Dismissal.
<note>A red paragraph mark</note> O you number of the elect and all you heavenly citizens, choir of the patriarchs, John the Baptist, forerunner of Christ, John the Evangelist, the virginal guardian of Christ, the praiseworthy number of the apostles, the roseate army of the martyrs, the glorious choir of priests and confessors
pages.58: and the virginal army of the spouses of Christ, and the chastity of widows. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> I summon all you beloved and elect of God, and I ask you with a suppliant vow that you may praise and glorify the Giver of all good things, our Lord Jesus Christ, for me, because He fed me, although unworthy, with His holy Body and watered me with His own Blood, who came from heaven and willed to be incarnate by the glorious Virgin Mary, giving life to the world here. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> Ask also for me, pious fathers, that assisted by your merits, the sweetness of His most sacred Body may come to me and remain in me, and that I may feel no other sweetness of flavor besides that. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> Implore also for me, with the glorious Virgin Mary, the Mother of God, that she may obtain for me in her Son, Jesus Christ, purity of life, contrition for sins, true confession, and worthy satisfaction, and after this misery, may she associate me with the joys of the blessed, He Himself granting it, who lives and reigns as God forever and ever. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> O blessed and benedicted and glorious Trinity, Creator and Governess of all, holy and undivided Unity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, of whose exuberant and magnificent glory heaven and earth are full. pages.59: in purity of heart and chastity of body for receiving [this sacrament], so that through this sweet nourishment of the most holy Body and the cup of His precious Blood, all the incitements of vices may perish in me, and I may merit to be united to the very fountain of all good things, in which, being absolved and sanctified, I may be able to see and praise with the angels, enjoying them perpetually, the Lord and Spouse of my soul, the Trinity in Unity, forever and ever. the trembling hour of my death, You do not deny me the reception of Your most holy Body and Blood, complete and perfect satisfaction, with the happy assurance of the present life. Amen.

<note>A red decorative initial 'G'</note>I give thanks to Your immense majesty and everlasting piety, Lord holy Father, almighty and eternal God, who, when I was an unworthy servant and a miserable sinner, did not demand my own merits, but deigned to satisfy me with the many and great mercies of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. And I pray that this communion may not be for me guilt unto punishment, but a saving intercession unto forgiveness. May it be for me the armor of faith and the shield of good will. May it be the evacuation of my vices, the extermination of concupiscence and lust, and the augmentation of humility, charity, patience, chastity, obedience, and all virtues, and of all holiness and salvation. May it be a firm defense against the snares of all my enemies, visible and invisible, the perfect calming of my movements, both carnal and spiritual, a firm adhesion to You, the living and true God, and the happy consummation of my end.

X.text:
<note>A red paragraph mark</note>May this, I beseech You, holy Father, the most holy sacrament of the Body and Blood of Your beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, be the sweetness and pleasantness of my soul, its salvation and sanctity in every temptation, peace and joy in every tribulation, light and virtue in every word and work, solace and final protection in death. And I pray that through this I may merit to be filled with Your Holy Spirit, and directed through the way of Your commandments, and that I may be refreshed by this same viaticum at the final moment of my life, and having been refreshed now, may be preserved until then without intermission, and be led by Your holy angels to that place where You Yourself are for Your saints the true light, full satisfaction, consummate joy, perfect happiness, and everlasting gladness. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> We give thanks to You for all the beatified, asking to be helped by their intercession. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> But for those who are in the places of purgatory, the Son offers Himself to You, Father, in supplication that through this most holy host their pain may be lighter and shorter. <note>A red paragraph mark</note> But for us who are still burdened by the sins of flesh and blood, the Son offers Himself to You in supplication that the blood of Your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, may wash away the sins we have contracted from flesh and blood, and that His flesh may cleanse us. Amen.
