Sweet memory of Jesus, giving true joys of the heart. But above honey and all things is His sweet presence. Nothing is sung more sweetly, nothing heard more pleasantly, nothing thought more sweetly than Jesus, the Son of God.
Jesus, sweetness of hearts, living fountain, light of the mind, exceeding every joy and every desire.
Jesus, hope for the penitent, how kind You are to those who ask, how good to those who seek, but what are You to those who find?
Neither tongue is able to say, nor letter to express; the experienced person knows how to discern what it is to love Jesus.
I will seek Jesus in my bed, in the closed chamber of my heart, privately and in public I will seek Him with diligent love.
With Mary at dawn, I will seek Jesus in the tomb; with the complaining cry of my heart, I will seek Him with the mind, not the eye.
At the tomb, I will pour out tears, I will fill the place with groans; I will kiss the feet of Jesus, and embrace Him with goodly arms.
Jesus, You are a lovable King, an ineffable sweetness, and a noble victor, entirely desirable.
Stay with us, Lord, stay with the new light; dispel the darkness of night, filling the mind with sweetness.
Jesus, most sweet love and truly most pleasant, a thousand times more grateful than we are sufficient to say.
Recognize, you who have experienced it, ask for the love of the pious, seek Jesus ardently; in seeking, become inflamed.
Jesus, author of clemency, hope of all joy, <unclear>sweet</unclear>
pages.61:
fountain of the heart and grace, true delight of the heart.
Since I am not able to speak worthily of You, yet I would not be silent; love makes me dare, since I rejoice of You alone.
Your love, Jesus, is a grateful refreshment of the mind; You fill without disgust, giving desire to the hungry.
Those who taste You hunger; those who drink still thirst; they are unable to desire anything except Jesus, whom they love.
He whom Your love intoxicates knows what Jesus tastes like; a happy taste that satisfies, there is nothing more that he could desire.
Jesus, angelic beauty, a sweet song to the ear; in the mouth, marvelous honey; in the heart, celestial nectar.
I desire You a thousand times; my Jesus, when will You come to me? When will You make me joyful of You? When will You satisfy me?
Your continuous love is for me an assiduous longing; Jesus, most honey-sweet, fruit of eternal life.
Jesus, highest kindness, wonderful joy of the heart, incomprehensible goodness; Your charity binds me.
It is good for me to love Jesus, to seek nothing beyond, and to completely fail, so that I may be able to live for Him.
O my most sweet Jesus, hope of the sighing soul; pious tears and the cry of my heart seek You inwardly.
In whatever place I may be, I desire Jesus with me; how happy when I find Him, how blissful when I hold Him.
Then embraces, then kisses, which surpass cups of honey; through these, let there be no delay, may I follow Jesus through the ages.
pages.62:
Now I see what I sought; I hold what I longed for; I languish with the love of Jesus and am entirely burning in my heart.
Say, love burns constantly, it sweetens wonderfully, it purifies delightfully, it delights and makes happy.
Say, love sent from heaven, clings to my marrow; it inflames the mind deeply; here the spirit is delighted.
O blessed burning, o ardent desire, o sweet refreshment, to love the Son of God.
When Jesus is thus loved, this love is not extinguished, nor does it grow tepid, nor does it die, but rather grows as it approaches.
Jesus, flower of the Virgin Mother, love of our sweetness, to You be praise, honor of the divinity, kingdom of beatitude.
Come, come, best King, Father of immense glory, and shine clearly more joyfully, now expected very often.
Jesus, more serene than the sun, and sweeter than balsam, sweeter than all sweetness, more lovable than all things.
By whom love is so affected, and whose fragrance so refreshes me, in whom my mind fails, He alone suffices for the lover.
You are the delight of the mind, the plumage of love, You are my glorification, Jesus, salvation of the world.
My beloved, return, partner of the paternal right hand; You have conquered the enemy quickly; now enjoy the kingdom of heaven.
I will follow wherever You go, I cannot be taken away when You have taken my heart, Jesus, praise of our race.
Citizens of heaven, come forward, lift up your gates.
pages.63:
Say to the victor, hail Jesus, illustrious King.
King of virtues, King of glory, King of signal victory, Jesus, bestower of grace, honor of the celestial court.
The chorus of heaven proclaims You and repeats Your praises; Jesus makes the world joyful and reconciles us to God.
Jesus commands in peace and overcomes every sense; my mind desires this and hastens to enjoy Him.
Jesus has returned to the Father, He has entered the celestial kingdom; my heart has departed from me, and at the same time has gone after Him.

And first, for Sunday.

<note>A red decorative initial 'R' begins the prayer.</note>
I beseech You, Jesus Christ, Son of God, through the glory of Your most holy passion, that today You may introduce my soul into the cell of Your most sweet love. And casting out all impediments, make me persist in the joy and silence of mutual union, so that with full charity I may be able to enjoy the sweetness of Your desired consolation. Come, most faithful Father of orphans; come, most sweet consoler of all the miserable; provide me such a drink from the cellars of Your wounds, through which all my inward parts may feel You to be immediately
pages.64: the possessor of all my faults. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through Your precious blood which You voluntarily shed on the cross in Your passion, that today You may pour into my heart and my soul Your holy blessing. And make me receive Your most holy body and Your most precious blood with such devotion, that I may merit to rejoice eternally in the contemplation of Your most sweet face. Come, fountain of mercy; come, best consoler; cleanse the dwelling of my soul, for it is not fitting that there should be any filth there where You are to reign, King and Spouse of virginal modesty. Daughters of Jerusalem, announce to the Beloved that I now promise the amendment of all my sins; I desire with my whole heart to amend their perpetration, for without Him I neither wish nor am able to live. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through Your five wounds, that today You may deign to wash and whiten my soul in the wave of Your most holy blood, so that, although I am not worthy to be called one of Your least, You are nonetheless so powerful and so merciful that You may be able to inscribe me among Your dear ones and beloved. Come, faithful friend of friends; come, sweet purifier of penitent sinners. Make my soul feast in the breaches of Your wounds and limbs, so that I may eternally merit to see and rejoice in the sight of Your eyes. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ,
pages.65: through the most holy scars of Your body, that You may come quickly and break the chains of all my sins, and extinguish my vices today so that not even a spark of any offense may be able to be cast against me at my end by diabolical malice. Come, medicine of souls; come, pool of all graces. And just as in the paschal night You led Your captives out from the places of punishment, so free my soul today from the chains and knots of all miseries. Daughters of Jerusalem, announce to the Beloved that I am now preparing the bridal chamber of my heart, and that without Him I neither wish nor am able to live. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through the passion of Your most holy body, that today You may place the candle of Your most sweet body upon the candlestick of my soul, so that it may ignite the flame of Your most holy blood, so that just as once with Your most holy hands You did not disdain to touch and heal the most filthy leprosy, so do not cease to anoint and heal the wounds of my soul with all Your virtues and limbs. Come, refuge of the poor; come, my only salvation, and perfect in me the desire of the heart; for I can joyfully show You the bitterness of my wounds, since You Yourself felt and endured the pain and bitterness of wounds. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through the glory of Your passion, that You may ignite in my heart the fire of Your love, and do not allow me to separate
pages.66: from the joy of Your contemplation, for You prefer the life rather than the death of the sinner. Come, glory of the world; come, joy of the heavens; for the door of my heart is open to You. Behold, all my inward parts expect and desire You, because my whole salvation and life hangs on Your mercy. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through the wounds which You bore in Your most holy hands, that today You may deign to cleanse my soul from the filth of all vices, and deign to sprinkle it with the flowers and leaves of all virtues, so that You, King of kings, entering into it, may feel such a scent that it may eternally bloom in Your joys and desires. Come, Sun of Justice; come, morning star; illuminate the darkness of my soul, You who alone can remake the just and holy from sin, because for You nothing is impossible, since even all those mourning for You can be saved, and hoping in You, they do not wish to abandon You. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through the wounds and through the footprints of Your feet, that as I open my heart today to sigh, You may open the paradise of Your most joyful heart and heaven to me, and make my soul thus enter into You, the most sweet Jesus, so that it may flourish and grow and remain in Your most sweet love now and forever. Come, illuminator of hearts, and illuminate my soul; come and restore all Your grace to me, so that I may be able to recount securely my misery
pages.67: You who do not love me less than Your flesh and Your own soul. Daughters of Jerusalem, announce to the Beloved that I languish with His love and without Him I neither wish nor am able to live. I beseech You, Lord Jesus Christ, through the wound of Your most holy side, that today You may place in my heart the ladder of Your most precious blood and body, and make my soul ascend through it with the holy angels, so that it may be able to find and seek Your mercy in the individual joints of Your limbs. Come, ray of the eternal sun; come, my Redeemer, and free me from all my tribulations. Sweet is the memory of Jesus, giving true joys to the heart. But sweeter than honey and all things is His sweet presence. Nothing is sung more sweetly, nothing is heard more joyfully, nothing is thought more sweetly than Jesus, the Son of God.
Jesus, sweetness of hearts, living fountain, light of the mind, exceeding all joy and all desire.
Jesus, hope for the penitent, how kind You are to those who ask, how good to those who seek, but what are You to those who find!
Neither can the tongue speak, nor the letter express; only one who has experienced it knows how to discern what it is to love Jesus.
I will seek Jesus in my bed, in the closed chamber of my heart; in private and in public, I will seek Him with diligent love.
At dawn, with Mary, I will seek Jesus in the tomb; with the complaining cry of my heart, I will seek Him with my mind, not my eye.
I will pour out tears at the tomb, I will fill the place with groans; I will touch the feet of Jesus, I will embrace Him with goodly embraces.
Jesus, You are a lovable King, an ineffable sweetness, and a noble victor, entirely desirable.
Stay with us, Lord, with the new light, driving away the darkness of the night, filling the mind with sweetness.
Jesus, most sweet love and truly most pleasant, a thousand times more grateful than we are able to say.
You who have experienced it, acknowledge it; ask for the love of the pious; seek Jesus ardently; in seeking, be set aflame.
Jesus, author of clemency, hope of all joy, <unclear>sweet</unclear>

In whatever place I may be, I desire Jesus with me; how happy when I find Him, how blissful when I hold Him.
Then the embraces, then the kisses which surpass cups of honey; through these, little by little, I follow Jesus through the ages.

Behold, the time is now that you crown my soul with the ornaments of virtues, which today will celebrate the festivals of joy in your wounds and in your limbs. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by your most bitter tears which you shed for my salvation, that you may today make me approach you with all the devotion and charity that your eternal affection craved in your eternal desire. And wrap your most satisfying body, which you took on for me from the virginal womb, in the shroud of my soul; wash my soul in your blood and extinguish all the sins that you lamented most bitterly upon the cross. Come, chosen one from among thousands; come, beauty and adornment and honor of the paternal glory, who are for me, beyond all, propitious and first. For it is not fitting that you should withdraw your consolation from me for too long, because my soul, which you love, is attacked by the arts of the demons, and therefore desires your advent with all its heart. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by all the sorrows and afflictions that you sustained in your goodness for thirty-three years, that you may deign to weigh my manifold misery in the scales of your ineffable mercy. And as much as you see by your goodness that my malice exceeds in measure and gravity, so much deign to magnify your ineffable glory and mercy in me, a miserable sinner. Come, planter of virtues.
pages.69: come, restorer of all health and sweetness. Behold, my soul, which you love, is infirm and cannot be healed unless you are its faithful physician, whom it seeks and demands with all desire, because it cannot bear the delay of your coming any longer. Daughters of Jerusalem, announce to the beloved that I desire greatly that He visit my soul with the discourse of His own mouth, because without Him I neither wish nor am able to live. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by your paschal victory, that just as you, hanging on the cross, kept no drop of blood in yourself, so today you may not permit any stain of sin to remain in me. And make me receive your precious body and blood in such a way that through it I may deserve to progress from grace to grace, so that in your vision I may deserve to ascend from glory to glory. Come, true salvation of the world; come, Son of the Virgin and crown of virgins. Place your paternal and holy hands upon my languishing soul. For who can feel so paternally and mercifully for me, or who is so prepared for all my salvation as you, who were inebriated with all bitterness for my sake? Therefore, my miserable soul desires greatly to kiss you with the most sweet kiss of your mouth. I beseech you, most sweet Lord Jesus Christ, by your glorious resurrection, that today you may extinguish in my heart all
pages.70: harmful and evil affection. And do not allow me any earthly consolation here, so that in your most sweet love I may have full joy and assiduous affection here. Come, arrow of love; come, praise and glory of the heavenly palace; come, in whose inward parts my memory is inscribed. Who will worthily or more faithfully blot out all my offenses than you, to whom alone my soul is entrusted? Therefore, my soul desires with all its heart that it may have discourse with the most sweet mouth of your own person. O lovable Jesus; O most praiseworthy of all praise; O honey-sweet joy; O irrigation of the heart’s love, make me enjoy your sweetness, O Jesus, here and in eternal beatitude, for infinite ages of ages. Amen. <note>A small red paragraph mark is visible.</note> Prayer after the Mass. <note>A large red decorative initial B is visible.</note> Blessed are you, most powerful Lord Jesus Christ, King of eternal glory, promiser and bestower of everlasting beatitude, who brought me forth from my mother’s womb with whole limbs and senses, and today have poured new and singular grace into all the limbs and wounds of your most holy body, in sweetness and abundance. Blessed are you, most holy God, who created me in your own image and likeness, adorned me with all virtues, and today have illustrated me with the beauty of your image through your body and blood, and have made all your virtues shine forth and be reformed in me in a wonderful way. Blessed are you, most clement God, who in the laver of baptism
pages.71: willed to betroth me to yourself as a heavenly bridegroom, and today have brought forth your body and blood as a gift of a new betrothal and a consumption of your lawful love. Blessed are you, most generous God, who from my infancy even to this hour have brought me innumerable benefits and inexplicable gifts, and today have handed over your body and blood to me for the augmentation and consolation of all your gifts and benefits. Blessed are you, most mild God, who in all my infidelity and in all my sins, by patiently tolerating, have extended my life even to this hour, and in this most happy hour, through your body and blood, have consigned all my sins to perpetual oblivion, and have happily inscribed me in the memory of your most happy heart and in all the inward parts of your mercy. Blessed are you, most noble God, who have guarded me from many sins and miseries, and have mercifully freed me from those into which I had fallen, and today, through your body and blood, have mercifully converted all my damnation into salvation. Blessed are you, most bountiful God, who have led me out from the vanity of the world and from the consolation of all my parents, and today have satisfied me through your body and blood and mercifully joined me to the friendship of your saints. Blessed are you, most pious God, who in all my temptation and tribulation
pages.72: <sig>E</sig> have always stood by me with pious consolation, and have shown and offered all my desires and all my labors to your Father in your wounds, and have satisfied me with your holy body and blood in your mercy. And what reward and consolation you have prepared and acquired for me. May your most clement, most pious, most merciful, and most sweet Mother, the Virgin Mary, bless you, who brought to me today, for my eternal remedy, the same body and blood which you received from her virginal womb; and through it you have made me a fellow-citizen of all your saints. May all your angels, archangels, thrones, principalities, dominations, powers, virtues, cherubim, seraphim, and all your saints bless you, who have made a new joy and a sweet banquet for them out of my salvation. And today you have granted to my desire, with all your faithfulness, yourself, the mirror of eternal life, in which all the saints desire to gaze at every hour. May all your holy patriarchs and prophets bless you, who, as the Creator of heaven and earth, willed to find rest today in the anguish of my heart, and have poured out the dew of your most generous blessing abundantly over all my interior parts. May all your holy apostles and evangelists bless you, who today willed to dine with my soul, and have arranged to make a sweet mansion with me and to remain with me until the end of my life. May all your holy martyrs and confessors bless you, who
pages.73: today received my miserable soul into the embrace of your paternal mercy, and brought and restored to me the robe, the ring, and all the ornaments of virtues from your mercy. <note>The red symbol represents the abbreviation for "Benedicat"</note> May all your holy virgins bless you, who willed to plant your virginal body in my soul like a rose, and willed and made it to pluck and gather the flowers of virtues and the fruits of graces from your limbs and wounds. May the multitude of those mourning, widows, and penitents bless you, who, as the most benign physician of those who languish, entered the hospice of my heart with all your mercy. And today, by piercing all the wounds of my soul with the medicament of your body and blood, you have restored them to your eternal salvation. May the heavens and all the praise and jubilation of the heavens bless you, who today opened the heavens of your wounds to my miserable soul and introduced it into yourself, the true paradise of everlasting joy and happiness. May the earth and the fullness of the earth bless you, who today made me an angel from a human, a heavenly being from an earthly one; truly you alone have deigned to honor me and to show mercy to me, because you have redeemed me with your most precious blood. May the sea and all that is in it bless you, who have made me a participant in the virtue of your graces and all your goods, and who now are able or wish to abandon me, because you have indivisibly connected me to yourself today with the bond of your body and blood and all good
pages.74: <sig>E2</sig> things you confer upon me and have announced. Behold, my soul is today joined to the virginal flower of your love. Blessed are you, most mild God, who in all my infidelity and in all my sins, by patiently tolerating, have extended my life even to this hour, and in this most happy hour, through your body and blood, have consigned all my sins to perpetual oblivion, and have happily inscribed me in the memory of your most happy heart and in all the inward parts of your mercy. Blessed are you, most noble God, who have guarded me from many sins and miseries, and have mercifully freed me from those into which I had fallen, and today, through your body and blood, have mercifully converted all my damnation into salvation. Blessed are you, most bountiful God, who have led me out from the vanity of the world and from the consolation of all my parents, and today have satisfied me through your body and blood and mercifully joined me to the friendship of your saints. Blessed are you, most pious God, who in all my temptation and tribulation

pages.68: ...nor do you reject or despise those hoping in you. Behold, the time is now that you should crown my soul with the ornaments of virtue, which will celebrate today the feasts of joy in your wounds and in your limbs. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by your most bitter tears, which were shed for my salvation, that you may make me today draw near to you with all the devotion and charity that your eternal affection has thirsted for in your eternal desire. And wrap your most satisfying body, which you assumed for me from the virginal womb, in the shroud of my soul, and wash my soul in your blood, and extinguish all sins that you lamented most bitterly upon the cross. Come, elect one out of thousands; come, ornament, beauty, and honor of the Father’s glory, who are propitious and first to me beyond all others. For it is not fitting that you should withdraw your consolation from me for long, because my soul, which you love, is assailed by the arts of demons. Therefore, it desires your arrival with its whole heart. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by all the sorrows and afflictions that you sustained in your goodness for thirty-three years, that you may deign to weigh my manifold misery in the balance of your ineffable mercy. And as much as you see, in your goodness, that my malice exceeds in measure and gravity, so much may you deign to magnify your ineffable glory and mercy in me, a miserable sinner. Come, sower of virtues,
pages.69: replenisher of all salvation and sweetness. Behold, my soul, which you love, grows weak and cannot find health unless you are its faithful physician, whom it seeks and demands with all its desire, because it cannot bear the delay of your arrival any longer. Daughters of Jerusalem, announce to the beloved that I desire much to satisfy my soul with the conversation of your own mouth, because without him I neither wish nor am able to live. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, by your Paschal victory, that just as you, hanging on the cross, held back no drop of blood in yourself, so today you may not permit any stain of sin to remain in me. And make me receive your precious body and blood so that through it I may deserve to advance from grace to grace, so that in your vision I may deserve to ascend from glory to glory. Come, true salvation of the world; come, son of the virgin and crown of virgins. Place your paternal and holy hands upon my languishing soul. For who can feel for me so paternally and mercifully, or who is so prepared for my entire salvation as you, who were intoxicated with all bitterness for my sake? Therefore, my miserable soul desires much to kiss you with the sweetest kiss of your mouth. I beseech you, Lord Jesus Christ, most sweet, by your glorious resurrection, that today you may extinguish in my heart all
pages.70: harmful and evil love. And do not allow me any earthly consolation here, so that in your most sweet love I may find full joy and assiduous affection here. Come, arrow of love; come, praise and glory of the heavenly palace; come, in whose viscera my memory is inscribed. Who will worthily or more faithfully blot out all my offenses than you, to whom alone my soul is abandoned? Therefore, with my whole heart, my soul desires that it may be satisfied with the most sweet conversation of your own mouth. O most lovable Jesus; O most praiseworthy of praise; O mellifluous joy; O irrigating love of the heart: make me enjoy your sweetness, Jesus, here and in eternal beatitude, for infinite ages of ages. May your most clement, most pious, most merciful, and most sweet mother, the Virgin Mary, bless you, who contributed to me today the very body and blood that you received from her virginal womb as an eternal remedy, and through it made me a relative and fellow citizen of all your saints. May all your angels, archangels, thrones, principalities, dominations, powers, virtues, cherubim, seraphim, and all your saints, for whom you have made a new joy and sweet banquet out of my salvation, bless you. And you, the mirror of eternal life, in whom at every hour all the saints desire to look with all faithfulness, have today given yourself to my desire. May all your holy patriarchs and prophets bless you, for you, the Creator of heaven and earth, have willed to rest in the anguish of my heart today, and have abundantly poured all the interior parts of my soul with the dew of your most generous blessing. May all your holy apostles and evangelists bless you, for you willed to dine with my soul today, and have disposed yourself to remain with me, making a sweet mansion with me until the end of my life. pages.73: you received my miserable soul into the embrace of your paternal mercy today, and brought and returned to me the robe, the ring, and all the ornaments of virtues out of your mercy. <note>The red symbol represents the abbreviation for "Benedicat"</note> May all your holy virgins bless you, for you willed to plant your virginal body like a rose in my soul, and you willed and caused me to pick and gather the flowers of virtues and the fruits of graces from your limbs and wounds. May the multitude of those continuing in widowhood and penitence bless you, for you, the most benign physician of the languishing, entered the hospice of my heart with all your mercy. And today, by pricking, you have restored all the wounds of my soul to your eternal salvation with the medicine of your body and blood. May the heavens and all the praise and jubilation of the heavens bless you, for today you opened the heavens of your wounds to my miserable soul and introduced it into yourself, the true paradise of everlasting joy and happiness. May the earth and the fullness of the earth bless you, for today you made me an angel from a human, heaven from earth, and you alone deigned to honor me and to have mercy on me, because you redeemed me with your most precious blood. May the sea and all that is in it bless you, for you have made me a participant in the virtue of graces and all goods in you, and because you can or wish to abandon me now, because you have indivisibly connected me to yourself today with the bond of your body and blood, and you confer and have announced all goods to me.
pages.74: Behold, my soul is today united to the virginal flower of your love in the bridal chamber. I beseech you by your five wounds, by your blood, by your sweat, by your anguish, by your tears, by all the afflictions and sorrows of your heart and body, by your holy passion and your most bitter death, that you may overflow and replenish my soul and all my viscera with your blessing and your most sweet love, and by remaining with me until the end of my life, preserve that grace and that cleanliness which your incomprehensible goodness has brought and restored to me. Be the pious and faithful guard and most strong protection of the good angels, so that the enemies of all good things may be put to flight and depart by the virtue of such a mystery. And by the hand of your holy angel, repel from me and from all your servants the most dire spirit of pride and vainglory, of envy and blasphemy, of fornication and impurity, of doubt and diffidence. Let those who persecute us be confounded; let those who hasten to destroy all things perish. O King of virtues, lover of chastity and integrity, O God, extinguish in my heart with the heavenly dew of your blessing all the tinder of burning lust, so that the tenor of total chastity of soul and body may remain in me. Mortify in my members the goads of the flesh and all lustful commotions, and give me true and perpetual chastity with your other gifts that are pleasing to you in truth, so that I may be able to offer to you the sacrifice of praise with a chaste body and a clean heart. For with such contrition of heart and fountain of tears, with such reverence and trembling, with such bodily chastity and purity of soul, must this divine and heavenly sacrifice be celebrated, O Lord, where your flesh is truly taken and your blood is truly drunk, where the lowest are joined to the highest, where the presence of the holy angels is at hand, where you are both the sacrifice and the priest, in a way wondrous and ineffable. Who is worthy to celebrate
pages.77: it unless you, O almighty God, make the one offering it worthy? I know, O Lord, and I truly know and confess this same thing to your goodness, that I am not worthy to approach such a mystery on account of my excessive sins and my infinite negligences. But I know and truthfully believe with my whole heart, and confess with my mouth, that you can make me worthy, you who alone can make clean from unclean, accepted from seed, alone can make the worthy from the unworthy, the clean from the unclean, the just and the holy from sinners. Because of this your omnipotence, I ask you, grant me, a sinner, to celebrate this heavenly sacrifice with fear and trembling, with purity of heart and a fountain of tears, with spiritual gladness and heavenly joy. May my soul feel the sweetness of your most blessed presence, and the watch of your holy angels in my circuit. For I, mindful of your venerable passion, approach your altar, although a sinner, so that I may offer to you the sacrifice which you instituted and commanded to be offered in commemoration of you, for our salvation. Receive it therefore, I beseech you, most holy God, for your holy Church and for your people whom you redeemed with your blood. And since you willed me, a sinner, to be a medium between you and that people of yours, although you do not recognize in me a witness of good works,
pages.78: do not refuse the office of the stewardship entrusted to me, nor let the price of their salvation be lost through me, an unworthy one, for whom you deigned to become a saving victim and redemption. Therefore, O Lord, if you deign to look upon them propitiously, I bring forward the tribulations of the peoples, the dangers of nations, the groaning of captives, the miseries of orphans, the necessities of pilgrims, the poverty of the weak, the despair of the languishing, the failures of the old, the sighs of the young, the vows of virgins, the laments of widows. For you have mercy on all, O Lord, and you hate nothing of those things which you have made. Be the pious and faithful guard and strongest protection of the good angels, so that the enemies of all good things may be scattered and depart through the virtue of such a mystery. O King of virtues, lover of chastity and integrity, God, extinguish in my heart with the heavenly dew of your blessing all the tinder of burning lust, so that the tenor of total chastity of soul and body may remain in me. Mortify in my members the goads of the flesh and all lustful commotions, and give me true and perpetual chastity with your other gifts that are pleasing to you in truth, so that I may be able to offer to you a sacrifice of praise with a chaste body and a clean heart. Where your flesh is truly taken, and your blood is truly drunk; where the lowest are joined to the highest; where the presence of the holy angels is present; where you are sacrifice and priest in a wonderful and ineffable way. <note>A large red decorative initial 'E'.</note> Now I pray, O most sweet God, that this most sweet sacrament may be for me the most effective medicine for all my sins. May this most sweet sacrament be for me, O most dear God, the most virtuous completion of all virtue and grace. May this most suave sacrament be for me, O most benign God, both in life and in death, the most valid sustenance against all dangers. My Lord God, I beseech you through the Holy Eucharist that, cleansed from sins
pages.82:
and enriched by merits, and perfected by a good end, I may be blessed with you forever. I beseech you, most benign God, for all sinners, that through the repairing virtue of this sacrament you may repair and confirm them to eternal salvation. Item, another prayer before Mass

O Lord my God, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but trusting in your piety and clemency, I approach the sacrament of the body and blood of your only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. I approach, I say, as an invalid to the physician of life, as one unclean to the fountain of mercy, as one blind to the light of eternal clarity, as one needy to the Lord of heaven and earth, as one naked to the King of glory, as one poor to the Shepherd, as a creature to its Creator, as one desolate to the pious consoler, as a culprit to the mediator of God and men, as a wretched one to the compassionate, as one full of crimes to the dispenser of indulgence, as one dead to the vivifier, as one impious to the justifier, as one hardened to the infuser of grace. Asking the abundance of your immense majesty, that you may deign to heal my infirmity, to wash away my filth, to illuminate my blindness, to enrich my poverty, to clothe my nakedness, to lead back the wanderer, to console the desolate, to reconcile the culprit, to give mercy to the wretched, indulgence to the criminal, life to the dead, justification to the impious, the anointing of grace to the hardened, so that I may deserve to treat and receive you, the bread of angels, King of kings, and Lord of lords, with such purity of body and purity of mind, with such contrition of heart and fountain of tears, with such spiritual joy and

N.text: do not refuse the office of the stewardship entrusted to me. Nor may the price of their salvation perish through me, an unworthy one, for whom you deigned to become the saving victim and redemption. Therefore, I put forth, O Lord, if you deign to look upon it with favor, the tribulations of the communities, the dangers of the peoples, the groans of the captives, the miseries of the orphans, the needs of the pilgrims, the poverty of the weak, the despair of the languishing, the failures of the old, the sighs of the young, the vows of the virgins, the laments of the widows. For you have mercy on all, O Lord, and you hate nothing of those things which you have made. Remember what our substance is, how weak, how fragile, how mutable, how susceptible, and infirm, because you are our Father, you are our God. Do not be angry enough, nor withhold the multitude of your mercies over us. For we do not cast our prayers before your face trusting in our justifications, but in your many mercies. Take away from us, O Lord, all our iniquities, and mercifully kindle in us the fire of the Holy Spirit. Take away the heart of stone from our flesh, and give us a heart of flesh which fears you, loves you, delights in you, follows you, and enjoys you eternally.

We pray, O Lord, that you may deign to look with a serene countenance upon your family, awaiting the offices of your sacred name. And so that no one's vow may be ineffectual, and no one's supplication empty, do you yourself deign to hear and graciously answer the prayers you suggest to us. We also ask you, Holy Father, for the souls of all the faithful departed, that this great sacrament of piety may be for them salvation, health, joy, and refreshment. May it be for them today, my God, a great and full refreshment from you, the living bread, who descended from heaven and give life to the world, from your holy and blessed flesh, the Lamb, namely, who is immaculate and takes away the sins of the world, which was assumed from the holy and glorious womb of the Blessed Virgin Mary and conceived of the Holy Spirit. From that fountain of piety, I say, which through the soldier's lance happily flowed from your most holy side, so that from it, healed, refreshed, satisfied, and consoled, they may exult in your praise and glory. I ask your clemency, O God, that the fullness of your blessing and the sanctification of your divinity may descend upon it. May that incomprehensible and invisible majesty of your Holy Spirit also descend, Lord, just as it once descended upon the offerings of the fathers, and may it make our oblations your body and blood, and teach me, your unworthy priest, to treat such a mystery with purity of heart.

Likewise, do not repel me, miserable one, because of my innumerable crimes, from the communion of such a mystery as if I were unworthy. But grant me compunction of heart and a fountain of tears to wash away my sins, and crimes, and offenses, so that with a clean heart and pure conscience I may merit to receive your body and blood, for the remedy of my soul, for the remission of all my sins, for the winning of eternal life, and for the happy possession of it with your saints, and to be filled with your Holy Spirit and always restored by divine affections. loving and most mild God, grant me, I pray, not only to receive the sacrament of your body and blood, but also the virtue of the sacrament. Grant that I may receive your body, which you drew from the Virgin, in such a way that I may merit to be incorporated into your mystical body and counted among its members. <note>Decorative initial "I"</note>I humbly implore your ineffable mercy, Lord Jesus Christ, that this sacrament of your body and blood, which I have received unworthily, may be for me a purging of crimes, a strength for the fragile, a firmament against the perils of the world, an obtaining of pardon, a stabilizing of grace, a medicine of life, a memorial of your passion, a remedy against the weakness of the flesh <note>original: "fomitis"</note>, a viaticum <gloss>provision for a journey</gloss> for my pilgrimage. Let it conduct me going, lead me back wandering, receive me returning, hold me staggering, raise me falling, and bring me persevering into glory. O most high God, may the most blessed presence of your
pages.86:
body and blood so change the palate of my heart, that it may never feel any sweetness besides you, love no beauty, seek no illicit love, desire no consolation, admit no delight, care for no honor, and fear no cruelty.

I adore you devoutly, hidden deity, who truly lie concealed under these figures. To you my heart subjects itself entirely, because contemplating you, it fails entirely. O pious Jesus, whom I now see veiled, when will that happen which I so thirst for, that seeing you with unveiled face, I may be blessed by the sight of your glory? Amen.

<note>A large red decorative initial L begins the text.</note>Your letters have filled me with incredible pleasure. For I have never been inflamed with such great zeal for divine matters as I have since I read your letter, in which you commend religion and place it in such a position that it ought to be preferred above all things. I also, indeed, used to think not moderately of divine worship, and I praised above all others those who, putting all else aside, gave themselves entirely to it from the heart; yet such wonder for this matter did not hold me that I professed to desire it. But now, I do not merely desire it, but I am already beginning to be so drawn to it that there can be nothing in life that is sufficient to distract me from it without it. I desire, therefore, to be joined to you as a companion and partner. Formerly, there was another reason and plan for life, when there was a wife, children, and parents. And my mind was never set on these things; nor, had it been, would it have been permitted while preserving piety. But now, when I am deprived by death of almost all those necessary people, and I have lost those whom it helped to endure all troubles, even if I know them, you will surely yield to me. I hope to be with you shortly. In the meantime, I shall arrange my affairs, as they say, and since I am freer and more unencumbered for that kind of life which I embrace with the greatest heart, I will extricate myself from these impediments that have hitherto kept me conquered, so that there will be no greater care for me than that I should care for nothing but divine things. Farewell.

<note>A large red decorative initial Q begins the text.</note>What is it that I have contended with such great zeal at any time that I should not demand this from you again and again, that for the sake of our friendship you read most attentively those things about which I write to you this day? Often, as you know, I have warned you,
pages.74:
that you should not neglect your own judgment, and that you should look out for yourself in the future. But you have carried yourself with negligence thus far. Yet, do not be overconfident; I see that danger is not far from you. For Claudius, an old friend of your family, and one who was most familiar with your father while he lived, told me about you. For he says that you use neither modest expenses nor honorable men, and that you are surrounded by the deceit and snares of those who live with you, and whose counsel you use in all matters. They have deliberately suborned L. Sulla, a wealthy man, and one who has much power in your city. He, at their instigation, will bring a lawsuit against you concerning your property. They will indeed cast a doubt upon you, and they will persuade you to surrender the records of your property to their trust, so that they may more freely and easily manage your case, that is, to plunder and rob you of your goods. If this is done by you, I clearly see that you will be excluded. Therefore, if you love me, or rather if you hold yourself dear, do not entrust yourself to such men, whose entire speech is smooth, but whose actions are full of snares, or are far removed from their speech. I am forced to be anxious for your safety and all your fortunes, which I would not do, were I not to hold you in the highest regard. You should grant me this, that you do not bear less care for yourself than those who greatly desire that you be safe and your affairs intact. Farewell.

As for your mind and piety toward your parents and relatives, I never thought it was to be doubted. But since your piety is not equally known to all men, it easily happens that some, through envy, others through error, and some through the custom of disparaging what should be praised, might invent or believe something about you. But even if the matter has been steered by some fault of yours, and even if I judge you to be an excellent person, that is still something to be considered most carefully. For it could happen that even good men might not have a good opinion of you if you use the money left by your parents poorly. Therefore, it must be provided for again and again that you are not more splendid in your attire, or more extravagant in your household and other matters, than either the custom of your ancestors, or the dignity of your elders, or the means themselves warrant. For we see that such rumors often attach to men who lack fame, and who acquire more enemies than friends. For there are some in the city whose hearts ache that the goods that were for the help of the republic, and for the needs of friends, by the industry and labor of excellent citizens, should be consumed by the rashness and intemperance of youths. I do not think these vices are in you, but I mention them to you so that you may be more honorable in your whole life and abhor more deeply every immoderate expense and all society of those who are the ruin of all wealthy youths. As far as my zeal or diligence can achieve, I will take care of your reputation, if I hear that anything unworthy is reported about you. You, however, take care that, while I have praised my own duty, you yourself do not diminish it in the estimation of men by some good deed. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial Q.</note> How much I cherish all my relatives from the heart, you will easily understand if you consider my efforts on their behalf. For each person holds their own dear, and I do not think there is anyone among those I know who pursues their own with greater benevolence than I do mine. I cannot sufficiently admire what some men can think of me, whom neither previous services to my own nor kindnesses could move, who go around slandering me. But words (as I see) are useless for other things to them. They want to be busy, and they prefer to slander rather than speak well. I have, however, in this grief and annoyance one great relief: that we live in this city, where we are both sufficiently well known. But they will not succeed in making me depart from my custom, and, even more may their eyes burst with pain, I will always strive to be more dutiful and kind toward my own. Whatever effort can be made by you on my behalf against such men, you will undertake it all through our old benevolence. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial Q.</note> That I have received great annoyance from your letter, because your services toward all your relatives were sufficiently known to all citizens. For I was never less solicitous for your dignity than for my own. But since there is no one who does not judge excellently of you, I think you ought rather to be on guard for your dignity against those who desire to diminish your good estimation from the minds of men, rather than that you should have to doubt your own fame. If, in truth, you happen to hear anything about yourself, I would not endure it dissemblingly, and I will even make it so that those who came prepared to slander another would dare much worse things against themselves. Whatever they may plot against you, there is nothing that ought to disturb you greatly. For the opinion that good men have formed of you is stronger than to be able to be violated by such men. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial T.</note> I have cultivated friendship that is based on honor above all things, and I have never borne anything else of greater value to me
pages.100: in human affairs. Now, in truth, it would be most disgraceful to neglect this, whether by reason of virtue or custom, which I have often placed before many and great things. I will state the reason that has impelled me to this. For I have convinced myself that there is either no good in life, or that it is conjoined with friendship. If that were brought about by our own effort, I would not admire this good so much. But since I see that all men are led and driven by nature itself to live together and to cherish one another, there is no one who does not judge this thing to be divine. For not all come to friendship equally, but each one, as he excels in virtue and talent, adapts himself to them more rightly and better. For we see different desires of men, some hoping for utility in friends, others for honors, some excited by those things, so that they may have those with whom they take pleasure. The wise man, however, places all the fruit of friendship in honor. I, however, since I have established that I should not love through good men, have taken care not to follow others, which I understood to be pleasing to them for their own sake. I was afterward so attentive in that matter, that I would care for one thing: that I should not be surpassed by any of my own in duty. I will say what is true. I love men so that they may be pleased. I never love more than when things go well for my friends. And if I do not wish for them the least adverse things, still that seems to me the highest point of friendship, either when friends expect my effort most, or when they are able to love from the heart those who, when any grief of friends exists, which can be cured by work, make me furthermore more dutiful in friendship, because I promised myself that I could not fail to be loved by them, whom I loved so much, which reason has not once deceived me, though I shall never be fatigued in the love of my own. For I hope that by these reasons I can reconcile the minds of many men to myself. For you yourself have often exhorted me to this matter. You have valued your opinion so much, that I value no one else's more. You will see, therefore, according to your wisdom,
pages.101:
If anyone says something else about me: that you should trust an old friend more than other men. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial N.</note> I have never thought there was any danger or labor that I should avoid for the convenience of friends. Nor do I judge any other thing so great (virtue excepted) as that which should be preferred to friendship. I think you also know this. For you know from the conjecture of my own fate that we had the same teacher, who, after we departed from school, our friendship grew with the years. For I have been in the republic, or in private affairs, whether we were in the city or in the country, always, as if a king of all, we have held a great society of counsels toward us. There has, however, been no time yet in which I have been lacking in the mutual conversation in which you would miss my duty. I wish that your fortune may remain and that you may not suffer any unworthy insult. But where anything should happen to your affairs, you would understand what kind of mind I have toward you. One thing I ask of you in greater measure, not only to you but also I implore, that since I cherish you most, do not allow the envy of men to tear our friendship asunder. And may the memory of our friendship, which began from childhood, have more weight with you than the words of those who at this time strive most to destroy our friendship as much as they can. For I approve that we not only remain in friendship, but also that we be judged as those who are overcome by no other love and benevolence. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial Q.</note> That you admonish me of our friendship, I take great pleasure. For it is helpful to know the history of our friendship and of all the studies which we later celebrated in adult age with great effort. But I dare to hear this badly from you, because I do not know what you seem to suspect about our friendship, and to doubt that it might be shaken by envious men. What others may judge about this matter, I do not know well enough. I, however, think that that friendship which is formed from honorable services has deeper roots
pages.102:
to have, and firmer foundations. <note>A red paragraph mark.</note> I do not say it ought. What that thing certainly is, is that it cannot be thwarted by envy or by the distraction of some men. Therefore, if you have admitted any suspicion into your mind about me, I beg that you lay it aside. For since in other matters once undertaken by me I always wish to seem constant, I have thought that to be held most of all in friendship. What is judged about me, you will perceive according to your prudence and humanity. As far as it pertains to me, I will say. I have certainly cherished you more from the heart than today or yesterday. With these suspicions of this kind dismissed, let us make an end, and what you write to me, let us strive vehemently to overcome all men with benevolence and love. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial V.</note> There are those whom I think should be pursued by me with great zeal. <note>A red paragraph mark.</note> For I give effort to no thing more than that all those who love me may clearly understand that they are no less loved and esteemed. What may happen to you in practice, I do not know, but I conceive well of you. But see that you do not deceive my opinion. It would be most disgraceful not to love your own, by whom you are most cherished. What this may be like, you will shortly know in the case of Pomponius, who is your relative and a true friend. If you desert him, there is no one among your own who will not be alienated from you. But I, especially, who began to love him openly for you, think you will not allow us to change our opinion, nor to think of you other than we once did. For you will make in one time the loss of almost all your friends, such as you have not yet experienced. That this may not happen by your own fault, I ask you again and again. Farewell.

<note>A red paragraph mark.</note> The case of Pomponius can be defended by law, and there is nothing at all that he would do in his own affair. Nothing will be inequitable, nor will his relationship, nor his familiarity (which is true for me with him), have more power with me than equity and justice. But since, as you know, the loss of almost all friends is to be made by
pages.103:
me if I do not comply with his conveniences. I do not think I have reached such a state of indignation that I should omit what I have acquired through virtue and honorable services, and omit doing what is right. I never think (if the sentence of your mind should be judged by me) that you will be likely to carry this matter. It is for you to judge. For as far as it pertains to me, I judge well of you. Nor do I think that you ask anything for Pomponius, except what is good and equitable. That thing, as I am affected toward everyone in heart, I would have performed for him even without anyone's request. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial O.</note> After I took up the toga from my father, I thought there was no matter to be guarded with greater zeal than that I might seem to be such against those who have bestowed very many and great benefits upon me. Do not, therefore, trust those who (so that they may remove your mind from me) try to persuade you that I will never have gratitude for your benefits. For I have instituted my life so that I could never be justly accused by those to whom I owe something. But since they strive most before you so that you may have faith in them, they strive most to want that I should dispute about this matter before you. Unless I refute them so that they repent of their deed, there is nothing that I would want faith to be had in me in other matters. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial N.</note> That you have been attentive in reporting what you have heard, you do both what is worthy of your ancestors and worthy of yourself. Nor is there anyone who has yet reported anything to me about you. I do not know if you might have understood something badly from another, or what I am ignorant of, you perhaps know better than I. If, however, you make a conjecture from some sign that I am now doubting your gratitude, I would rather hear it from you here in your presence than by letters. If you do this, I will not allow you to be in this error for any longer. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial E.</note> That I believe my mind toward your relatives is sufficiently evident to you, I cannot, however, fail to write to you about the duty
pages.104:
I owe you. For I rejoice to do all things that have been done by me with pleasure. B. Appuleius, a man familiar to you, when he was brought into our port by the force of a storm, and was ignorant of the laws and customs of our country, removed goods from the ship in the custom of our people, which, when they had been intercepted by the publicans, the matter itself tended clearly toward confiscation. Nor was there any doubt but that they were being subverted by him. But when I happened to be present there, I began to be concerned. After I understood that he was one of your relatives, I immediately approached the praetor and alleged the ignorance of the foreign man. On that day I obtained that the confiscation should be suspended. On the following day, however, I approached the judges with my friends, to whom the investigation of such a cause had been delegated by the praetor. I taught that it could not be convicted by our laws that it was contracted through ignorance, and thus done by deceit. I had many helpers in the cause of your friend. We therefore dismissed that man, with his goods safe, from whom you will better understand how much zeal I have used in his danger. I write this to you willingly so that you may know that all who are friends to you are also cherished by me. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial R.</note> That B. Appuleius exposed to me diligently, when your letters were given to me, that you were in every duty and benevolence toward me, and that you did not speak to me before you saw him restored to his integrity. I, however, even if I have received the greatest pleasure from what he reported about me, still a great pile of love has been added to my former benevolence, when I understood that the same was signified to me later by your letters. For I love B. Appuleius dearly, for I use his familiarity most. And he is of such virtue and modesty that there is no one to whom he ought not to be most dear by his own merit. Think, therefore, how much I do, since no duty was missed by you for his defense. I desire that something might happen that I would not want to come about in any way with your inconvenience, in which matter
pages.105:
to be able to return gratitude to you. I hope you will understand that there is nothing that has been undertaken by me at any time with greater zeal than to prove the gratitude I have for you, which is immortal, by the thing itself. If you should recognize anything in which my work can be of use to yours, allow that to be asked of you most of all, so that as you used my duty in the case of Appuleius, so you may wish to use me for all your affairs as by your own right. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial N.</note> It would not have been possible to think that the effort and care I undertook for your safety could be increased more in you. It is incredible how much every single day adds to my love for you. For after I began to love you, there was no time in which I did not think of you at length, and have conversation about you often. If I meet any of your acquaintances, with whom I wish to mention what prudence and humanity you have, my love for you is doubled, and my benevolence toward you is increased much more than can be believed. For as often as I consider my benefits to you, which are daily greater, that thing brings so much to my former love that I now cherish you more than my own eyes. I therefore make no end of loving you, nor is there anything I think of more than that I may seem sufficiently grateful to you and to men. But so great are your merits in me, and so great a pile has been added to your benefits, that I do not say for returning gratitude, but not even for speaking about it (in my judgment) can I be your equal. That, however, you will consider more for your nature than for my merit, with what affection and benevolence, not by what faculties, I am prepared with a great mind and zeal to return the gratitude owed to you. Farewell.

<note>A red decorative initial N.</note> You are too dutiful toward me, with too grateful a mind, when you attribute more to my benefits toward you than I recognize should be attributed by reality. For there is no time in which you have not brought more gratitude than you previously received from me.

N.text: in human affairs. Now, in truth, it would be most disgraceful to neglect this, whether by reason of virtue or custom, which I have often placed before many and great things. I will state the reason that has impelled me to this. For I have convinced myself that there is either no good in life, or that it is conjoined with friendship. If that were brought about by our own effort, I would not admire this good so much. But since I see that all men are led and driven by nature itself to live together and to cherish one another, there is no one who does not judge this thing to be divine. For not all come to friendship equally, but each one, as he excels in virtue and talent, adapts himself to them more rightly and better. For we see different desires of men, some hoping for utility in friends, others for honors, some excited by those things, so that they may have those with whom they take pleasure. The wise man, however, places all the fruit of friendship in honor. I, however, since I have established that I should not love through good men, have taken care not to follow others, which I understood to be pleasing to them for their own sake. I was afterward so attentive in that matter, that I would care for one thing: that I should not be surpassed by any of my own in duty. I will say what is true. I love men so that they may be pleased. I never love more than when things go well for my friends.
